subject: NF-300 throughput drops during threat feed update
description: Evergreen Clinic Network NOC reported a recurring throughput drop on an NF-300 running 5.1.5. They said Internet traffic falls from normal levels to well under 1 Gbps for about a minute after a threat database update finishes, then recovers without a reboot. Existing sessions stay up, but new connections are slow to establish and the event lines up with the signature activation phase. TAC reviewed the current status and confirmed the issue is isolated to the update window rather than a general dataplane fault.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-3105 and applied the documented workaround. We set the threat update window to 02:00-02:15 UTC so the signature activation occurs during low traffic, and advised the customer to keep the feed set small enough to stay below the 128 MB bundle threshold. We also advised them not to make SSL inspection policy changes while an update is activating.

subject: 802.1X clients stuck authenticating after RADIUS challenge on OW-20 4.9
description: Partner escalation on behalf of Lakeside Hospitality: wireless users on Orion OW-20 controllers running 4.9 are intermittently failing 802.1X at the second RADIUS step. The customer reported that the username prompt appears, then the client sits in authenticating for roughly 15-20 seconds before timing out and retrying. TAC reviewed the controller logs and found repeated '%RADIUS-4-ATTR_DROP' entries during Access-Challenge processing, which lined up with the failures. The issue was reproducible only against one external policy server, and only when the challenge packet carried a long attribute set.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-4107. We applied the workaround by reordering the RADIUS response so the Vendor-Specific attribute was sent first, which prevented it from being dropped during repacking. After the change, 802.1X completed normally on the OW-20 4.9 cluster.

subject: HX-5000 100g uplink drops briefly after optics alarm clears
description: Sunset Power Authority phoned TAC about an HX-5000 core switch running 7.5. They reported a 100G uplink on a QSFP28 module that drops for a few seconds and then comes back without any configuration change. Their team first suspected a bad optic or fiber plant issue because the remote end logs a clean link loss and recovery. TAC reviewed the interface history and confirmed the module readings return to normal immediately before the brief withdrawal.
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as KB-6102 and applied the documented workaround on the affected interface to disable aggressive DOM alarm action. After that change, the port stayed in service while the module readings remained within the normal operating range. The customer was advised to monitor the optics and schedule an upgrade when practical.

subject: Threat update causes slow traffic on NF-300, request for workaround
description: Northstar Bank submitted a portal case for an NF-300 running 5.1.5 because traffic slows every time the threat database finishes updating. Their note said the firewall is not rebooting or dropping VPN tunnels, but user traffic pauses long enough to trigger complaints from traders and back-office staff. TAC checked the pattern against the device behavior and found that existing sessions remain stable while new sessions increase normally during the event. The customer included the firewall log message '%TP-4-SIGNATURE_STALL' and asked for a fix that does not require an immediate upgrade.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-3105 and applied the documented workaround. We configured a threat update window so activations run during a low-traffic period and advised the customer to keep the threat feed set small enough to stay below the 128 MB bundle size. We also advised them to avoid SSL inspection policy changes while the update is still activating.

subject: Tune BFD timers to reduce false failures
description: CivicWorks Public Agency asked how to tune BFD timers on Aurora AR-900 9.1.4 to reduce false failures on long-lived peers. They reported intermittent session drops after extended uptime and wanted a temporary timer profile for noncritical peers while they plan a maintenance window. They also asked what state checks TAC recommends after changing the timers.
resolution: TAC pointed them to GUIDE-AR and recommended using the 200 ms transmit interval, 200 ms receive interval, and multiplier 5 on noncritical peers where transient loss is acceptable. The guide also recommends verifying the session state after the change with show bfd neighbors detail. On 9.1.4, if BFD stops transmitting after long uptime, treat it as a process recovery issue rather than a link-layer fault and plan a controlled restart or reload during a maintenance window before platform uptime reaches 49 days.

subject: Routing process at 95% after BGP refresh on 9.2.1
description: Sunset Power Authority opened this case through the customer portal after seeing the AR-900’s routing process spike and the router become slow to respond during BGP maintenance. The device is running 9.2.1 and is used as an edge router with a large IPv4 unicast table. Their notes said the issue happened after several soft clears in a row while the network was still learning routes from peers. TAC confirmed the pattern in `show process cpu` and found the routing thread holding most of the CPU time. The system log also showed "ERR-CPU-7781" during the event, which aligned with the repeated refresh behavior.
resolution: TAC tied the behavior to KB-2110 and recommended upgrading the Aurora AR-900 from 9.2.1 to 9.2.3, where BGP refresh no longer rebuilds the full outbound queue on each soft clear. The customer completed the upgrade and verified that repeated soft clears no longer drove the routing process above normal levels. Post-upgrade monitoring showed stable convergence and no further CPU spikes.

subject: Reporting jobs on Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 taking 20+ minutes
description: BlueRiver Credit Union emailed that overnight reports on their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator had started running far longer than before, and the web dashboard was lagging while the job was active. They also noted no tunnel outages and no obvious alarm on the edges. TAC confirmed the orchestrator was on 3.3 and observed sustained high CPU in the reporting service during the scheduled run. The job behavior matched a reporting scalability issue rather than a general platform failure. The orchestrator log showed '%ERR-ORCH-5178' during the report window.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-5107 and applied the documented mitigation. We set `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed the change to reduce the amount of data each report must process, which restored acceptable report times.

subject: dual-sim lte site drops oversize traffic after 3.1 upgrade
description: IronGate Freight opened via partner escalation after a branch edge upgraded to Atlas SD-WAN 3.1 started failing only on LTE backup links. The edge, running 3.1 at 198.51.100.91, still reports the overlay tunnel as up, but shipping label uploads and other larger flows stall or retransmit heavily. The customer initially thought this was an ISP issue because small pings still worked, but packet captures showed fragmentation behavior changing immediately after the upgrade. The problem was limited to the interface with a pre-upgrade explicit LTE tunnel MTU below 1500.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-5104 and instructed the customer to reapply the pre-upgrade LTE tunnel MTU on the affected interface. After `interface lte0 tunnel-mtu 1400` and `commit`, the edge returned to stable forwarding and the site was cleared back into production.

subject: OW-20 APs stop joining after a few retries on 4.7
description: MetroLink Telecom opened this by phone for an Orion OW-20 running 4.7. They reported that a small set of APs would come online, fail to join, and then sit offline for several minutes before recovering on their own. TAC checked `show ap detail <name>` on the affected APs and confirmed that `last-seen` only moved again after the next discovery cycle. The pattern matched an AP join retry problem rather than a pure RF or power issue.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-4102 workaround by changing the join retry interval from 5 seconds to 2 seconds with `ap join retry-interval 2`. After the change, the APs continued through capability revalidation without being dropped from the retransmit queue. We also advised the customer to keep one-way latency under 80 ms and packet loss below 1% for remote sites.

subject: 5.1.5 upgrade on NF-300 lost rules and NAT objects
description: Evergreen Clinic Network emailed TAC about an NF-300 running 5.0.9 that was upgraded to 5.1.5 and appeared healthy, but a large set of security policy and NAT objects vanished after login. The customer suspected disk corruption because the appliance had rebooted cleanly and no hardware alarms were present. During triage, I confirmed the device was otherwise stable, with the issue limited to configuration state; `show running-config` showed default placeholders in several sections that previously held custom objects. The system log contained "%UPGRADE-4-REPLAY_CURSOR", which is consistent with a checkpoint replay failure during upgrade.
resolution: TAC advised the clinic to apply the KB-3111 workaround: export the policy objects, break the configuration into smaller chunks, and re-import the affected content after the first boot. We also had them save a pre-upgrade backup copy for validation and compare the running configuration after each import batch. The configuration was recovered without changing the release, and the customer confirmed the objects remained present after reboot.

subject: Intermittent reachability loss after gateway failover on HX-5000
description: An on-site field engineer for IronGate Freight reported brief loss of reachability between leaf-spine sites after moving an anycast gateway on an HX-5000 running 7.6. The engineer suspected duplicate MAC learning, but TAC review showed the local switch kept the type-5 prefix installed while upstream peers retained stale next-hop information. The issue reproduced only after the gateway MAC moved between leafs and then self-cleared much later. No log excerpt was included in the field notes, but packet traces confirmed the blackhole during the stale-route window.
resolution: TAC tied the behavior to KB-6108 and recommended the operational workaround. The engineer performed a controlled EVPN route refresh after the gateway move, which caused the prefix advertisements to update immediately and restored end-to-end reachability.

subject: Urgent: orchestrator policy commit blocked on 3.0
description: HarborPoint Retail emailed TAC about an Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator 3.0 tenant where a policy update had remained in processing for more than 12 minutes and then failed. The customer described the issue as a branch outage, but TAC verified the edges were still forwarding on the previous policy and the overlay tunnels remained up. On the orchestrator, the policy worker stayed above 90 percent CPU while compiling a large route-map with 260+ entries. Because the commit could not complete, the intended routing changes never reached the branch devices.
resolution: TAC traced the failure to KB-5103 and confirmed it was the 3.0 policy compiler limitation on large route-maps. HarborPoint Retail upgraded the orchestrator to 3.1, which resolved the serialization problem. After the upgrade, policy pushes completed successfully and the tenant changes propagated to the edges.

subject: OW-20 rolls back after 5.0 upgrade from 4.6
description: Pinnacle Energy called in after an Orion OW-20 running 4.6 attempted a direct upgrade to 5.0. The controller rebooted into the new image, stayed up briefly, then rolled back about 10 minutes later and returned on the previous release. The upgrade log stopped during guest portal object processing and included the line "%ERR-UPG-2204". TAC reviewed the configuration and found a large set of legacy guest portal ACL objects created before 4.7.
resolution: Per KB-4111, TAC instructed the customer to boot the old image, remove unused legacy guest portal ACL objects, and export the configuration for review before retrying the upgrade. After pruning the stale ACL entries, the customer reran the upgrade successfully and the controller completed the migration.

subject: App-aware routing held old next-hop after BGP withdraw
description: Prairie State College called TAC because VoIP and web traffic kept taking the old WAN next-hop after a BGP change on an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.1. The caller said the circuit had been shut down, but application traffic continued to prefer it for roughly two to three minutes before failing over on its own. TAC validated on the edge that the withdrawn path was still present in the application-routing view and that `show app-route sla-class` did not drop the candidate immediately after the route disappeared. The log bundle included "%SDWAN-4-ROUTE-CACHE", which matched the stale cache condition.
resolution: TAC confirmed this was the known 3.1 routing defect documented in KB-5109. To mitigate the issue, TAC set the route-cache aging timer to 60 seconds using `app-route cache age-time 60` and committed the change, which shortens the window in which the withdrawn route can remain selected. The customer was told to trigger a route-refresh before planned underlay withdrawals and to verify the backup path before returning services to production.

subject: intermittent unreachable bgp prefixes on ar-900 9.1.4
description: CivicWorks Public Agency called TAC after a scheduled circuit switchover caused several internal subnets to disappear from an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4. The phone log indicated the BGP peer stayed up, but traffic to some branch routes blackholed until the router was manually refreshed. TAC verified the control plane was healthy and saw the routes still present in BGP, while the corresponding entries were missing from `show ip route bgp`. The router syslog included "%BGP-4-NH-RESOLVE" at the time the underlay route changed state.
resolution: TAC recognized the defect as KB-2101 and instructed the customer to clear the BGP IPv4 unicast process for the affected ASN. After `clear bgp ipv4 unicast 65001`, the router recalculated next-hop resolution and repopulated the missing routes. We documented the workaround and advised the agency to apply it any time the underlay is withdrawn and relearned within the same hold interval.

subject: lte tunnel up but large packets fail after orchestrator upgrade
description: Partner escalation for Summit Logistics reported that a warehouse edge began dropping ERP traffic after being upgraded from 3.0 to 3.1. The device is an Atlas SD-WAN edge on 192.0.2.77, and the orchestrator still shows the LTE overlay tunnel as healthy. Their first note blamed application-aware routing, but TAC reviewed the edge and found the issue reproduces with plain ICMP when the payload is above the low 1400-byte range. The edge log contains "%UPG-5-MTU-MIGRATE", which aligns with an upgrade migration problem on dual-SIM LTE interfaces.
resolution: TAC identified KB-5104 and applied the documented workaround by restoring the LTE tunnel MTU on the affected interface with `interface lte0 tunnel-mtu 1400` and `commit`. After the change, the tunnel stopped advertising an oversized encapsulation size and large packets passed normally.

subject: HX-5000 master role oscillation during normal load
description: Phone call logged by the TAC agent: CivicWorks reported that a Helix HX-5000 core switch stack running 7.3 has been changing masters several times per hour. The customer initially suspected a bad stack cable, but the hardware LEDs and interface counters do not show any physical disconnects. Triage confirmed brief split election domains in `show stack`, and the system log contained repeated "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN" events while the links stayed operational. The pattern increases when background management tasks and other control-plane work run at the same time.
resolution: TAC mapped the issue to KB-6103 and advised the customer to upgrade the stack to 7.4. After the upgrade was completed, master election no longer oscillated and the stack remained in a single election domain during verification.

subject: ar-900 9.1.6 bgp routes missing after underlay failover
description: Summit Logistics emailed TAC that an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.6 lost reachability to a set of customer prefixes after a transport failover on the WAN edge. The message noted the BGP neighbor remained established and there was no obvious session reset, but the affected routes were not being used for forwarding. TAC confirmed the pattern on the device: `show bgp summary` showed the session as Established, while `show ip route bgp` did not list the impacted prefixes until the unit was reloaded. The log buffer contained "%BGP-4-NH-RESOLVE" immediately after the underlay route change.
resolution: TAC identified the problem as KB-2101 and advised upgrading the router to 9.2.0, where the next-hop recursion cache is invalidated correctly when the resolving route changes state. After the upgrade, the customer repeated the failover test and the BGP routes remained installed through the underlay transition. No additional workaround was required after the software change.

subject: Periodic latency on firewall under heavy session churn
description: Redwood University emailed the TAC mailbox about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.0 that was introducing brief delays during registration and video traffic. They reported that the firewall was otherwise healthy and that the problem only showed up when many new flows were created at once. TAC compared the session-table counters and found a repeatable skew pattern with one shard significantly hotter than the rest, which is consistent with the issue described in KB-3110. The customer had not yet changed any session-handling settings, and the imbalance was consistent with the 5.2.0 hashing defect.
resolution: TAC recommended an upgrade to 5.2.2 in accordance with KB-3110. The customer completed the upgrade, and post-change checks showed balanced shard occupancy with no further latency complaints during test traffic.

subject: After moving to 5.1.3, some firewall objects reverted to default
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets emailed TAC stating that their NF-300, previously on 5.0.8, came back from a planned upgrade to 5.1.3 with a number of rules and address objects missing. They initially described it as a 'partial save' and noted that internet access was still working for most users, which made the issue look like a selective policy problem. I reviewed the startup behavior and confirmed the appliance completed boot normally, but the running configuration no longer contained approximately 150 custom entries. This is consistent with a replay/import defect during checkpoint migration on heavily populated systems.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-3111 workaround by exporting the existing policy objects, splitting the configuration into smaller chunks, and re-importing them after the first boot. The customer was also instructed to keep each checkpoint file under 4,000 entries and verify the running configuration immediately after reboot. The missing objects were restored without requiring a version change.

subject: Certificate renewal broke check-in for field edge
description: CivicWorks Public Agency escalated that a remote edge lost orchestrator contact after a planned certificate rotation. The device is CW-EDGE-07 running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and the disconnect occurred within roughly 3 minutes of the renewal completing on the edge. The edge log shows the renewal itself succeeded locally, but the next registration attempt was denied. The log includes "%PKI-3-CHAIN-UNTRUSTED", which matches the orchestrator-side validation failure we saw in the certificate status view.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-5102. We imported the updated trust bundle containing the active intermediate CA on the orchestrator and committed the change before retrying registration. After the bundle refresh, the edge checked in normally and configuration pushes resumed.

subject: HA pair keeps swapping active/standby after switch maintenance
description: Crescent Health Group opened this after a maintenance window on a Nimbus NF-300 pair running 5.2.2. The on-site engineer reported that the firewall roles were flipping every few minutes, which briefly interrupted VPN and several internal applications. TAC reviewed the event timeline and saw that the heartbeat links and the monitored uplink were both connected through the same upstream access switch. That topology can make the pair react to the same Layer 2 disturbance on both signals, so the failover pattern matched the symptom.
resolution: TAC identified this as the known topology issue described in KB-3107. We had the customer move the heartbeat links to a dedicated Layer 2 segment independent of the monitored interfaces, and where cabling had to remain in place, we set the monitor interval to 10 seconds with `ha monitor-interval 10` followed by `commit`. After the change, the active node remained stable and no further oscillation was observed.

subject: Repeated topology change events on access switch ports after host reboot
description: Redwood University opened this by email after a reboot of a downstream virtualization host attached to a Helix HX-5000 running 7.4. The campus network team reports that several access switches started relearning MAC addresses and the MAC table aged out much faster than the configured 300-second timer. TAC checked `show spanning-tree detail` and confirmed the same access port was reentering forwarding every 2 to 4 seconds even though the physical link stayed up and the host cabling did not change. No hardware fault indicators or interface errors were present.
resolution: TAC identified this as the known rapid-pvst design limitation described in KB-6105. We advised the customer not to use rapid-pvst on ports facing multi-MAC downstream virtualization hosts and to place the server on a dedicated edge VLAN design or restrict the port to a single access device. The customer applied the workaround and the topology-change events stopped.

subject: Orion OW-20 5.0 voice clients pausing on roams
description: Prairie State College called TAC to report that handheld voice phones were dropping audio for a fraction of a second every few AP moves. The site runs an Orion OW-20 wireless LAN controller on 5.0, and the issue is most noticeable when classes change and many clients roam at once. TAC reviewed client state and saw reassociation succeed, but `show client detail <mac>` showed `ft fallback: yes` on devices expected to stay on 802.11r fast transition. The pattern matched a roaming-path delay rather than an AP or RADIUS failure.
resolution: TAC identified the symptom as KB-4106. Because the controller was on 5.0 and the site needed a permanent fix, Prairie State College upgraded the Orion OW-20 to 5.1, where FT key pushes are sent immediately on reassociation.

subject: IPv6 neighbor churn on AR-900 after traffic burst
description: MetroLink Telecom opened a web form case for an Aurora AR-900 on 9.2.3 because several customer edge hosts lost IPv6 reachability for short periods. Their initial note blamed an upstream ISP flap, but packet captures from the router showed repeated NS/NA bursts from one VLAN without any matching routing instability. TAC reviewed `show control-plane protection statistics` and observed the control-plane CPU rising from about 15% to above 80% while the IPv6 ND drop counter remained at zero during the burst window. The issue was reproducible only when the access VLAN generated a short spike of neighbor discovery traffic.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-2106 for the 9.2.3 control-plane protection defect. Because the customer requested immediate mitigation, we had them apply the documented workaround to reduce the IPv6 ND policer to 2000 pps and limit burst traffic at the edge with access-layer storm control. The router recovered without further stale neighbor events after the change.

subject: NF-300 failover loop on 5.2.0 after port flap
description: IronGate Freight emailed TAC about a Nimbus NF-300 pair running 5.2.0 that was “bouncing between firewalls” roughly every 20 seconds. Their notes said the units were healthy individually, but the production circuit kept dropping when both appliances were connected to the same access switch. During triage, TAC asked for the HA status output and the customer also captured the log line '%HA-3-LINK_MONITOR_FLAP' repeatedly during the event. The pattern suggested the heartbeat path and the monitored interface were being affected by the same L2 forwarding change.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3107 and confirmed there was no software defect to fix in 5.2.0. We instructed the customer to separate the heartbeat links from the monitored interfaces onto an independent Layer 2 segment, and we temporarily increased the monitor interval to 10 seconds using `ha monitor-interval 10` and `commit`. The failover oscillation stopped after the cabling change and timer adjustment.

subject: intermittent vpn outage on nf-300 after pfs change
description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened the case from an on-site field engineer working on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8. The report was that a healthcare site VPN stayed up most of the day, then briefly stopped passing traffic even though the dashboard still showed the tunnel as connected. Initial review showed the IKE SA remained up while the child SA renegotiated, and the device log contained `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. The timing lined up with rekey activity, so TAC suspected a stale proposal set being reused after a recent PFS change on the peer.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-3101 and implemented the workaround rather than changing the platform release. The customer was instructed to keep the same PFS group on both peers and disable child SA rekey on the Nimbus NF-300 with `crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable` under `config`, followed by `commit`. After a coordinated tunnel restart, the VPN remained stable and traffic resumed normally.

subject: BFD neighbors freezing on AR-900 9.1.4
description: Customer portal web form: Prairie State College submitted that an Aurora AR-900 on 9.1.4 was showing one-sided BFD failures after weeks of uptime, with upstream routing becoming unstable during the event. They noted that interface counters were clean and that the problem seemed to move between peers over time. TAC reviewed the attached operational output and saw `show bfd neighbors detail` with a stuck transmit counter on the affected session, while the receive path still looked healthy. The device log included `%BFD-3-ERR-BFD-2201: transmit scheduling stalled for session 198.51.100.77/198.51.100.78`, which matches the reported behavior.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-2102 and recommended the documented workaround on the AR-900. The customer applied `configure`, `router bfd`, `timers 200 200 5` to the affected noncritical peers and was instructed to plan a controlled restart before the uptime threshold is reached again. This kept the sessions stable pending a later maintenance window.

subject: Repeated EVPN refreshes causing routing memory exhaustion on HX-5000
description: Crescent Health Group escalated this from the NOC for a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6. They saw increasing control-plane latency overnight and said the routing process was consuming more memory each hour, even though no major configuration changes had been made. TAC checked the device and found the routing daemon RSS had increased from about 900 MB to just over 1.8 GB after repeated EVPN route-refresh activity, with free memory at 11 percent. The switch log included "%MEM-4-LEAK", matching the pattern seen in the field. Initial suspicion was a transient burst from a peer reset, but the growth was cumulative across multiple refresh cycles.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to the 7.6 memory leak documented in KB-6112. The customer upgraded the HX-5000 to 8.0, which fixes the refresh handler to reuse attribute cache objects and release stale generations immediately. After the upgrade, the routing process stopped growing and control-plane latency returned to normal.

subject: 802.11r roam pauses on OW-20 4.9 during peak hours
description: Evergreen Clinic Network NOC reported brief voice drops when staff roam between APs on Orion OW-20 running 4.9. The issue is intermittent but becomes easier to reproduce during daytime peak load, and `show client detail <mac>` shows the reassociation completing before traffic resumes. The controller CPU was observed above 70% during the affected period. The event log also showed "%ROAM-5-FT_KEYTIMEOUT" on failed fast-transition attempts.
resolution: TAC confirmed this matches KB-4105 for Orion OW-20 4.9. We applied the workaround from the article by setting `wlan corp accounting interval 60` and advised the customer to keep controller CPU below 70% during roaming validation. For the affected voice SSID, we also recommended temporarily disabling 802.11r until the next maintenance window if the call path remains sensitive.

subject: BGP routes dropping after backup static route change
description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened an escalation for an Aurora AR-900 on 9.2.3 because a set of partner routes disappeared from the routing table during a failover test. The BGP peer never dropped, and the router continued to receive prefixes, but the installed routes stopped forwarding traffic until a manual reset was performed. The customer’s first assumption was a redistribution issue, but the failures were limited to prefixes that depended on a recursive static path. TAC reproduced the behavior by replacing a static route to the same prefix and verified the defect was isolated to the 9.2.3 release.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-2107 and advised upgrading the device to 9.3.0. In 9.3.0, the recursion engine is updated so BGP is notified when a static route changes attributes without changing the destination prefix. After the upgrade, the clinic repeated the failover test and the BGP routes remained installed throughout the transition.

subject: SD-WAN change window blocked by certificate validation
description: HarborPoint Retail escalated through a partner, reporting that routine SD-WAN policy updates were failing during a change window on an Atlas SD-WAN 2.9 orchestrator. The customer believed the issue was related to tunnel stability because the update would not proceed, but `show sdwan tunnels` on the edges still showed established sessions. TAC review showed the failure happened on the orchestrator before policy distribution began, and the log captured "%PKI-4-CRL-EXPIRED" during preflight checks. The symptoms were consistent with a CRL age check rather than an edge or routing defect.
resolution: TAC identified KB-5111 as the root cause and applied the workaround from the article. The revocation list was refreshed on the orchestrator using `certificate import crl revocation-list.pem`, then `commit` was issued to update the timestamp before retrying the push. The customer was advised to repeat this refresh before the 24-hour threshold on future change windows.

subject: nf-300 ipsec tunnel blackholing during rekey on p2 site link
description: CivicWorks Public Agency called TAC after a site-to-site VPN on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 started dropping traffic for short intervals while the tunnel still appeared established. The caller said the outage usually lasts 10 to 20 seconds and happens after the tunnel has been up for several hours, which initially looked like a peer stability issue. During triage, `show crypto ikev2 sa` showed the IKE SA in ESTABLISHED while the child SA counter reset during rekey, and the device log included `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. The peer-side team reported repeated ESP rekey failures, and the symptom pattern matched a child-SA renegotiation problem rather than a full IKE teardown.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3101 and applied the documented workaround on both peers: keep the PFS group unchanged, disable child SA rekey, and schedule a controlled tunnel restart after the change. On the Nimbus NF-300, TAC entered `config`, set `crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable`, and committed the change. The tunnel stabilized after the manual restart and no further traffic blackholes were observed.

subject: After upgrade to 3.2, LTE WAN path breaks on larger frames
description: Crescent Health Group emailed TAC after noticing intermittent application drops on one 3.2 branch edge following a planned upgrade. The device is an Atlas SD-WAN branch running 3.2 with LTE on a nondefault APN; smaller traffic passes, but larger packets are fragmented and some sessions reset. TAC reproduced the issue in the running config review and saw that the preupgrade tunnel MTU setting was absent from the LTE interface after migration. The upgrade output also contained "%UPG-5-MTU-MIGRATE".
resolution: TAC referenced KB-5110 and recommended upgrading the edge to 3.3. Once the customer completed the upgrade, the LTE tunnel MTU migrated correctly and the branch no longer exhibited fragmentation on larger packets.

subject: IPv6 clients dropping off after RA suppression on AR-900
description: HarborPoint Retail escalated on behalf of the customer after point-of-sale terminals on an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.0 began failing new TCP sessions over IPv6. The loss starts about 180 seconds after the last valid router advertisement is blocked, even though the VLAN is configured with a 7200-second valid lifetime and the prefix remains present on the router. TAC saw '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' in the system log during the outage window, which aligned with the time clients lost their global address and Neighbor Discovery started failing. This points away from a pure host issue and toward router-side prefix aging behavior.
resolution: TAC tied the symptoms to KB-2104 and confirmed the router was removing SLAAC prefix state too early when RA suppression was active. We implemented the workaround by avoiding RA suppression on the active user VLAN and, where suppression is required, using DHCPv6 stateful addressing for the segment. After the change, the customer verified IPv6 addresses stayed valid past the preferred-lifetime transition and sessions no longer dropped.

subject: Repeated CAPWAP join rejects on 4.6 controller
description: Northstar Bank submitted this through the customer portal for an Orion OW-20 running 4.6. Their APs at one branch keep bouncing between discovery and join, and the branch engineers thought it was a firewall issue because the APs can ping the controller and the CAPWAP ports are open. TAC checked `show ap summary` and saw the affected units in down/joining state with no radios enabled. The controller log shows `%CAPWAP-3-JOIN_REJECT` each time the APs try to associate, with no subsequent configuration download.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-4101 and confirmed the controller was sending an empty RF profile TLV from the AP group configuration. We applied the documented workaround by removing the RF profile override from the AP group, which stopped the controller from emitting the zero-length TLV. After that change, the APs joined normally and remained stable.

subject: Scheduled reports slowing down the orchestrator after a week of flow history
description: Redwood University reported that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator started taking much longer to generate scheduled usage reports after the flow history aged past about a week. They said the dashboard felt sluggish during the same window, but edge tunnels and policy forwarding were still up. TAC reviewed the orchestrator and confirmed the reporting job window now overlaps with peak change activity. The issue is isolated to the reporting service on the 3.3 orchestrator.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-5107 and applied the documented workaround. We reduced flow-history retention to 5 days with `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed the change, which brought report runtime back to normal and reduced CPU contention during the job window.

subject: Encrypted tunnel drops during bring-up to managed peer
description: MetroLink Telecom NOC reported that a regional edge on Atlas SD-WAN 3.2 could not complete IPSec bring-up to a managed remote peer. The edge kept retrying negotiation on a 10-second cycle, and `show sdwan tunnels` showed the peer entry stuck in negotiating. TAC pulled the edge event log and saw repeated "%IKE-3-PROPOSAL-MISMATCH" messages during proposal exchange. MetroLink initially believed the issue was related to NAT traversal, but the same path worked for other tunnels on the box.
resolution: TAC traced the failure to the interoperability problem documented in KB-5106. We applied the workaround from the article by adjusting the remote peer to accept `tunnel ipsec proposal set aes-gcm-256 sha384` and committed the change. After the peer accepted the updated proposal form, the tunnel reached established and traffic resumed.

subject: AR-900 losing BGP routes after static path change
description: Northstar Bank reported that several Internet routes vanished from the forwarding table on an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 after a change to a backup static route. BGP remained Established, but `show ip route bgp` showed about 40 prefixes as inactive until the routing process was reset. The device was still receiving updates, so the customer initially suspected a peer problem or a FIB programming issue. During triage we confirmed the affected prefixes all used a recursive next hop through the static prefix that had just been replaced, and the event log contained `%BGP-4-NH-RESOLVE` when the routes dropped.
resolution: TAC identified this as the 9.2.3 recursive static route recursion defect described in KB-2107. We advised the customer to issue a soft clear of the affected BGP IPv4 unicast process after changing the static route, which rebuilt the recursion state and restored the inactive prefixes without a full session reset. The customer confirmed the routes returned to the forwarding table after `clear bgp ipv4 unicast 65001 soft`.

subject: Intermittent 25g link flap on hx-5000
description: MetroLink Telecom reported that an HX-5000 core switch on 7.2 was losing a 25g uplink every several minutes, usually during normal customer traffic and not only during maintenance windows. The field engineer on site had already swapped the cable and moved the optic to another port, but the behavior followed the module. I reviewed `show interfaces transceiver detail` and saw a consistent jump in transmit bias current just before each down event, while temperature and power remained within normal range. The pattern did not point to a physical seating problem or a remote device fault.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-6101 and applied the documented workaround: the transceiver monitoring interval was increased on the affected interface to reduce DOM polling activity, and the optic was kept below the observed temperature threshold where possible. After the change, the link flaps stopped during observation.

subject: core switch latency spikes on 100g port
description: Lakeside Hospitality called TAC after noticing delayed check-in and payment traffic across the main hotel network. The affected platform is a Helix HX-5000 running 7.2, and the issue was isolated to one oversubscribed 100G uplink on the core switch. TAC reviewed `show queue counters` and found that drops were increasing even though average bandwidth stayed below full line rate, which made the customer suspect a bad optic or cabling fault. No physical-layer alarms were present, and the pattern was consistent with microbursts overwhelming the egress queue on the switch.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-6109 and implemented the published workaround. Lakeside Hospitality split traffic across an additional uplink, applied upstream shaping to reduce burst depth, and reserved a dedicated queue for payment applications on the affected interface. These changes prevented the queue from staying above the 85 percent sustained utilization point and cleared the latency spikes.

subject: HX-5000 sending constant spanning-tree TCNs on one edge port
description: Crescent Health Group called TAC about a Helix HX-5000 running 7.4 that was generating frequent network instability after a nurse station appliance rebooted. Their report said the switch was “flapping,” but interface counters and the physical link were stable when TAC reviewed the case. `show spanning-tree detail` showed the affected access port repeatedly transitioning back to forwarding and the MAC table entries for the downstream appliance aging out in under a minute. The behavior was isolated to a single 10G edge port connected to a device that presents multiple MAC addresses.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-6105 and confirmed there was no software defect to correct. We instructed the customer to remove rapid-pvst from that multi-MAC edge design and to use a dedicated access VLAN or a single-device edge connection instead. After the port was treated as a restricted edge attachment, the topology-change notifications ceased.

subject: Standby missing sessions after split-brain recovery on NF-300
description: CivicWorks Public Agency called TAC after noticing that one side of their Nimbus NF-300 cluster on 5.0.9 came back from a split-brain condition with fewer sessions on standby. The caller initially suspected a session-leak condition because the standby table stayed short by about 20,000 to 30,000 entries even though `show ha status` reported the pair as synced. TAC checked the device version and confirmed both units were running Nimbus NF-300 5.0.9. The issue appeared only after the recovery event and then slowly improved, which is consistent with delayed replication catch-up rather than a permanent data loss condition.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3103 and used the recommended workaround. A full HA resync was initiated from config mode with `ha resync full`, followed by `commit`, and the customer was instructed to keep the failover links stable for at least 120 seconds after node return. After resync, the standby session table matched the active unit.

subject: APs fail to finish join on controller 4.8
description: Sunset Power Authority submitted a portal request stating that several APs were "connected but not ready" after deployment on an Orion OW-20 running 4.8. The report suggested an RF problem, but the controller logs and AP status indicated the APs were reaching the join process and then restarting the CAPWAP session before authorization. TAC confirmed `show ap summary` was showing additional join pending entries and the controller was incrementing the same join retry counter twice before stopping. The log view included "%ERR-APJ-4417", which aligned with a delayed second capability exchange on a link with moderate RTT and brief retransmit bursts.
resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-4103 and advised an upgrade from 4.8 to 4.9 on the OW-20. After the upgrade, delayed capability responses were matched to the active join session before it could age out, and the APs completed authorization normally. The customer confirmed the join pending count stopped growing after the change.

subject: BFD neighbors timing out after long uptime on AR-900
description: On-site field engineer reported that an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4 began dropping a few BFD sessions after the box had been up for about seven weeks. `show bfd neighbors detail` showed the local discriminator still Up and the receive side active, but the transmit counter stopped increasing on the affected peers. The field engineer also captured this log entry during the event: `%BFD-3-ERR-BFD-2201: transmit scheduling stalled for session 198.51.100.14/198.51.100.15`. Initial triage confirms the issue appears only on long-lived sessions and matches the pattern of peers expiring after several missed control packets.
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as KB-2102 and applied the documented workaround on the router: `configure`, `router bfd`, `timers 200 200 5` for noncritical peers. The customer was advised to plan a maintenance reload or BFD process restart before platform uptime reaches the wrap point. This stabilized the affected sessions until a software fix can be introduced in a later release.

subject: Branch policy marks SLA down after brief probe loss
description: Redwood University opened this through a partner escalation for a remote campus using atlas-edge-11 on Atlas SD-WAN 2.8. The campus saw Zoom and ERP sessions shift away from LTE after a short radio fade, but the link itself remained usable. TAC reviewed `show app-route sla-class` and found the SLA class staying down for longer than expected after only one missed probe, which did not align with the configured loss and latency thresholds. The edge logs also showed "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN" during the affected interval.
resolution: TAC traced the behavior to KB-5101 and determined the branch was running the affected 2.8 code path. Redwood University upgraded atlas-edge-11 to 2.9, then rechecked the application-aware routing state after the same probe pattern. The upgraded system kept the SLA class up as expected, and the customer closed the issue after validation.

subject: 5 GHz DFS events leave APs pinned on OW-20 5.1
description: Partner escalation on behalf of the customer reported that several outdoor APs on an Orion OW-20 running 5.1 stopped moving to new 5 GHz channels after repeated radar detections. The APs stayed reachable and `show ap summary` still listed them as up, so the customer initially suspected a backhaul problem. TAC triage found that the RF dashboard no longer showed channel-change activity even though DFS counters continued to rise. The behavior matched a controller-side RF manager stall rather than an AP join issue.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-4110 by disabling DFS on the impacted radio group and setting the 5 GHz radios to a fixed non-DFS channel plan. Once the channel set was pinned, the APs stopped accumulating DFS-triggered stalls and service stabilized.

subject: 3.3 orchestrator reports causing long delays and policy lag
description: Prairie State College called in to report that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator was spending most of the morning running scheduled reports, and administrators noticed policy edits were sometimes delayed until the reports finished. The caller initially suspected a database issue because the graphs were slow to refresh, but the orchestrator services remained otherwise healthy. TAC checked the reporting workload and saw the jobs were running against a large flow-history set. The problem is confined to the reporting process on the 3.3 orchestrator.
resolution: TAC traced the behavior to KB-5107 and implemented the workaround. We shortened flow-history retention to 5 days using `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed it, then advised the customer to keep larger reports in a smaller time window or schedule them during low-change periods.

subject: vpn pause on route-based tunnel after rekey on nf-300
description: Redwood University submitted a portal case for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 because their campus VPN would stop passing traffic for a moment, then resume on its own. They first described it as a routing issue, but the firewall health checks and peer reachability looked normal. TAC observed that `show crypto ikev2 sa` remained ESTABLISHED throughout, and the disruption lined up with DPD probe handling around the same time as child-SA rekey. The event log included `%IKEV2-4-REKEY_TIMER` when the pause occurred.
resolution: TAC closed the case against KB-3112. The workaround was to avoid identical timer values on the route-based tunnel, so we updated the DPD timer with `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committed it. That prevented the scheduler overlap and restored continuous forwarding.

subject: SNMP traps missing during interface flap storm on AR-900 9.3.0
description: Evergreen Clinic Network reported that their Aurora AR-900 edge router running 9.3.0 stopped sending some linkUp and linkDown traps during a maintenance window on the access layer. The on-site field engineer saw the NMS show gaps in port-state history even though polling continued to report the interfaces correctly. In the system log, the router emitted "ERR-SNMP-3019" while the flap rate was high. Initial triage confirmed the event loss started after a burst of interface transitions exceeded the trap queue capacity.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-2109, a fixed-depth SNMP trap queue limit on the AR-900. We applied the documented workaround by enabling link debounce on the affected access ports to reduce the event rate and advised the team to use 30-second polling for state reconciliation. The customer kept the router on 9.3.0; no software change was required.

subject: Intermittent source-port allocation errors on AR-900
description: HarborPoint Retail escalated through a partner after registers and handheld scanners behind an Aurora AR-900 running 9.3.0 started timing out in short waves. Their team reported that the problem was worst after batch uploads finished, even though NAT tables did not look full when they checked them. TAC confirmed the router was logging `ERR-NAT-4108` during the incident and that `show nat translations` showed only a limited active translation count. The symptoms were consistent with a burst-driven allocation failure rather than a sustained capacity problem.
resolution: TAC matched the issue to KB-2108 and explained that 9.3.0 can misreport NAT port exhaustion while deferred ports are still counted as in use. We implemented the workaround by enlarging the NAT pool with additional public address space and setting the NAT translation timeout to 240 seconds. With the added headroom in place, the customer stopped seeing the 2-4 minute allocation failures after traffic spikes.

subject: APs stuck joining after 4.6 upgrade
description: CivicWorks Public Agency opened this case by email after upgrading an Orion OW-20 wireless LAN controller to 4.6. Several access points now sit in discovery for about a minute, then retry join repeatedly, and users report the SSIDs never come up on those APs. On the controller, `show ap summary` shows the affected APs as down/joining with radios disabled. The last 50 log lines include `%CAPWAP-3-JOIN_REJECT` for the same AP MACs, even though the APs have valid management IP addresses and can reach UDP 5246/5247.
resolution: TAC correlated the repeated join failures to KB-4101, which matches a 4.6 defect triggered by a zero-length RF profile TLV during CAPWAP negotiation. We removed the AP group RF profile override so the controller stopped emitting the empty TLV, then verified the APs completed join and radios came up. The customer was advised to keep the workaround in place until a move to 4.7, where the parser issue is fixed.

subject: Intermittent wireless login failures on Orion OW-20 4.9
description: TAC logged a phone call from HarborPoint Retail about sporadic wireless authentication failures on an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.9. Users could connect to SSID corp, but some devices never moved past authenticating and eventually fell back to the login prompt. Initial checks showed the controller forwarding the Access-Challenge and then receiving a follow-up response that the RADIUS server rejected as incomplete. No controller alarms were present, and the failure pattern suggested an attribute handling problem in the RADIUS exchange rather than a general AAA outage.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-4107 and recommended upgrading the controller from 4.9 to 5.0. After the upgrade, the Access-Challenge repacking behavior no longer truncated the attribute list, and 802.1X authentication completed consistently.

subject: Orchestrator rejects policy jobs, edges remain up
description: Pinnacle Energy submitted a portal case stating that policy pushes from the Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator began failing overnight, but existing tunnels and application routing stayed up. The orchestrator is running version 2.9, and the customer confirmed no edge devices were rebooted and no certificates were replaced. During triage, TAC confirmed the job was stopping in preflight validation before any edge received the change. The orchestrator log included the message "%PKI-4-CRL-EXPIRED", which aligned with a certificate revocation list age check rather than a connectivity fault.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-5111 and recommended upgrading the orchestrator to 3.1. After the upgrade, the validator honored the CRL nextUpdate field instead of the fixed 24-hour timer, and policy pushes completed normally. No additional edge-side changes were required.

subject: HX-5000 port goes down briefly after optic alarm clears
description: Sunset Power Authority submitted a portal case for an HX-5000 running 7.5. Their note said the 100G uplink on a QSFP28 optic 'keeps bouncing' when the module cools back down after a warning, but the optic diagnostics otherwise look normal. TAC compared the interface timestamps and saw the port was withdrawn for about 3 to 5 seconds before recovering. The pattern was isolated to one uplink and did not affect the rest of the stack.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-6102 and applied the recommended workaround on the affected interface by disabling aggressive DOM alarm action. The interface remained up after subsequent alarm-clear events, provided the optic stayed within its normal operating range. TAC left the case open only long enough to confirm stability, then resolved it.

subject: Critical 25g uplink instability on hx-5000 core switch
description: Crescent Health Group phoned TAC about an HX-5000 running 7.2 where a critical 25g uplink was dropping often enough to affect clinical application traffic. The customer suspected a routing issue at first because the outage seemed to happen during heavier traffic periods, but the interface itself was the only component flapping. TAC checked the transceiver detail and saw the same bias current jump before each loss of signal event, with the port recovering by itself after a short interval. The optic remained seated and there was no evidence of a stack or spanning-tree event on the switch.
resolution: TAC matched the case to KB-6101 and recommended upgrading the switch from 7.2 to 7.3, which includes the corrected DOM sampling logic. The customer completed the upgrade and the uplink remained stable, with no further loss-of-signal events observed.

subject: MetroLink IPv6 access loss on access VLAN during RA suppression
description: MetroLink Telecom emailed TAC about an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 in a customer access site where IPv6 clients on VLAN 10 began failing after a change intended to reduce unsolicited advertisements from upstream. They reported that addresses disappeared from endpoints after about three minutes, even though the router still showed the delegated prefix and the configured lifetime was much longer. The log bundle included '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' messages matching the time of failure. TAC observed that the problem was limited to clients using SLAAC on the suppressed VLAN and was not reproduced on adjacent non-suppressed segments.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-2104 and confirmed the router was aging prefix state from received advertisements rather than from the locally configured timers while RA suppression was active. We instructed the customer to remove RA suppression from the production VLAN, or to migrate the affected segment to DHCPv6 stateful addressing if suppression must remain. After applying the workaround, the customer reported that IPv6 endpoints retained their addresses and new sessions completed normally.

subject: Move OW-20 controllers from 4.9 to 5.0 to stop 802.1X failures
description: On-site field engineer report for Redwood University: students were intermittently failing to join the secure wireless network on an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.9. The symptoms looked like a bad password to the help desk, but the same credentials would often succeed on the second or third attempt. TAC checked the controller state and saw clients lingering in authenticating while the RADIUS server sent a multi-attribute Access-Challenge sequence. The controller logs included '%RADIUS-4-ATTR_DROP', which pointed to an attribute handling defect rather than an endpoint or certificate problem.
resolution: TAC tied the issue to KB-4107 and advised the customer to upgrade the OW-20 controller from 4.9 to 5.0. After the upgrade, Access-Challenge repacking preserved all attributes and the intermittent 802.1X failures stopped. The customer confirmed stable logins across multiple test devices after the change.

subject: Short latency spikes on mixed traffic after voice calls start
description: TAC logged this call from Summit Logistics for an Aurora AR-900 at version 9.2.1. The site reported that once softphones started sending RTP, file transfers on the same uplink slowed dramatically for a few seconds at a time. Interface counters were clean, and the customer had already ruled out duplex and cabling issues. During verification, the router logged "%QOS-5-SCHED-DEFICIT" and `show qos interface` indicated the priority queue was emptying at line rate while the weighted classes were not being serviced normally. The customer asked whether packet loss on the WAN circuit could be causing the delay, but the symptoms were isolated to the router egress scheduler.
resolution: TAC found the issue described in KB-2105 and advised an upgrade to Aurora AR-900 9.2.3. The customer completed the upgrade and retested with the same traffic mix. After the upgrade, the scheduler preserved weighted queue service credits after each priority burst, and the latency spikes were no longer observed.

subject: Soft clear causes CPU spike on AR-900
description: Sunset Power Authority reported that their Aurora AR-900 on 9.2.1 shows a short but repeatable CPU surge after BGP refresh operations. The portal submission included the log line "ERR-CPU-7781" and described intermittent control-plane lag, but data forwarding was not impacted. TAC checked `show process cpu` and saw the routing task dominate the scheduler slice during route churn. The router carries more than 250,000 prefixes, so the symptoms align with a scaling problem in the refresh path.
resolution: TAC matched the case to KB-2110 and advised the customer to use the documented workaround: avoid repeated soft clears while updates are actively arriving, and if a refresh is needed, either wait until churn has been quiet for at least 60 seconds or use a single hard clear in a maintenance window. The customer applied the workaround and the CPU spikes no longer reproduced. We advised continued monitoring during future routing changes.

subject: P2: AP onboarding delay on Orion OW-20 4.7 impacting wireless service
description: MetroLink Telecom escalated this through the NOC for an Orion OW-20 on 4.7 after multiple APs failed to return to service in time for a planned maintenance window. They initially suspected a controller redundancy problem because the APs came back only after long delays, but the controller remained stable and no failover occurred. TAC verified the issue on `show ap detail <name>` and confirmed that the affected APs were repeatedly retrying join, then becoming inactive until the next discovery cycle. The behavior was consistent across a small number of APs, which narrowed it to the join state machine.
resolution: TAC used the KB-4102 workaround and set `ap join retry-interval 2` to keep the join attempt active during radio capability revalidation. After the change, the affected APs completed the join sequence without dropping out of the retransmit queue. We also confirmed the WAN path met the latency and loss guidance for remote APs.

subject: Missing policy objects after upgrade to 5.1.3 on NF-300
description: IronGate Freight reported that an NF-300 running 5.0.9 was upgraded to 5.1.3 overnight, and the firewall came back online but several policy objects were missing the next morning. The NOC initially suspected a bad import because around 100 access rules and NAT entries had reverted to defaults. I checked the device and confirmed the system was healthy, but `show running-config` showed multiple objects absent or reset after the first login. This matches a post-upgrade configuration replay issue rather than a failure of the upgrade itself.
resolution: TAC advised the customer to move the firewall to 5.2.0, which preserves replay cursor state during checkpoint migration. After the upgrade, the missing objects were restored from the saved pre-upgrade configuration and verified with `show running-config`. This aligns with KB-3111, which identifies the defect in 5.1.3 and 5.1.5 when upgrading from 5.0.x.

subject: AR-900 CPU spikes after repeated BGP soft clears
description: HarborPoint Retail reported that their Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.1 began pegging the routing process after several `clear bgp ipv4 unicast 65001 soft` commands were issued during a prefix refresh window. The on-site engineer noted that forwarding stayed up, but route convergence slowed and the control plane became sluggish for roughly a minute at a time. TAC reviewed `show process cpu` and confirmed the routing task was consuming most of the scheduler slice, with the problem worsening while inbound updates were still arriving. The platform is a busy edge router with a large BGP table, which matches the observed behavior.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2110 and advised avoiding repeated soft clears during peak update activity. The customer was instructed to wait at least 60 seconds after route churn settled before issuing any refresh, or use a single hard clear during a maintenance window if a full session reset was required. After changing the operational procedure, the CPU spikes stopped recurring.

subject: Route recursion issue on AR-900 after static swap
description: Lakeside Hospitality escalated from the NOC after guests reported intermittent loss of outbound connectivity on an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3. The team saw BGP sessions still in Established state, but a group of routes tied to one upstream prefix were missing from `show ip route bgp`. They initially suspected policy changes on the peer, but the route advertisements were still arriving and only the locally installed entries were affected. We found that the problem began immediately after a static route to the same destination was replaced during a change window, and the syslog included `%BGP-4-NH-RESOLVE`.
resolution: TAC matched the case to KB-2107 and confirmed the issue is fixed in 9.3.0. The customer upgraded the Aurora AR-900 from 9.2.3 to 9.3.0, then revalidated the static route replacement and BGP convergence. The affected routes remained active after subsequent changes, which confirmed the fix.

subject: Voice traffic drops for 10-20 seconds after brief LTE brownout
description: Prairie State College opened this through the customer portal after several VoIP calls were moved off the primary LTE path during a short signal drop. The affected edge is atlas-edge-17 running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and `show app-route sla-class` shows the voice class going down even though subsequent probes recover within a few seconds. TAC reviewed the event history and found a single missed 1-second probe followed by path switching for about 15 seconds. The edge log includes "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN" at the time the class state changed.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-5101 and applied the documented workaround on atlas-edge-17 by increasing the SLA probe window to five samples and extending hold-down so one missed probe would not clear the class. The final configuration used the KB-5101 workaround commands, then was committed on the orchestrator and verified with `show app-route sla-class`. The customer confirmed the voice path remained stable after the change.

subject: Intermittent AP join failures on Orion OW-20 4.7
description: Crescent Health Group submitted this through the customer portal for an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.7. They stated that several APs were “stuck waiting” and only reappeared after a reboot, which initially suggested a hardware fault at the edge. TAC reviewed the controller logs and saw the APs stop after repeated join attempts, then go quiet during capability revalidation. The log contained `ERR-APJ-4417`, which aligned with the join-state issue we were seeing on 4.7.
resolution: Per KB-4102, TAC advised an upgrade to 4.8, where join retries are not consumed until capability revalidation completes or times out. The customer upgraded the controller from 4.7 to 4.8 and retested the affected APs. After the upgrade, the APs joined normally and remained registered through subsequent reboot cycles.

subject: Critical uplink bundle on HX-5000 only comes up partially after failover
description: Prairie State College opened a P1 NOC escalation for a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.4 because a campus uplink bundle came back degraded after an upstream change. The team reported that the port-channel should have four members, but only two were forwarding and the other two remained suspended long enough to affect voice and authentication traffic. TAC confirmed the neighbor still shows LACP sync and the local switch logs repeated collect/distribute mismatch events during recovery. The console also displayed "%LACP-4-MISBUNDLE" at the time of the incident.
resolution: TAC identified the incident as the 7.4 LACP condition documented in KB-6106. We applied the article's workaround by setting fast LACP timers on the local bundle and on the peer where possible, then cleared the EtherChannel after link restoration. The port-channel returned to four active members and the college verified the uplink stayed stable after additional failover tests.

subject: Partner escalation: AR-900 OSPF adjacency fails on shared Ethernet segment
description: A partner escalated on behalf of Summit Logistics for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.0 at a regional hub. The reported symptom was that the routing neighbor would not stay established on a multiaccess network, causing route changes and occasional loss of downstream prefixes. TAC found that the problem reproduced only on the shared Ethernet segment and not on point-to-point test links, which narrowed it to an adjacency negotiation problem rather than a generic OSPF process failure. The local interface MTU was 1500, while the peer side was configured lower, matching the known trigger for this release.
resolution: TAC directed the customer to upgrade the AR-900 from 9.2.0 to 9.2.1, per KB-2103. Once upgraded, OSPF correctly re-evaluated the remote MTU on each DBD exchange and the adjacency no longer reset. Post-change monitoring showed the neighbor stable in Full and no further routing interruptions.

subject: Field verification shows microburst starvation on egress queueing
description: An on-site field engineer opened the case for Northstar Bank after users reported that transactions slowed whenever voice traffic peaked on the branch WAN link. The affected platform is an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.1, connected to a 10 Gbps uplink with a strict-priority voice class in the egress policy. Initial field checks found no CRCs, no port errors, and no sign of upstream provider impairment. TAC asked for queueing data and confirmed the priority class was consuming the transmit window while the weighted queues were not being replenished as expected during the burst interval. The symptom was repeatable and limited to short microbursts, which pointed away from a general forwarding problem.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-2105 and directed the customer to upgrade the Aurora AR-900 to 9.2.3. After the upgrade, the router no longer starved best-effort traffic during the voice bursts. The customer confirmed that transaction latency returned to normal under the same test conditions.

subject: AR-900 BGP routes missing after static route edit
description: HarborPoint Retail’s field engineer reported that an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 lost a subset of BGP routes after a static route was modified during a site cutover. The router still showed the BGP neighbor as Established, but the affected prefixes were absent from the forwarding table and traffic to those destinations blackholed. The issue appeared only after the old static route was replaced with a new one to the same prefix, which pointed to a recursive next-hop resolution problem rather than a peer outage. TAC confirmed the behavior on the running version and correlated it with the route-change sequence described by the customer.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-2107 by having the field engineer remove the old static route, wait more than 5 seconds, and then install the replacement so the recursion graph could rebuild cleanly. We also had the customer perform `clear bgp ipv4 unicast 65001 soft` to refresh the affected prefixes without bouncing the session. The routes returned to the table and continued forwarding normally after the change.

subject: Standby on Orion OW-20 not fully catching up after failover
description: Sunset Power Authority sent a TAC mailbox message regarding an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.8. They observed that after a switchover, some wireless clients stayed connected while others had to reauthenticate, which led them to suspect a client roaming issue. TAC checked the controller and found the redundancy pair reporting `sync state: partial`; the event log also repeated `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL`. The configuration database summary showed more than 32,768 rows, which aligns with the incremental sync limit problem in this release.
resolution: TAC advised upgrading the controller to 4.9 per KB-4104, which fixes the incremental synchronization encoder and prevents stalls above 32,768 rows. After the upgrade, redundancy synchronization completed normally and a test failover preserved current WLAN and policy state. The customer confirmed the reauthentication delay was no longer present.

subject: Encrypted path intermittently drops between freight sites
description: IronGate Freight opened an NOC escalation for a Nimbus NF-300 at a regional distribution site. Operators reported that the IPsec tunnel to the head office would drop and re-establish without any obvious WAN outage, usually once or twice per hour. The firewall is running 5.1.5. TAC triage found no interface errors or session table saturation, and the IKEv2 rekey timing aligned with the recurrence pattern seen on affected releases. The customer did not provide logs, but the symptoms were consistent with a phase 2 rekey failure.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3102 and applied the workaround from the article. The tunnel policy was updated to use a single DH group, preferably group 14, on both peers with `crypto ikev2 proposal default dh-group 14`, then committed. After the configuration change, the VPN stayed stable and the periodic drops stopped.

subject: AP join stalls after retries on OW-20 4.7
description: Crescent Health Group called TAC about an Orion OW-20 running 4.7 after noticing that some APs would never finish provisioning unless they were power-cycled. The customer described it as a “stale registration” issue, but TAC saw the controller was accepting the initial join attempts and then stopping partway through the process. The event history showed repeated join retries followed by capability revalidation, after which no more CAPWAP messages arrived from the AP. The log included `ERR-APJ-4417`, matching the known 4.7 join defect.
resolution: TAC followed KB-4102 and applied the supported workaround by changing the join retry interval from 5 seconds to 2 seconds with `ap join retry-interval 2`. This prevented the controller from expiring the transaction before capability revalidation returned. The APs subsequently joined without requiring a power cycle, and the customer confirmed the issue was no longer reproducible.

subject: HX-5000 stack instability on 7.6, request for recommended software version
description: CivicWorks Public Agency escalated through a partner regarding a Helix HX-5000 core switch stack on 7.6 that intermittently showed one member missing from the stack status. The partner initially suspected a stacking module failure, but TAC noted that the member returned automatically after a brief interval and the interconnects never reported down. The event pattern aligns with a heartbeat timing issue on longer cable runs rather than an election problem. During the incident, the switch logged "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN".
resolution: TAC advised upgrading the stack to 8.0, which contains the corrected stack heartbeat processing described in KB-6104. After the upgrade, the stack required three consecutive missed intervals before adjacency teardown and the intermittent member separations stopped. Follow-up monitoring showed stable `show stack` output with no further split-brain events.

subject: Critical application traffic stayed on dead WAN route after maintenance
description: Pinnacle Energy submitted a portal report that a critical application kept sending traffic to a removed WAN route during a scheduled circuit change. The affected Atlas SD-WAN edge is running 3.1, and the customer stated that failover only happened after they waited a few minutes and retried the change. TAC examined the configuration and confirmed that the application-routing policy was still reading the withdrawn path from the local cache until the aging timer expired. This behavior was consistent with the route-cache defect seen on 3.1 edges during underlay withdrawal events.
resolution: TAC resolved the case by applying the workaround described in KB-5109. The route-cache aging timer was changed to 60 seconds with `app-route cache age-time 60`, and the configuration was committed so the stale route would age out sooner during planned cutovers. The customer was advised to use a route-refresh before any future maintenance window and to verify the backup next-hop is selected before proceeding.

subject: intermittent mtu mismatch on lte overlay after moving to 3.1
description: Redwood University emailed that one remote campus lost connectivity to cloud apps after an Atlas SD-WAN edge upgrade to 3.1. The affected edge is 203.0.113.18 running 3.1, and `show sdwan tunnels` still reports both LTE tunnels as established. Their network team originally suspected carrier packet loss, but the failure is consistent across two different SIMs in the same chassis and only for larger packets. The edge log includes repeated "%UPG-5-MTU-MIGRATE" notices, which points to an upgrade-time configuration issue rather than a transport outage.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-5104 and advised upgrading the edge to 3.2, where the migration preserves the configured LTE tunnel MTU across dual-SIM upgrades. After the customer completed the 3.2 upgrade, the LTE tunnel MTU remained intact and the large-packet drops stopped without further manual changes.

subject: HX-5000 stack flapping between members in 7.3
description: NOC escalated a Helix HX-5000 core switch stack running 7.3 after monitoring detected multiple master changes within the same shift. The stack has three members and services a clinic campus; users reported short management-plane interruptions, but data traffic remained mostly unaffected. `show stack` captured momentary split election domains, and the switch log included repeated "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN" events with no corresponding stack port loss or optics alarm. TAC noted the pattern was consistent with a known 7.3 stacking defect triggered by moderate control-plane load.
resolution: TAC tied the symptoms to KB-6103 and recommended upgrading the stack to 7.4. After the upgrade, the election process stabilized, the master remained fixed during load testing, and the repeated stack re-election messages stopped.

subject: HarborPoint Retail NF-300 missing config after upgrade to 5.1.3
description: This was logged from a phone call with HarborPoint Retail regarding an NF-300 that had been upgraded from 5.0.9 to 5.1.3. The caller said the firewall 'looked fine' after reboot, but several policy sets, address groups, and some NAT rules were gone once they signed in. I verified that the appliance was running 5.1.3 and that the issue was not related to session table exhaustion or a failed boot; the startup sequence completed normally, but `show running-config` showed a noticeable set of defaulted objects. The event log included "%UPGRADE-4-REPLAY_CURSOR", which pointed to a migration replay cursor loss during the upgrade.
resolution: TAC referenced KB-3111 and recommended upgrading the NF-300 to 5.2.0, where the checkpoint replay cursor defect is corrected. After the upgrade, the customer restored the missing objects from the saved pre-upgrade configuration and confirmed the running configuration matched the intended policy set. The issue did not recur after reboot on 5.2.0.

subject: OW-20 backup rolled back last SSID change after restore
description: BlueRiver Credit Union emailed that an Orion OW-20 running 4.9 restored without error, but the last SSID security update made before the backup was missing. They noted that the backup was taken after several WLAN edits were staged, and the restored controller appeared to revert only the newest change. TAC reproduced the timing with a similar configuration state and confirmed the commit queue was still non-empty when the backup snapshot was created. There was no database corruption; the backup simply captured the previously committed configuration.
resolution: TAC referenced KB-4112 and advised the customer to wait for the commit queue to clear before performing backups. We recommended verifying the queue state with `show configuration database summary`, issuing `commit` for the staged WLAN edits, and then running `backup configuration` after the system had been idle for 30 seconds.

subject: Brief drops on unicast flows from HX-5000 core
description: BlueRiver Credit Union submitted a portal request stating that a Helix HX-5000 core switch on 8.0 was causing short interruptions to east-west traffic. They described the problem as a general network slowdown, but TAC found that the disruption was isolated to brief output loss on unrelated unicast flows during multicast replication bursts. The switch showed discard increments on the uplink queue in the same intervals, with utilization still below 80 percent, and the logs contained "%BUF-3-OVERFLOW". That combination matched a shared-buffer headroom problem rather than an oversubscribed link.
resolution: TAC followed KB-6110 and applied the recommended workaround. We reduced the multicast reservation on the busiest leaf, placed the replication-heavy workloads on a separate uplink group, and asked the customer to avoid the largest bursts during congestion-sensitive windows. The customer reported that the intermittent loss stopped after the changes were made.

subject: NF-300 slows briefly when threat database activates
