description: Prairie State College emailed TAC about an NF-300 running 5.1.5 that briefly slows down every time the threat database activates new signatures. They initially suspected an ISP issue because the firewall still passed traffic, but students and staff saw downloads stall for under two minutes while new connections were being established. TAC reviewed the reported timing and confirmed existing sessions aged out normally during the event, which pointed away from a session-table exhaustion issue. The customer also provided a recent system log excerpt containing the message '%TP-4-SIGNATURE_STALL' during activation.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3105 and advised an upgrade to 5.2.0. The customer installed 5.2.0 on the NF-300, which resolves the dataplane stall during large signature activation. After the upgrade, the update process completed without the previous throughput drop.

subject: nf-300 rollback during upgrade from 5.0.8 to 5.0.9
description: A partner escalated on behalf of Cornerstone Supermarkets after a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 failed to move to 5.0.9 during a change window. The appliance accepted the HTTPS download, but the next boot entered image verification and then returned to the previous software level. The console includes "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL", while the downloaded image hash matches the published SHA-256 value. TAC confirmed the issue is tied to the boot-loader verification phase on 5.0.8 rather than to the transfer itself.
resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-3104 and directed the customer to upgrade the appliance to 5.0.9, which contains the fix for the boot-loader digest calculation. After the upgrade completed, the device remained on 5.0.9 and no further verification failures were observed.

subject: 3.2 branch LTE overlay drops large packets after upgrade
description: Sunset Power Authority opened this through their partner after upgrading a remote site to Atlas SD-WAN 3.2. The branch edge is on 3.2 and uses LTE as an underlay on a customer-defined APN; the tunnel shows established, but applications fail when packets exceed about 1400 bytes. TAC checked the configuration export and found the interface-level tunnel MTU was not preserved during migration. The upgrade log includes "%UPG-5-MTU-MIGRATE", which matches the behavior seen on the site.
resolution: TAC confirmed the problem matches KB-5110 and advised moving the branch to 3.3, where the migration preserves LTE tunnel MTU values for both default and nondefault APNs. After the customer completed the upgrade, the LTE interface retained the configured MTU and the overlay no longer fragmented oversized packets.

subject: 9.1.4 bgp next-hop unresolved after interface bounce
description: Pinnacle Energy opened the case after an Aurora AR-900 on 9.1.4 stopped forwarding several remote-site prefixes following an interface bounce on the transport VLAN. The on-site field engineer initially suspected a BGP peer problem because the neighbor stayed up and advertisements were still being received. TAC checked the router state and saw BGP remained Established, but the affected IPv4 routes were absent from the forwarding table even though the AS path was present in the BGP table. The behavior matched a recursion issue triggered by a rapid withdraw-and-relearn of the underlay route.
resolution: TAC mapped the symptoms to KB-2101 and used the workaround to force recursion to be rebuilt. The customer removed and re-added the underlay route with `clear ip route 198.51.100.0/24`, which restored the missing prefixes without resetting the BGP session. We noted that the condition is limited to the 9.1 family and recommended scheduling a software update.

subject: Urgent: OW-20 upgrade to 5.0 reverts after migration
description: Redwood University emailed TAC about an Orion OW-20 running 4.6 that failed a direct upgrade to 5.0 during a campus change window. The controller rebooted into the new release, remained reachable for a short period, and then reverted to the prior image after the post-upgrade migration ran. The upgrade log stopped at guest portal object conversion and included "%ERR-UPG-2204". TAC checked the configuration database and found many legacy guest portal ACL objects with empty destination fields.
resolution: Per KB-4111, TAC had the customer boot the old image, remove unused legacy guest portal ACL objects, and export the configuration for review before rerunning the upgrade. After the stale objects were pruned, the upgrade completed successfully on 5.0.

subject: Critical HX-5000 100g link resets with qsfp28 alert clear
description: Sunset Power Authority had an on-site field engineer open a P1 on an HX-5000 core switch running 7.5. The engineer reported that a critical 100G uplink was resetting whenever a transceiver alarm cleared, and captured the following message on the switch: '%TRANSCEIVER-4-LOS'. TAC correlated the event with the optic returning to normal DOM values and the port being withdrawn for a short interval before recovering. The issue was isolated to the transceiver manager path rather than the physical link itself.
resolution: TAC identified the defect as KB-6102 and directed the customer to upgrade the switch to 7.6, where the debounce handling is corrected. After the upgrade, the uplink no longer asserted a spurious loss-of-signal event when DOM thresholds were recomputed. TAC confirmed stable operation and closed the incident.

subject: configure ikev2 tunnels to avoid phase 2 renegotiation
description: HarborPoint Retail is asking how to configure IKEv2 tunnels on Nimbus NF-300 5.1.3 so they do not see phase 2 renegotiation or selector-related failures. They are using a policy-based design today and want to know whether specific selector widths or transform settings can trigger resets. TAC reviewed the request against the product guidance and confirmed the recommended configuration pattern for this release family.
resolution: TAC pointed the customer to GUIDE-NF and recommended avoiding policy-based IKEv2 tunnels with local selectors narrower than /30. For host-to-host designs, the guide recommends using route-based VPN and enforcing traffic restrictions with firewall policy instead. On 5.1.3 and 5.1.5, pin a single DH group on both peers, preferably group 14, and avoid mixed transform sets to prevent phase 2 resets. The guide also provides the following example configuration: config, vpn ikev2 policy-based disable, crypto ikev2 proposal default dh-group 14, crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable, commit.

subject: HX-5000 routing memory leak impacting production fabric
description: MetroLink Telecom submitted a partner escalation on behalf of the customer for a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6. The report said the switch was still forwarding traffic, but the routing process memory kept increasing and the fabric was becoming less responsive during EVPN changes. TAC observed the routing daemon RSS climbing from roughly 900 MB to more than 1.8 GB within a day, with free memory approaching the 12 percent threshold. The logs contained "%MEM-4-LEAK", confirming the same failure signature seen in prior cases. The customer initially believed the issue was caused by a transient peer flap, but the growth continued even after the fabric settled.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as the 7.6 EVPN refresh memory leak described in KB-6112. MetroLink upgraded the HX-5000 to 8.0, which resolves the issue by reusing attribute cache objects and freeing stale generations on each refresh cycle. After the upgrade, RSS remained stable and no further control-plane degradation was observed.

subject: AR-900 upgrade rolls back on 9.1.6 with BGP sessions flapping
description: Prairie State College opened a P2 after an in-service upgrade of an Aurora AR-900 from 9.1.6 to 9.2.0 rolled back to the previous release. The router stayed reachable, but BGP adjacencies dropped for about a minute during the rollback and then recovered; the team initially suspected a software image corruption issue. TAC confirmed the device was running 9.1.6 and that BGP add-path was configured toward at least one neighbor with more than 1,000 advertised paths. No hardware alarms or storage errors were present, and the failure reproduced at the installer precheck stage rather than during image transfer.
resolution: TAC identified this as the upgrade migrator issue described in KB-2111 and had the customer disable BGP add-path before retrying the upgrade. After removing the add-path send configuration on the affected neighbor, the upgrade to 9.2.0 completed normally. Once the router was stable on 9.2.0, the customer re-enabled add-path on the required session.

subject: child sa fails with ikev2-3-ts_unsupported on nf-300
description: MetroLink Telecom phoned TAC about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.1.3 that had a newly built branch VPN with no payload traffic. During initial triage, the device showed an established IKE SA, but the child SA never came up and the peer retried the exchange every 10 seconds. The system log also showed "%IKEV2-3-TS_UNSUPPORTED" during CHILD_SA negotiation, which pointed away from PSK or proposal mismatch and toward a selector problem. The local tunnel policy was configured with a host address selector, which is narrower than the platform accepts for this mode.
resolution: TAC traced the failure to KB-3108 and confirmed the selector compiler limitation affecting policy-based IKEv2 tunnels. We applied the documented workaround by disabling policy-based VPN and moving the security control to a firewall policy on the route-based design. MetroLink Telecom verified the tunnel came up cleanly and traffic counters increased after the change.

subject: NF-300 session spikes after turning on asymmetric routing
description: CivicWorks Public Agency opened an urgent escalation for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.0. After enabling asymmetric path handling on a policy set for several large /24 networks, the firewall began showing intermittent 3 to 4 ms latency spikes on otherwise healthy flows. TAC reviewed the session-table summary and saw two shards climbing into the high 80 percent range while the remaining shards stayed under 40 percent, which matches the reported slowdown. The issue started after about 300,000 new sessions and did not correlate with CPU or HA state.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-3110 by entering config mode, disabling asymmetric routing handling for the affected policy set, and committing the change. After the update, shard occupancy remained below 75 percent and the latency spikes stopped.

subject: 7.2 to 7.4 maintenance upgrade fails on HX-5000 core switch
description: Evergreen Clinic Network’s NOC reported a failed maintenance upgrade on an HX-5000 core switch running 7.2. The process consistently stopped in the high 70s and the management plane came back after a brief restart, but the system returned to the previous image. Operators initially suspected a power issue because traffic stayed up during the attempt. TAC triage confirmed the behavior was limited to the upgrade path and noted that the platform had many populated transceivers, which increased migration time on post-rollback checks.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-6111 and applied the workaround from the article. The NOC backed up the configuration, removed nonessential DOM history, and used `configure terminal`, `no transceiver calibration-history`, `write memory`, and `reload` before retrying the upgrade from a quieter window. The second attempt completed successfully.

subject: Best-effort traffic slows when priority queue is active
description: A call was opened for a MetroLink Telecom Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.1. The customer reported that routine Internet traffic became unusably slow whenever a voice burst hit the WAN link, but only for brief intervals. They initially blamed the provider circuit because the symptom looked like congestion, yet the interface counters showed no drops from the physical layer. TAC review confirmed the router was forwarding on a 10 Gbps uplink with strict-priority voice configured, and `show qos interface` showed the priority queue emptying normally while the other queues stayed almost idle. The behavior was repeatable under microburst load and matched a scheduler fairness problem rather than a carrier issue.
resolution: TAC identified the problem as KB-2105 and moved the customer to Aurora AR-900 9.2.3. The upgrade was completed during the maintenance window, and no configuration workaround was required after validation. Post-upgrade testing showed the weighted queues receiving service normally even after priority bursts.

subject: Repeated overlay alarms on edge during LTE handoff
description: TAC logged this from a phone call with Cornerstone Supermarkets regarding an Atlas SD-WAN edge on version 3.3. The caller said the site had repeated tunnel alarms and a short outage whenever LTE failed over, and they initially believed the orchestrator was pushing a bad policy. On investigation, the edge was running dual LTE modems and the control-plane process was saturating during the handoff window, with CPU pinned close to 100 percent for roughly half a minute. The edge log captured "ERR-LTE-2201" at the same time as the event, which helped correlate the problem with the modem state transition. The issue cleared on its own after the transition completed, and no persistent tunnel or routing faults remained.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-5112 for Atlas SD-WAN 3.3. We applied the workaround by configuring interface lte0 handoff-debounce 5000 and advised the customer to stagger policy changes away from carrier switchover events. After the adjustment, the overlay alarms stopped recurring during LTE handoff.

subject: partner escalation: vpn to branch stuck after ike sa establishes
description: A partner escalated on behalf of IronGate Freight regarding a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.1.5 at a branch office. The report said the VPN looks healthy in the dashboard, but end users cannot reach the remote subnet and the counter values stay at zero. TAC checked the configuration and found a policy-based IKEv2 tunnel using a local host route instead of a broader subnet, which matches the failure pattern for child SA negotiation. The peer was retrying every 10 seconds, while the IKE SA remained established throughout the call.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3108 and explained that policy-based IKEv2 on this platform does not accept a local selector narrower than /30. We implemented the workaround from the article by disabling policy-based VPN and preserving access control with a firewall policy. After the configuration change, IronGate Freight confirmed the tunnel installed its child SA and traffic flowed.

subject: vpn up but zero counters on policy-based ikev2 tunnel
description: Pinnacle Energy submitted a web form for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.1.3. They reported that the VPN shows connected, but the application servers behind it cannot reach the remote site and the tunnel counters remain at zero. TAC reviewed the configuration and found a policy-based IKEv2 setup with a local selector defined as a single host address. The peer was retrying every 10 seconds, which aligned with a child SA negotiation issue rather than a generic outage.
resolution: TAC associated the case with KB-3108 and confirmed the platform limitation for policy-based IKEv2 when the local selector is narrower than /30. We used the documented workaround by disabling policy-based VPN and enforcing the required traffic with firewall policy on the broader subnet design. Pinnacle Energy confirmed the tunnel installed the child SA and carried traffic after the change.

subject: Standby drops replicated sessions after split-brain; recommend code fix
description: A partner escalated on behalf of Prairie State College after repeated HA recovery issues on a Nimbus NF-300 pair running 5.0.9. The customer reported that after a split-brain event, the standby firewall returned to service with a noticeably smaller session table, even though `show ha status` still showed the pair as healthy and synced. TAC reproduced the behavior in lab terms consistent with the customer report and noted the log message "%HA-4-RSYNC_STALE_SEQ" during the recovery path. The pattern matched stale replication handling during resync rather than an outage on the dataplane.
resolution: TAC traced the problem to KB-3103 and, because the customer requested a permanent fix path, recommended upgrading the cluster to 5.2.2. After the upgrade, the standby no longer discarded queued session updates during split-brain recovery. TAC confirmed the issue was resolved without needing repeated manual resyncs.

subject: NOC sees no drops but AR-900 CPU rises on IPv6 bursts
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets escalated through the NOC after several stores began reporting slow IPv6 connectivity on Aurora AR-900 routers running 9.2.3. The network team initially suspected a memory leak, but the devices recovered after a short quiet period and no other protocols showed instability. TAC checked the routers and saw sustained neighbor discovery bursts from a single access VLAN, with `show control-plane protection statistics` remaining at zero drops while CPU utilization climbed from about 15% to 80% plus. The router also logged "%CPP-3-THROTTLE ERR-CPP-4412 IPv6 ND punt accounting mismatch on control-plane queue 2" during the event.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as the 9.2.3 control-plane protection defect documented in KB-2106. We applied the recommended workaround by configuring `police ipv6-nd 2000` and instructed the NOC to use RA guard or storm control on the affected access VLAN to limit further bursts. After the workaround, the drop counter incremented normally and the intermittent IPv6 reachability complaints ceased.

subject: Customer reports 5 GHz channels frozen after radar activity on OW-20 5.1
description: The customer opened this through the portal for an Orion OW-20 running 5.1, saying wireless users were seeing slowdowns and that the access points seemed to “ignore” radar events. Initial triage showed the APs were still up in `show ap summary`, but neighboring APs remained on the same 5 GHz channel after several DFS detections and retries climbed during the busy period. TAC noted that the RF dashboard stopped showing channel-change activity even though the radar counter continued increasing. The pattern was consistent across the affected radio group.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-4110: DFS was disabled on the affected radio group and the radios were pinned to a non-DFS channel set with sufficient separation from neighboring cells. After the change, the controller resumed stable channel behavior and the client retry increase was no longer observed.

subject: brief ipsec traffic loss on nf-300 during timer overlap
description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened a portal ticket for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 after clinicians reported short interruptions to a routed VPN link between clinics. The outage lasted only a second or two, but it recurred every few minutes and affected application traffic more than the tunnel state itself. TAC found the IKEv2 session remained established, yet packet forwarding paused during rekey activity when DPD was also firing on the same 10-second interval. The firewall logs also showed `%IKEV2-4-REKEY_TIMER` during the incident window.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3112. We implemented the documented workaround by changing the DPD interval so it no longer matched the rekey timing, using `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committing the change. Following the adjustment, the tunnel continued to forward traffic without the recurring pause.

subject: OSPF neighbor instability between AR-900 and core switch
description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed TAC stating that their Aurora AR-900 has been losing one routing neighbor since a recent network clean-up. The device is running 9.2.0, and they observed the neighbor never stays in Full state on a broadcast VLAN. Initial triage showed the local interface MTU at 1500 and the peer at 1492, which correlates with repeated database exchange retries on the segment. TAC advised that this behavior is consistent with an OSPF adjacency defect in the current release rather than a general routing failure.
resolution: TAC recommended upgrading the AR-900 from 9.2.0 to 9.2.1, per KB-2103. After the upgrade, the router re-evaluated the remote MTU on each DBD exchange and the neighbor transitioned to Full without further resets. The issue was closed after post-upgrade monitoring showed stable adjacencies and no additional LSDB churn.

subject: Recurring stack member loss on HX-5000 7.6, request for permanent fix
description: IronGate Freight opened this case after their Helix HX-5000 core switch stack running 7.6 showed repeated short outages of one member during the day. They reported that traffic continued, but monitoring kept showing one unit missing and then returning on its own. TAC observed that the stack ports remained electrically up and the pattern matched a heartbeat adjacency drop rather than a hardware fault. The switch generated "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN" during the event.
resolution: TAC confirmed the issue matched KB-6104 and advised that the corrected behavior is available in 8.0. The customer upgraded the HX-5000 stack from 7.6 to 8.0, after which the heartbeat logic no longer tore down adjacency after a single delayed interval. Post-upgrade validation showed stable stack membership with no further brief separations.

subject: AR-900 on 9.1.4 needs upgrade for recurring BFD drops
description: MetroLink Telecom emailed TAC that an Aurora AR-900 on 9.1.4 was losing BFD reachability on multiple upstream peers after extended uptime. Their note said the links stayed up physically, but routing convergence broke and traffic shifted away from healthy paths for a few seconds at a time. Initial review of the exported CLI output showed `show bfd neighbors detail` with frozen transmit counters on the impacted sessions and no corresponding interface errors. The pattern aligns with a known long-uptime BFD scheduler defect on this release.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2102 and advised the customer to upgrade the AR-900 from 9.1.4 to 9.1.6. After the upgrade, BFD transmit scheduling no longer stalled at the uptime wrap point and the affected peers remained stable. No further workaround was required once the system ran the fixed code.

subject: Intermittent TLS bypass on perimeter firewall
description: HarborPoint Retail reported that a small number of customer-facing web sessions were not being inspected on their Nimbus NF-300 firewall. The device is running 5.2.0, and the team initially suspected a policy issue because only certain destinations were affected. TAC checked the SSL inspection statistics and found the cache eviction counter climbing quickly, with the problem appearing after the appliance had been under sustained certificate-cache pressure for several minutes. No packet loss or general forwarding issue was observed, and the rest of the traffic matrix remained stable.
resolution: TAC determined the symptom matched KB-3106 for Nimbus NF-300 5.2.0. We applied the recommended workaround by increasing the certificate cache size so eviction activity stayed below the threshold associated with the bypass condition, then committed the configuration. The customer was advised to restart SSL inspection only if they needed to clear any remaining stale lookup state before the change took effect.

subject: HX-5000 7.6 EVPN routes not updating after gateway move
description: Summit Logistics submitted this through the customer portal and reported intermittent blackholing between two DC pods on an HX-5000 fabric running 7.6. They initially suspected a routing loop, but TAC found the symptom occurred only after the anycast gateway MAC moved between leafs during a maintenance event. `show evpn route-type 5` still listed the affected prefixes locally, yet the remote VTEPs continued forwarding to the older next hop. The switch log included "%EVPN-4-RT5-STALL" shortly after the move, matching the stalled route advertisement behavior.
resolution: TAC correlated the behavior to KB-6108 and applied the documented workaround: configure terminal, router evpn, address-family l2vpn evpn, route-refresh. After the controlled EVPN route refresh, the remote VTEPs relearned the current next hop and traffic recovered without requiring a software change.

subject: Interface traps arriving out of order on 9.3.0 during link oscillation
description: Crescent Health Group opened the case after their Aurora AR-900 on 9.3.0 began sending interface alarms out of order to the monitoring system. The on-site field engineer said the NMS was missing some linkDown notifications and then receiving stale linkUp alerts several seconds later. The router log included "ERR-SNMP-3019" while multiple copper ports were bouncing during a patch-panel issue. TAC confirmed that polling remained stable and the loss was limited to trap delivery during the burst.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-2109 and explained that the SNMP notification queue can overflow under a flap storm. We applied the workaround from the article by configuring link debounce on the affected interfaces to suppress rapid transitions, and recommended treating traps as advisory while relying on short-interval polling. No upgrade was performed; the customer remained on 9.3.0.

subject: NAT pool exhaustion alarms on AR-900 with low active translation count
description: Sunset Power Authority opened a P1 from the NOC because their Aurora AR-900 running 9.3.0 began dropping new internet-bound connections across several substations. The NOC noted the router was not actually full in `show nat translations`, but application retries spiked whenever a burst of short-lived telemetry sessions ended. TAC checked the event buffer and found repeated `ERR-NAT-4108` entries associated with source-port allocation failures. The failure pattern was tied to traffic bursts of roughly 20,000 to 30,000 sessions per minute, which lined up with the customer's reporting window.
resolution: TAC mapped the case to KB-2108 and confirmed this was the known 9.3.0 NAT allocator issue with deferred-free accounting. We implemented the workaround from the article by enlarging the NAT pool with an additional public address and setting the translation timeout to 240 seconds so the allocator had more headroom. The customer restored service without changing software and agreed to watch for deferred-free pressure during future peak events.

subject: HX-5000 port-channel only forms with 2 members after link flap
description: Redwood University opened this through the customer portal after a classroom core maintenance window. Their Helix HX-5000 core switch is running 7.4, and a 4-link EtherChannel to an adjacent switch comes back with only 2 active members after one member is bounced. The missing links stay suspended for roughly a minute, then may join later without intervention. TAC confirmed the peer reports LACP sync, but the local switch is seeing repeated collect/distribute mismatch events; the log also shows "%LACP-4-MISBUNDLE" during the flap.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-6106 for HX-5000 7.4. We applied the documented workaround by configuring fast LACP timers on the port-channel and the peer where supported, then cleared the affected bundle after link restoration. After the change, all four members joined consistently and no further mismatch events were observed.

subject: OW-20 redundancy pair shows partial sync until upgrade
description: Lakeside Hospitality opened a NOC escalation for an Orion OW-20 running 4.8 after a failover test left several guest SSIDs in an inconsistent state. The customer initially suspected a bad HA link, but both peers remained reachable and the standby never fully converged after the switchover. TAC confirmed `sync state: partial` on `show redundancy status` and noted repeated `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL` messages in the event log. `show configuration database summary` showed the database had passed 32,768 rows, matching the known 4.8 sync stall behavior.
resolution: TAC identified KB-4104 as the cause and recommended upgrading the controller from 4.8 to 4.9, where incremental synchronization uses a 32-bit object index. After the customer completed the upgrade, a follow-up failover test showed the standby receiving the full configuration and no further sync stall events. Client reauthentication after switchover returned to normal timing.

subject: Some access points stuck in joining state
description: HarborPoint Retail opened this portal case because a small set of APs on an Orion OW-20 running 4.6 never finish joining after a controller reboot. The APs can communicate with the controller and keep trying, but they remain stuck in discovery/join and their radios do not enable. `show ap summary` shows the affected APs as down/joining, while other APs in the same site are healthy. Initial triage indicated the failures were limited to models that use the same AP group and custom RF settings.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-4101 and confirmed it was the 4.6 CAPWAP parser defect tied to an empty RF profile TLV. We implemented the workaround by clearing the AP group RF profile override so the controller stopped generating the zero-length TLV during join. The APs then completed association normally, and the customer was advised that the permanent fix is in 4.7.

subject: 802.11r roaming issue on OW-20 4.9 causing brief packet loss
description: Lakeside Hospitality emailed TAC to report that some roaming clients on Orion OW-20 4.9 experience a brief stall when moving between APs. The customer originally suspected RF interference, but packet captures and `show client detail <mac>` indicate the client completes reassociation and then delays before user traffic resumes. The controller was operating above normal load during the incident window. The logs showed "%ROAM-5-FT_KEYTIMEOUT" on the affected clients.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-4105 and implemented the workaround described there. We set `wlan corp accounting interval 60` to reduce queue pressure and advised the customer to keep controller CPU below 70% when validating roaming performance. The customer was asked to retest after the change and to defer any broader 802.11r changes until the next maintenance window.

subject: Summit Logistics: VXLAN prefix stale until EVPN refresh on HX-5000
description: Summit Logistics emailed TAC reporting that hosts behind their HX-5000 core switch on 7.6 could reach the gateway locally, but remote sites could not reach some new prefixes after a maintenance switchover. Their message suggested a BGP peer flap, but TAC found the underlay remained stable and only EVPN type-5 propagation was affected. The local switch continued to show the prefix in `show evpn route-type 5`, while remote VTEPs kept the previous next hop for several minutes. The log history included "%EVPN-4-RT5-STALL" at the same time as the anycast gateway MAC move.
resolution: TAC determined the case matched KB-6108 and applied the documented workaround rather than changing software. After entering configure terminal, router evpn, address-family l2vpn evpn, and running route-refresh, the stale type-5 routes were re-advertised and the remote peers updated to the correct VTEP.

subject: Repeated TCN storms from edge port on helix hx-5000
description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed TAC about a Helix HX-5000 running 7.4 that was causing intermittent campus outages on a security appliance uplink. They reported that the switch was “rebooting the port” after a downstream device restart, but the port never actually bounced. TAC found the log message "%STP-5-TCN-STORM" recurring every few seconds, and `show spanning-tree detail` showed the same access port reentering forwarding while the MAC table on that interface aged out far faster than 300 seconds. The affected device was a clustered appliance that legitimately moves multiple MAC addresses, which matched the pattern of a stable physical link with repeated topology-change events.
resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-6105 and advised that there is no software fix for this behavior. We applied the documented workaround by removing rapid-pvst from that multi-MAC edge design and recommending a dedicated edge VLAN or a port restricted to a single access device. After the change, the TCN storm cleared and the MAC aging behavior normalized.

subject: Branch LTE circuit fragments traffic after upgrade
description: Evergreen Clinic Network submitted a portal request for a branch edge running Atlas SD-WAN 3.2. They said their LTE backup circuit was online, but video and other larger flows were unstable after the upgrade, while basic browsing still worked. TAC checked the edge state and saw the tunnel was established, then confirmed the issue affected an interface using a nondefault APN where the previous MTU override was not present in the migrated config. The customer noted packet loss on larger transfers, but no log details were included in the submission.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as the 3.2 migration issue described in KB-5110 and directed the customer to upgrade the edge to 3.3. After the upgrade, the LTE tunnel MTU was retained correctly and the branch stopped fragmenting larger packets.

subject: Frequent tunnel degradation on 2.9 freight hub edge
description: IronGate Freight called TAC after a second branch site began switching overlay tunnels between up and degraded several times an hour. The agent noted the customer was running Atlas SD-WAN 2.9 on the edge and had already replaced the ISP handoff without improvement. TAC checked `show sdwan tunnels` on the reported device and observed that the loss counter increased only when large uploads were active; the transport stayed physically up throughout the event. The log buffer also contained "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN", which matched the customer's report of application steering moving voice calls away from the preferred route.
resolution: TAC identified this as the 2.9 queueing defect described in KB-5105. We implemented the workaround by reserving a high-priority queue for SLA probes with `app-route sla-class voice probe-queue priority` and committed the policy change. Once applied, the tunnel health remained stable during the freight export jobs and the path selection stopped oscillating.

subject: Intermittent client reauth after standby takeovers on OW-20
description: MetroLink Telecom NOC escalated an Orion OW-20 in 4.8 after a planned failover caused voice clients to reauthenticate and some handsets dropped traffic for roughly 30 to 60 seconds. The standby came back online, but the WLAN and policy state appeared older than the active peer. TAC checked the redundancy status and found `sync state: partial`; the event log repeatedly showed `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL`. The configuration database summary indicated the row count had exceeded 32,768, which is consistent with the sync encoder stall seen on this release.
resolution: TAC implemented the KB-4104 workaround by removing unused configuration objects to bring the database under 30,000 rows, then ran `redundancy force-resync` during a maintenance window. Synchronization completed and the standby received current WLAN and client-policy state. The customer was advised that this is a 4.8 limitation and to plan an upgrade path when possible.

subject: Guest portal login loop after redundancy switchover on OW-20 4.9
description: Partner escalation for Crescent Health Group on an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.9. Guest users can complete the captive portal login on the active unit, but after a planned redundancy failover the browser returns to the login page and the session never becomes authorized. TAC reviewed the portal and redundancy status and confirmed the issue starts immediately after the standby takes over, while the guest database remains populated. The controller portal log shows repeated "%PORTAL-5-COOKIE_MISMATCH" messages during the redirect loop.
resolution: This matched KB-4109. The customer upgraded the OW-20 pair from 4.9 to 5.0, which changes guest portal cookie validation to use the redundancy cluster identity rather than the active node UUID. After the upgrade, guest authentication and post-failover session persistence were verified with repeated switchover testing.

subject: Partner reports upgrade rollback on Orion OW-20
description: A partner escalated on behalf of MetroLink Telecom for an Orion OW-20 running 4.6. The customer had initiated a direct upgrade to 5.0, but the controller rebooted into the target image and then fell back to the older software before the maintenance window ended. The upgrade log ended while guest portal objects were being converted and showed "%ERR-UPG-2204". TAC also noted that the database summary showed more than 50 legacy guest ACL entries created before the schema change in 4.7.
resolution: Per KB-4111, TAC advised the partner to boot the old image, delete unused legacy guest portal ACL objects, and verify the database export before running the upgrade again. After the stale ACL objects were pruned, the retry completed successfully.

subject: ar-900 bgp routes vanish after underlay flap on 9.1.4
description: Prairie State College reported that an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4 was losing a block of eBGP IPv4 routes after the WAN handoff flapped during a maintenance window. The on-site field engineer said BGP stayed established, but several prefixes would no longer install into the routing table until the box was touched. TAC reviewed `show bgp summary` and confirmed the session remained up while `show ip route bgp` omitted about 120 learned routes. The event log also showed "%BGP-4-NH-RESOLVE" shortly after the connected underlay route was withdrawn and re-added.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2101 and applied the documented workaround by clearing the BGP process for the affected IPv4 unicast table. After `clear bgp ipv4 unicast 65001`, the next-hop recursion was recomputed and the missing routes reinstalled. We advised the customer to avoid repeated underlay flaps until a maintenance window is available.

subject: AR-900 9.3.0 SLAAC prefix expires early when upstream RA is blocked
description: IronGate Freight reported that an Aurora AR-900 on 9.3.0 was still advertising the prefix in configuration, but client devices on VLAN 10 lost IPv6 access shortly after a scheduled upstream filter change. The complaints were that laptops could still ping locally for a short time, then new connections stopped working and Neighbor Discovery lookups failed. No log extract was provided with the escalation, but the timing matched the typical 3-minute hold interval after the last valid router advertisement was suppressed. TAC confirmed the configured valid lifetime remained 7200 seconds and that the router itself had not removed the prefix from the running configuration.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2104 and explained that this is a design constraint when SLAAC is combined with router advertisement suppression on Aurora AR-900. We advised the customer to stop suppressing router advertisements on the active user VLAN, or to use DHCPv6 stateful addressing for that subnet if suppression must remain. The workaround was applied and verified by the NOC, restoring stable IPv6 connectivity for the affected hosts.

subject: NF-300 requires upgrade for session-table imbalance
description: CivicWorks Public Agency submitted a follow-up case through the portal for the same Nimbus NF-300 appliance, still on 5.2.0. They reported that the firewall was stable for a while after a policy change, but later the session-table imbalance returned under a larger traffic burst. TAC reviewed the live state and saw the log message "%SESSION-4-HASH_SKEW" alongside one shard holding near 88 percent occupancy while the others remained below 40 percent. This behavior aligned with the known asymmetric-routing hashing defect on 5.2.0.
resolution: TAC advised and assisted with an upgrade to 5.2.2 per KB-3110, which fixes session hashing to use the full 5-tuple and redistributes shards once occupancy exceeds 75 percent. After the upgrade, the shard imbalance did not recur during validation traffic.

subject: Site-to-site tunnel on Atlas 3.2 stays in negotiating
description: Sunset Power Authority’s field engineer reported that a solar farm edge could not establish its site-to-site tunnel after the remote firewall team tightened the proposal policy. The Atlas SD-WAN edge is running 3.2, and `show sdwan tunnels` shows the peer permanently in negotiating while other local services continue to pass traffic. The edge logs include "%IKE-3-PROPOSAL-MISMATCH" on each retransmission interval, which points to a transform-set compatibility problem rather than a link issue. The engineer also noted that the WAN circuit is stable and latency is within normal range.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-5106 and used the documented workaround. We had the remote peer accept an AES-GCM proposal without a separate integrity field, then committed the change and verified the resulting SA proposal on both sides. The tunnel established on the next negotiation cycle and remained stable afterward.

subject: Fast transition roam delay on wireless controller 4.9
description: IronGate Freight's field engineer reported that handheld scanners and softphone clients pause for a fraction of a second when moving between access points on an Orion OW-20 running 4.9. The delay is noticeable in the warehouse aisles and is worse when several users roam at once. TAC reviewed a live `show client detail <mac>` sample and saw successful reassociation followed by a delayed return to forwarding state. The controller was under moderate load at the time, which aligned with the reported symptoms.
resolution: This behavior matches KB-4105. TAC applied the documented workaround by lowering the accounting interval to 60 seconds with `wlan corp accounting interval 60` and recommended keeping controller CPU below 70% during roaming tests. The customer was told to use the workaround until their planned maintenance window.

subject: NF-300 IPsec tunnel flaps every hour on 5.1.3
description: Partner escalated for Evergreen Clinic Network reporting intermittent IPsec tunnel drops between a Nimbus NF-300 and a remote healthcare hub. The customer sees the tunnel recover on its own, then drop again roughly 30 to 60 minutes later, which is causing brief loss of access to imaging and scheduling systems. The firewall is running 5.1.3. Initial TAC review of `show crypto ikev2 sa` shows the child SA lifetimes alternating between rekey cycles, which matches the rekey instability pattern seen on this release.
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as KB-3102 and applied the documented workaround by pinning a single DH group on both peers. The customer set `crypto ikev2 proposal default dh-group 14` in config mode and committed the change. After the update, the tunnel stopped flapping and rekeys completed normally.

subject: ikev2 child sa does not install on /31 selector
description: Pinnacle Energy emailed TAC about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9 that could not carry traffic over an IKEv2 VPN. Their message reported that the peer reaches an established state, but no packets move and the remote end retries the exchange every 10 seconds. TAC review showed the local policy uses a /31 selector on the firewall, which matches the symptoms of a child SA negotiation problem rather than an authentication failure. The issue reproduced in lab with the same selector size, and the log buffer contained "%IKEV2-3-TS_UNSUPPORTED" during CHILD_SA setup.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-3108 and confirmed it is the known selector limitation for policy-based IKEv2 tunnels. Per the documented workaround, we disabled policy-based VPN and shifted the design to route-based VPN with a firewall policy to restrict traffic. Pinnacle Energy applied the change and reported the tunnel passed traffic normally afterward.

subject: SNMP alert gaps on AR-900 after port flapping, 9.2.0
description: Evergreen Clinic Network submitted this through the customer portal for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.0. They reported that the monitoring platform was missing some interface-down alerts and later replaying them out of sequence, which made the incident timeline confusing. During TAC review, we saw repeated trap loss consistent with a notification burst rather than a polling failure, and the router logged "ERR-SNMP-3019" during the event window. The issue was reproduced only when the access ports were flapping rapidly over a short interval.
resolution: TAC traced the symptoms to KB-2109, which documents the AR-900 SNMP trap queue limit. We implemented the workaround by enabling 500 ms link debounce on the affected Ethernet ports and advised the customer to shorten polling to 30 seconds so the NMS could reconcile state changes if traps were dropped. The device stayed on 9.2.0 because no software fix is available for this queue-capacity behavior.

subject: HX-5000 7.4 does not restore all EtherChannel members after link bounce
description: Evergreen Clinic Network escalated through a partner after seeing intermittent throughput loss on a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.4. They described the problem as “one or two links disappearing” from a four-port aggregation after a maintenance cutover. TAC review showed the partner switch and the local switch both advertise LACP, but the local system is suspending ports that should be participating in the bundle. The symptoms match a transient aggregation mismatch on member rejoin.
resolution: TAC mapped the case to KB-6106 and advised the documented workaround for 7.4. We configured fast LACP timers on the affected port-channel and coordinated the peer configuration so the members would rejoin promptly after a flap. Once the link state was cleared, the bundle returned to four active links and the clinic confirmed normal traffic levels.

subject: AR-900 CPU spikes and IPv6 neighbors flapping on 9.2.3
description: CivicWorks Public Agency called TAC after an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 began showing brief CPU spikes to the 80% range during business hours. The reporter said several IPv6 hosts on one access VLAN kept going stale and then relearning, even though interface counters and BGP looked normal. During triage, `show control-plane protection statistics` stayed at 0 drops for nearly a minute while the control-plane CPU increased, and the event correlated with bursts of neighbor discovery traffic from a single switch segment. The syslog buffer also contained "%CPP-3-THROTTLE ERR-CPP-4412 IPv6 ND punt accounting mismatch on control-plane queue 2".
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as the 9.2.3 control-plane policer accounting issue tracked in KB-2106. We applied the workaround from the article by lowering IPv6 ND policing with `configure` followed by `control-plane` and `police ipv6-nd 2000`, then asked the customer to enable RA guard/storm control on the access VLAN and isolate the source port if needed. After the change, drop counters began incrementing as expected and neighbor state stabilized.

subject: LACP bundle on HX-5000 intermittently suspends members after maintenance
description: Northstar Bank reported that a production uplink on a Helix HX-5000 running 7.4 does not always return to four active members after scheduled maintenance. The issue appears when one member link is bounced; the bundle stays partially formed for 30 to 90 seconds and traffic uses only half the links. Initial triage found the neighbor in LACP sync state, but the switch kept logging repeated collect/distribute mismatch transitions. The agent captured "%LACP-4-MISBUNDLE" on the console during the event.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as the known 7.4 LACP mis-bundle described in KB-6106. We used the workaround from the article: enabled fast LACP timers on the local port-channel and coordinated the same setting on the peer, then cleared the EtherChannel after the link was restored. The bundle recovered with four active members and remained stable under subsequent maintenance testing.

subject: rekey failures on nf-300 fixed after moving to 5.1.3
description: IronGate Freight called TAC by phone about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9 that was protecting an operational tunnel to a warehouse site. The caller initially described the problem as 'random packet loss,' but packet captures and device counters showed the loss only during IPsec rekey windows. TAC confirmed that `show crypto ikev2 sa` held the IKE SA in ESTABLISHED while the child SA restarted, and the logs included `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. The symptoms matched a proposal mismatch during CREATE_CHILD_SA, especially after a recent PFS group change on the remote peer.
resolution: TAC linked the case to KB-3101 and recommended upgrading the Nimbus NF-300 to 5.1.3, the first fixed release for this issue. The customer completed the upgrade and then cleared the tunnel so both peers renegotiated cleanly with the rebuilt proposal list. After validation, rekey traffic completed without drops and the case was closed.

subject: SLA class flaps on short brownouts in 2.8
description: IronGate Freight escalated through the NOC because eastbound traffic was being moved away from the preferred MPLS path after brief LTE brownouts. The branch edge, atlas-edge-04, is running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8 and shows the app-route voice class dropping for roughly 10 to 20 seconds after a single probe timeout. TAC checked `show app-route sla-class` and saw that packet loss stayed below the configured threshold after the event, but the class still recovered slowly. The issue was isolated to the 2.8 SLA decision logic rather than a transport failure.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-5101 and confirmed it is fixed in 2.9. The customer upgraded atlas-edge-04 from 2.8 to 2.9, then revalidated the policy state after the upgrade. After the version change, the SLA class no longer dropped on a single missed probe interval.

subject: AR-900 OSPF adjacency bouncing on shared segment
description: BlueRiver Credit Union opened this case from the field after users reported intermittent reachability to a branch site. Their Aurora AR-900 is on 9.2.0 and peers with another router on a shared Ethernet segment. The engineer noted that the neighbor comes up briefly and then falls back to ExStart, with the route table oscillating every 20 to 30 seconds. TAC review of the interface details showed a local MTU of 1500 and a peer MTU lower than that, which points to the known adjacency reset condition on this release.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-2103 workaround by configuring OSPF MTU-ignore on the affected interface so the routers would complete adjacency despite the MTU difference. The neighbor reached Full after the change and remained stable during soak testing. The ticket was closed as a workaround success on Aurora AR-900 9.2.0.

subject: CPU saturation on Atlas edge during LTE failover, tunnels briefly degraded
description: Partner escalation opened for Evergreen Clinic Network on an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.3. The site uses two LTE modems and reported intermittent tunnel drops when one carrier lost signal, with the orchestrator showing degraded overlay status for a short period. TAC observed the edge control plane at 95 to 100 percent during the switchover interval and saw tunnel keepalives lagging until the handoff completed. The edge log captured "%LTE-3-HANDOFF_DEFERRED" and "ERR-LTE-2201" during the event, followed by repeated transport reevaluation activity until the state machine settled. The symptom was transient and did not present on a comparable single-modem edge in the same tenant.
resolution: TAC traced the behavior to KB-5112 and confirmed it matches the 3.3 dual-modem LTE handoff defect. We implemented the workaround by configuring interface lte0 handoff-debounce 5000 and advised the customer to avoid policy pushes during carrier switchover windows. This reduced the handoff churn and eliminated the CPU spike.

subject: IKEv2 child SA resets after rekey on 5.1.5
description: Evergreen Clinic Network NOC opened this case after their Nimbus NF-300 began dropping one of several site-to-site VPNs during scheduled rekey events. They reported the issue started after a maintenance window and that only one peer was affected, while others remained stable. The firewall is running 5.1.5. TAC reviewed the tunnel history and found that `show crypto ikev2 sa` showed rekey activity consistent with a phase 2 reset rather than a transport outage, and the device log included `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH` immediately after the peer attempted the rekey.
resolution: TAC tied the symptoms to KB-3102 and advised upgrade to the fixed release. The customer upgraded the firewall from 5.1.5 to 5.2.0, where the responder uses the negotiated DH group from the active child SA context. After the upgrade, rekey events completed without child SA resets.

subject: AR-900 stale IPv6 neighbors during peak on 9.2.3
description: HarborPoint Retail reported that a branch Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 intermittently showed IPv6 neighbors in Stale state during store opening traffic. The caller originally suspected an OSPF problem, but routing adjacencies were stable and only the local access VLAN was affected. On triage, TAC saw that the control-plane protection counters did not move for several seconds even though the CPU climbed from 18% to roughly 85% under a burst of neighbor discovery frames. The platform logs included "%CPP-3-THROTTLE ERR-CPP-4412 IPv6 ND punt accounting mismatch on control-plane queue 2".
resolution: TAC determined this was the known 9.2.3 policer undercount issue described in KB-2106. We implemented the workaround from the article by setting `police ipv6-nd 2000` in control-plane configuration and recommended enabling RA guard on the access VLAN to reduce the burst rate. After the change, the router resumed dropping excess ND traffic instead of forwarding it to the CPU, and neighbor state no longer oscillated.

subject: Branch VPN negotiation failure on Atlas edge 3.2
description: Prairie State College called after a branch VPN stopped coming up following a routine policy change on the far-end security device. The Atlas SD-WAN edge is running 3.2, and the tunnel remained down while the edge continued normal overlay retry attempts. TAC reviewed the configuration and saw that the remote side required a single ESP proposal with both encryption and integrity attributes combined. No log excerpt was provided by the caller, but the negotiation pattern matched a known compatibility limitation in this release.
resolution: TAC determined the case aligned with KB-5106 and recommended moving the edge to 3.3, where the negotiator emits the combined ESP proposal required by the peer. The customer completed the upgrade and rechecked the site. The tunnel came up on the first post-upgrade negotiation attempt.

subject: Voice handsets brief dropouts when moving between APs
description: Summit Logistics emailed TAC about short audio interruptions on warehouse handhelds as employees walked between coverage zones. Their Orion OW-20 controller is on 5.0, and the customers said the handsets reconnect quickly but sound like they are 'hanging' for a moment during roaming. TAC reviewed the mobility pattern and found the problem only showed up when a larger group of clients moved within about ten seconds. The controller was completing reassociation, but the fast transition path was not always staying on the expected sequence.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-4106 and applied the recommended workaround on the 5.0 controller. `roam batch-size 8` was set and roaming tests were staggered to keep the FT flush inside the required completion window, which eliminated the noticeable service gaps.

subject: Session table on standby lags after HA recovery event
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets reported on-site that their Nimbus NF-300 appliance on 5.0.9 recovered from an HA flap, but the standby box still showed fewer sessions than the active unit. The field engineer said the cluster looked normal in `show ha status`, yet the standby remained behind by about 40,000 sessions before gradually catching up. TAC reviewed the device state and found the log message "%HA-4-RSYNC_STALE_SEQ" associated with the recovery period. The symptom profile fit a replication ordering issue after split-brain rather than a packet-loss or licensing problem.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3103 and applied the documented workaround. The engineer ran `ha resync full` in config mode and committed the change, then left the failover links stable for longer than 120 seconds so the replay queue could drain. The standby session table converged to match the active unit.

subject: FT fallback seen on OW-20 after busy clinic roaming
description: Partner escalation for Evergreen Clinic Network reported that the Orion OW-20 on 5.0 was allowing clients to roam, but voice handsets were still pausing every few moves. TAC reproduced the problem during a mobility test with many clients roaming together and captured a controller event trail showing reassociation success followed by the log message '%ROAM-5-FT_KEYTIMEOUT'. The partner also provided client output showing `ft fallback: yes` on devices that should have stayed on 802.11r. The symptom only appeared under heavier roam density and did not resemble an authentication outage.
resolution: TAC correlated the case with KB-4106. The controller was upgraded from 5.0 to 5.1, which resolves the delayed FT key push behavior by sending keys immediately when the client enters reassociation.

subject: Upgrade to 9.2.0 aborts on AR-900 with add-path state error
description: Summit Logistics reported that their Aurora AR-900 on 9.1.4 failed an in-service upgrade to 9.2.0 and stayed on the old release after rollback. The event log included "ERR-UPG-1307" during the session migration step after the image was staged. TAC reviewed the configuration and found BGP add-path enabled on an external neighbor, with the router advertising well over 1,000 paths at the time of the attempt. The symptom set matched an installer precheck abort rather than a routing-plane crash.
resolution: TAC traced the failure to KB-2111 and recommended upgrading to 9.2.1, where the migrator handles add-path state correctly. The customer completed the upgrade path by first moving the router from 9.1.4 to 9.2.1, which succeeded without rollback. After booting 9.2.1, BGP add-path was left enabled and sessions came up normally.

subject: Partner escalation: AR-900 upgrade from 9.1.4 aborts at add-path migration
description: Lakeside Hospitality escalated through a partner for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4 that repeatedly failed an in-service upgrade to 9.2.0. The partner initially suspected a bad image because the device rebooted back into 9.1.4 after staging, but the router showed no flash or bootloader faults. TAC confirmed the upgrade log contained "ERR-UPG-1307" and that BGP add-path was enabled on at least one neighbor. The configuration and path count both matched the known trigger condition, with more than 1,000 advertised paths present during the attempt.
resolution: TAC referenced KB-2111 and instructed the customer to proceed to 9.2.1 instead of 9.2.0, since the fix is present in 9.2.1. The partner completed the upgrade from 9.1.4 to 9.2.1 successfully. Once on 9.2.1, the AR-900 resumed normal operation and the add-path configuration remained in place.

subject: OW-20 backup missing recent WLAN edits after restore
description: Pinnacle Energy reported that an Orion OW-20 running 5.1 restored from a manual configuration backup, but the newest SSID rename and radio profile change from earlier the same morning were gone. Their portal note said the backup completed cleanly and there was no warning, but the restored controller reverted the last WLAN changes to the prior values. TAC reviewed the configuration database status and confirmed the commit queue was not empty when the backup was taken. The behavior matches a backup captured before pending WLAN edits were committed.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-4112 and advised the customer to wait until the commit queue drains to zero before taking a configuration backup. We recommended using `show configuration database summary` to verify the queue is empty, then `commit` if needed and run `backup configuration` only after at least 30 seconds of idle time following the last WLAN edit.

subject: HA pair shows synced but standby session count stays low after failover event
description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed TAC to report that their Nimbus NF-300 HA pair on 5.0.9 recovered from a brief split-brain event, but the standby unit was still missing a portion of sessions. They said the firewall pair showed healthy and synced, yet the standby session table remained lower than the active unit by roughly 25,000 entries for several minutes. On review, TAC confirmed the device was running Nimbus NF-300 5.0.9 and noted the log message "%HA-4-RSYNC_STALE_SEQ" on the standby during recovery. The behavior matches a replay/sequence mismatch during HA resynchronization rather than a general session table capacity issue.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3103 and applied the documented workaround. The customer forced a full HA resync from config mode with `ha resync full`, then kept the failover links stable long enough for the replay queue to drain. Session counts converged after the full resync completed.

subject: APs not coming online on OW-20 4.6
description: Crescent Health Group escalated this from the NOC after several APs at one site failed to come online following an Orion OW-20 controller update to 4.6. The APs reach the controller and keep retrying, but they never get past discovery/join and the radios remain disabled. `show ap summary` shows the units as down/joining, which was initially mistaken for a link or DHCP issue. TAC reproduced the behavior on the controller and confirmed the APs were not completing CAPWAP association.
resolution: TAC matched the failure pattern to KB-4101 and found the AP group had a custom RF profile override causing the controller to emit a zero-length RF profile TLV. We applied the workaround described in the article by removing the RF profile override, then verified the APs joined successfully and stayed up. The customer was told this is a 4.6 defect and to maintain the workaround until they can move to 4.7.

subject: OW-20 5.1 5 GHz radios stop changing channels after repeated DFS hits
description: On-site field engineer reported that multiple APs on an Orion OW-20 running 5.1 stayed on the same 5 GHz channel after several radar hits in a short window. `show ap summary` showed the APs remained up, but neighboring cells continued to use a channel that should have been vacated and client retries rose during the event. TAC reviewed the RF state and confirmed the radar counter kept incrementing while no further channel-change entries were generated. The controller syslog also showed "%RF-4-DFS_FREEZE" at the time channel changes stopped.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-4110: DFS was disabled on the affected radio group and the 5 GHz radios were pinned to a non-DFS channel set with adequate separation from adjacent cells. After the change, channel updates resumed normally and client retry rates returned to baseline.

subject: stage a firmware upgrade with minimal config loss risk
description: Pinnacle Energy is preparing to upgrade a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 and asked how to stage the upgrade while reducing the chance of configuration loss or image rejection. They want to know which prechecks to run, whether to back up the configuration first, and what transfer method to use for the 5.0.9 image. TAC reviewed the request and summarized the upgrade handling steps from the product guide.
resolution: TAC pointed the customer to GUIDE-NF and advised keeping each checkpoint file under 4,000 entries before upgrading from 5.0.x to 5.1.3 or 5.1.5, then verifying the running configuration immediately after reboot. If the configuration has more than 4,096 replay entries, the guide recommends splitting the upgrade into smaller chunks or exporting and re-importing policy objects after first boot. On 5.0.8, stage 5.0.9 images with SCP or USB rather than HTTPS so the boot loader does not reject a valid image because of padding, and always verify the staged image hash and confirm the image appears in software inventory. Example commands from the guide are: show configuration checkpoint summary, copy running-config backup://198.51.100.20/nf300-preupgrade.cfg, copy scp://198.51.100.10/nf300-5.0.9.bin system image, and show software image.

subject: Policy push delay on 3.0 orchestrator with large route-map
description: Lakeside Hospitality emailed TAC about Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator 3.0 after a branch policy update appeared to hang and then fail with no visible change on the edge. Initial triage showed the orchestrator policy worker consuming sustained high CPU during the push, and the tenant configuration included one route-map with 258 entries. The customer also attached logs showing repeated policy serialization retries. The quoted error was: "%ORCH-3-ERR-ORCH-4412 policy push stalled during route-map serialization".
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-5103 and confirmed it was the known 3.0 route-map expansion defect. Lakeside Hospitality upgraded the orchestrator to 3.1, where the policy compiler uses a dynamically sized route-map serializer. After the upgrade, the policy push completed normally and subsequent commits cleared on the first attempt.

subject: AR-900 OSPF neighbor on 10.0.14.0/24 keeps dropping to Down
description: IronGate Freight reported that the Aurora AR-900 at their cross-dock site was flapping OSPF with the upstream switch every few seconds after a change window. The router is running 9.2.0, and the interface on the AR-900 is configured for 1500-byte MTU while the peer is advertising 1492 bytes. On-site checks showed the neighbor cycling between ExStart and Down, with the LSDB changing continuously and route convergence never completing. The event log also showed "%OSPF-4-ADJ-EXSTART" on each reset. TAC confirmed the pattern matches the known 9.2.0 adjacency issue on multiaccess segments with an MTU mismatch.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-2103 workaround during the maintenance window by configuring matching OSPF MTU handling on both peers, using `ip ospf mtu-ignore` on the affected interface while keeping the physical MTU unchanged. After the change, the adjacency reached Full and remained stable under load. The case was closed as a confirmed KB-2103 workaround on Aurora AR-900 9.2.0.

subject: nf-300 software verification failure on reboot
description: Sunset Power Authority escalated through the NOC after their Nimbus NF-300 on 5.0.8 would not complete an upgrade to 5.0.9. Operations reported that the image download finishes, but the appliance rolls back during boot and logs "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". TAC reviewed the target image details and confirmed the checksum matches the expected SHA-256 value, so the file is valid. The behavior is consistent with a verification issue in the loader, not a transport corruption problem.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-3104 and used the supported workaround: copy the image with SCP instead of HTTPS staging, then verify the image before rebooting. After the image was staged through SCP, the appliance booted cleanly and remained on the upgraded release after restart.

subject: Temporary tunnel degradation on 3.3 edge during LTE switchover
description: MetroLink Telecom opened this case through the portal for an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.3. They reported that some spoke tunnels briefly showed degraded status whenever the active LTE link changed, but only on one branch with two modems installed. TAC checked the edge and saw the control plane become heavily loaded during the handoff window, while application routing and the rest of the WAN remained healthy once the transition finished. The customer suspected a radio issue, but the pattern lined up with the switchover timer rather than signal quality. No lasting packet loss was observed after the event cleared.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as the 3.3 dual-modem LTE handoff issue documented in KB-5112. We applied the recommended workaround by setting interface lte0 handoff-debounce 5000 and committing the configuration. The branch no longer shows temporary overlay degradation during LTE switchover.

subject: HA pair on 5.1.5 is alternating roles and dropping sessions
description: Crescent Health Group submitted a portal report for a Nimbus NF-300 pair running 5.1.5. They described brief outages where traffic would move to the standby unit and then move back again, with no clear hardware failure and no persistent interface down condition. TAC’s initial review showed that both appliances were cabled to the same upstream switch, and the monitored interface shared the same broadcast domain as the heartbeat path. The behavior is consistent with a link-monitor event being triggered by a short Layer 2 forwarding disruption, which can happen even when the firewall hardware is healthy.
resolution: TAC resolved the case by referencing KB-3107 and applying the topology workaround. The customer re-homed the heartbeat links to a dedicated Layer 2 segment and increased the monitor interval to 10 seconds with `ha monitor-interval 10`, then `commit`. Once the shared-switch dependency was removed, the pair stopped oscillating and session interruptions ceased.

subject: reapply lte tunnel settings after upgrade on dual-sim edges
description: Prairie State College asked what to change after an upgrade because LTE tunnels and handoff behavior changed on dual-SIM edges. They are on Atlas SD-WAN 3.2 and saw some sites come back with different tunnel characteristics after migration. They also use custom APN profiles and want to know which LTE settings should be rechecked before returning sites to service.
resolution: TAC pointed them to GUIDE-AT and advised reapplying the LTE tunnel MTU after any 3.1 upgrade, since the upgrade may rewrite it to 1500. For most carrier LTE links, use a tunnel MTU between 1400 and 1420 bytes and validate the path with 1472-byte pings; on 3.2 systems with custom APN profiles, recheck each LTE interface because the per-interface tunnel MTU can be dropped during migration. Where applicable, set `interface lte0 tunnel-mtu 1400`, commit, and confirm tunnel state with `show sdwan tunnels`; for 3.3 dual-modem edges, also set `interface lte0 handoff-debounce 5000` to reduce CPU spikes during transient signal loss.

subject: HX-5000 25g port drops every few minutes
description: Summit Logistics called TAC about an HX-5000 core switch running 7.2 on a 25g server-facing port that kept dropping under steady traffic. The caller initially suspected a bad patch cable or an optics seating issue because the link would come back on its own after a short pause. I checked the interface history and transceiver data; the port showed a repeating pattern of loss of link every 8 to 12 minutes, with DOM bias current stepping up immediately before each flap. The optic was seated correctly and the far-end device was also reporting a brief loss of signal during each event.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-6101 for HX-5000 7.2 optics and advised upgrading the switch to 7.3, where the DOM sampling logic is corrected. After the upgrade, the port remained stable and the bias current readings no longer triggered link drops.

subject: Policy deployment blocked on Atlas 2.9 orchestrator
description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened a portal case saying that one site group could no longer receive configuration updates even though no visible network alarm was present. The Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator is version 2.9, and the edges continue to pass traffic over existing tunnels. TAC confirmed the policy job fails during orchestrator-side validation and never reaches the devices. The log line "%PKI-4-CRL-EXPIRED" appears at the time of failure, which points to a certificate revocation list timer expiring on the controller rather than a problem with the remote sites.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-5111 and completed the recommended upgrade path. The orchestrator was upgraded to 3.1, after which the certificate validator used the CRL nextUpdate field instead of a fixed 24-hour expiry. Policy pushes were retested and completed successfully.

subject: Change push fails after CRL ages out
description: TAC logged a phone call from HarborPoint Retail reporting that SD-WAN changes were failing on their Atlas orchestrator during routine operations. The system is running version 2.9, and the customer noted that tunnel status and application SLA metrics looked normal, which initially suggested a routing or transport issue. TAC observed that the failure occurs before the job is sent to any edge node, and the orchestrator log shows "%PKI-4-CRL-EXPIRED" during the preflight stage. That behavior matched a certificate validation problem rather than an edge configuration fault.
resolution: TAC identified KB-5111 and applied the documented workaround. We refreshed the CRL on the orchestrator with `certificate import crl revocation-list.pem` and committed the change so the policy engine would accept the next push. The customer was told to refresh the CRL before it reaches 24 hours old until the orchestrator can be upgraded.

subject: BGP prefixes inactive after static route replacement
description: HarborPoint Retail contacted TAC about intermittent loss of a small set of BGP-learned routes on an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3. Their network team replaced a static route to the same prefix during a maintenance window, and shortly after that some customer VLAN routes stopped appearing in the routing table. The BGP neighbor stayed up and route updates continued, which made the issue look non-deterministic at first. Our initial review showed the affected prefixes were all using the changed recursive next hop and the condition cleared only after the BGP table was refreshed.
resolution: TAC traced the symptom to KB-2107 and confirmed it matches the 9.2.3 next-hop recursion defect. We recommended upgrading the AR-900 to 9.3.0, where BGP is re-notified whenever a recursive static route changes attributes. After the upgrade, the customer repeated the static route change and the prefixes remained installed normally.

subject: Atlas SD-WAN policy push stuck on large route-map tenant
description: Partner escalation for Lakeside Hospitality on Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator 3.0. The customer reported that a policy change for a branch tenant stayed in processing for about 10 minutes and then never reached the edges. TAC checked the orchestrator policy worker and saw CPU pinned above 90 percent during the push; the affected tenant had a route-map with more than 256 entries. The edge devices were still running the previous policy, and `show sdwan tunnels` on a sample branch remained stable while the new route was absent.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-5103. Lakeside Hospitality upgraded the orchestrator from 3.0 to 3.1, which uses the fixed route-map serializer. After the upgrade, policy pushes completed normally and the tenant policy applied to the edges without delay.

subject: Recover BGP next-hop resolution after underlay route change
description: Sunset Power Authority asked how to recover BGP next-hop resolution after an underlay withdrawal or a recursive static route change on Aurora AR-900 9.3.0. They reported that the next hop can remain unresolved until the routing process is refreshed, and they wanted the least disruptive recovery method during maintenance. They also asked whether there is a preferred way to keep recursion stable when the underlay route is being replaced.
resolution: TAC pointed them to GUIDE-AR and advised using the least disruptive recovery method for the release in use. For 9.2.3, issue a soft clear of the affected BGP IPv4 unicast address family after changing recursive static routes; if a clear must be avoided, withdraw the old static route for at least 5 seconds before installing the replacement. If the next hop remains unresolved on 9.1.4 or 9.1.6, clear the BGP process for the affected IPv4 unicast address family, and avoid repeated soft clears during peak update periods because routing CPU can spike to 95% on 9.2.1.

subject: Atlas edge tunnels stuck negotiating after peer crypto change
description: CivicWorks Public Agency NOC escalated that a branch edge stopped bringing up its Internet IPSec tunnel after the remote security gateway was updated. The affected device is an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.2, and `show sdwan tunnels` shows the session cycling through negotiating instead of reaching established. TAC reviewed the edge logs and found repeated "%IKE-3-PROPOSAL-MISMATCH" events every 10 seconds during phase 2 negotiation. The customer initially suspected a circuit issue because traffic failed at the same time, but the WAN interface and routing table were stable.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as the 3.2 interoperability defect described in KB-5106. We applied the documented workaround by changing the remote side to accept an AES-GCM proposal without a separate integrity field, then committed the proposal and revalidated the tunnel. The IPSec SA established normally after the next retry interval.

subject: Frequent failover on NF-300 pair after switch changes
description: Lakeside Hospitality escalated through a partner about a Nimbus NF-300 HA deployment running 5.0.9. They reported that the firewalls were failing over several times an hour after a switch replacement, and the problem was first noticed as short VPN drops and brief access interruptions. TAC triage determined that the heartbeat and the interface being monitored were both connected through the same access switch, so a spanning-tree or forwarding event on that switch could affect both paths at once. Because the monitor timer on this platform is only 3 seconds by default, a single missed heartbeat and a missed poll can cause an unnecessary switchover.
resolution: TAC closed the issue as KB-3107 and applied the documented workaround. We advised the customer to place the heartbeat links on an independent Layer 2 segment and avoid sharing the monitored interface path with the same upstream switch; where immediate cabling changes were not possible, we set `ha monitor-interval 10` and committed the change. The pair stabilized after the topology was corrected.

subject: Stabilize an oscillating switch stack
description: IronGate Freight asked what should be changed on HX-5000 when a stack is oscillating or briefly separating between members on release 7.4. They reported intermittent master changes and short stack adjacencies loss during normal operation. TAC treated this as a how-to question and checked the documented stack stability recommendations for the platform.
