resolution: TAC pointed the customer to GUIDE-HX and summarized the stack-stability guidance: pin the desired master by setting a higher priority on the preferred member, avoid adding or removing members during the unstable period, and keep control-plane load below 60 percent until the software is upgraded. The guide also notes that on 7.3 matched-length stack cables reduce master election oscillation, and on 7.6 stack cabling should be kept under 1 m where possible without chaining all members through a single long physical path. Example commands: configure terminal; stack member 1 priority 200; stack member 2 priority 100; stack heartbeat timeout 900; show stack.

subject: HTTPS flows not decrypted during peak hours on 5.2.0
description: MetroLink Telecom opened the case after a rise in encrypted web traffic caused some HTTPS sessions to pass through the NF-300 without decryption. The firewall is running 5.2.0, and the SOC reported that users sometimes saw the remote site certificate instead of the expected forged inspection certificate. TAC confirmed that the issue was intermittent and more likely after 5 to 10 minutes of sustained SSL inspection load, with cache evictions increasing above the normal baseline. The customer also provided the following log entry from the affected period: `%SSL-5-CERT_CHAIN_CACHE`.
resolution: TAC correlated the symptoms and log activity with KB-3106, which describes a configuration-sensitive outbound TLS bypass on 5.2.0. We applied the supported workaround by increasing the certificate cache size to reduce eviction pressure, then committed the change and verified that new HTTPS sessions were again being decrypted.

subject: OW-20 standby sync stalls after redundancy failover
description: Partner escalation for Cornerstone Supermarkets on an Orion OW-20 controller running 4.8. The customer reported that after an active-standby switchover, several SSIDs prompted for 802.1X again and some clients stayed offline for about a minute before recovering. TAC reviewed the redundancy state and saw `sync state: partial` on the standby; the event log also repeated `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL` every 10 seconds. `show configuration database summary` showed the configuration database had grown beyond 32,768 rows, which matched the stall condition.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-4104 workaround by pruning unused AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts to reduce the configuration database below 30,000 rows. After the cleanup, `redundancy force-resync` completed successfully and `show redundancy status` returned a healthy sync state. The case was closed with the customer advised to keep the database below the stated threshold until the controller can be upgraded.

subject: Inter-site VPN will not establish on Atlas 3.2 edge
description: Redwood University opened the case after a campus edge could no longer build its VPN to a partner site. The affected Atlas SD-WAN edge is on 3.2, and the tunnel state remained in negotiating even though the peer was reachable and basic connectivity tests passed. TAC checked `show sdwan tunnels` and confirmed the peer kept rejecting the transform set during negotiation. The customer did not report any packet loss on the underlay, so this was not consistent with a transport outage.
resolution: TAC confirmed the behavior matched KB-5106 for Atlas SD-WAN 3.2. Since the peer policy required a combined ESP proposal that the edge could not satisfy in this release, the customer was advised to upgrade the edge to 3.3. After the upgrade, the tunnel negotiated successfully without further changes.

subject: Tune DOM monitoring for flapping SFP28 ports
description: HarborPoint Retail asked how to tune optics and DOM monitoring on HX-5000 ports that are showing link drops and occasional LOS alarms on release 7.2. The affected SFP28 interfaces report rising bias current and intermittent remote LOS events under load. TAC reviewed the symptoms and confirmed the customer was looking for the recommended monitoring interval and optics handling guidance for this release.
resolution: TAC pointed the customer to GUIDE-HX and advised lowering DOM polling on the affected SFP28 ports by setting the transceiver monitoring interval to 120 seconds. TAC also recommended keeping optics below 50 C case temperature where possible, especially on ports showing bias current spikes or remote LOS alarms. If the port continues to flap under load, the guide recommends moving the optic to a later-release port or replacing the module with one that has a stable bias current profile. Example commands: configure terminal; interface ethernet 1/1; transceiver monitoring interval 120; show interfaces transceiver detail.

subject: HX-5000 stack briefly separates on 7.6 with 2 m cables
description: Prairie State College called TAC to report that one member of their Helix HX-5000 core stack on 7.6 would vanish from the stack view for a few seconds and then come back without any service impact. The caller thought the chassis might be rebooting, but the power and interface status stayed normal throughout the event. TAC checked the stack state and found a short split-brain condition on a long cable path, with no evidence of link failure. The issue was reproducible under load when the stack heartbeat timing slipped.
resolution: TAC mapped the symptoms to KB-6104 and applied the recommended workaround from configuration mode. We set `stack heartbeat timeout 900` and recommended that the customer avoid chaining all members through a single long path when possible. The stack remained stable after the change.

subject: site-to-site vpn drops during esp rekey on 5.0.9 firewall
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets escalated through the NOC after users on one branch link reported brief application hangs every few hours. The affected device is a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9, and the branch tunnel was described as 'up but not moving packets' during the event. TAC found that `show crypto ikev2 sa` kept the IKE SA in ESTABLISHED while the child SA was being recreated, and the event log showed `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH`. Because the outage was short and self-clearing, the initial suspicion from the NOC was a WAN flap, but the pattern matched a rekey negotiation failure instead.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3101 and applied the supported workaround. The customer was told to leave the PFS group unchanged, disable child SA rekey on the Nimbus NF-300 using `config`, `crypto ikev2 child-sa rekey disable`, and `commit`, then perform a manual tunnel restart during a maintenance window. After the restart, the branch tunnel stopped blackholing traffic during rekey and the NOC closed the incident.

subject: HX-5000 routing CPU and memory climbing after EVPN updates
description: Lakeside Hospitality opened this as an on-site field engineer case on a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6. They reported that the routing process memory keeps climbing during the day, and the box becomes sluggish when the fabric receives a burst of EVPN updates from remote sites. TAC reviewed `show process memory` and confirmed the routing daemon RSS had grown from roughly 920 MB to 1.7 GB over 18 hours, with free memory trending below 13 percent. The system log also showed "%MEM-4-LEAK" during the same window. The customer initially suspected a stacking issue, but stack status and control-plane counters were otherwise stable.
resolution: TAC identified this as the 7.6 EVPN refresh memory leak described in KB-6112. The customer upgraded the HX-5000 from 7.6 to 8.0, and post-upgrade memory usage stabilized with no further growth during EVPN route-refresh activity. TAC advised continued monitoring of free memory and verification with `show process memory` after maintenance windows.

subject: 802.1X auth timing out on wireless SSID after RADIUS challenge
description: On-site field engineer report for Summit Logistics: handheld scanners on Orion OW-20 version 4.9 were timing out during wireless sign-on several times per hour. The engineer noted that the first EAP exchange succeeded, but clients then remained in authenticating for about 20 seconds before failing over to a different AP. TAC review of the controller logs showed '%RADIUS-4-ATTR_DROP' during Access-Challenge handling, and the issue only appeared when the upstream server returned a larger attribute set. This pointed away from RF coverage and toward the RADIUS reply contents.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-4107 and applied the documented workaround. We instructed the customer to move the Vendor-Specific attribute earlier in the RADIUS response order and, where possible, reduce the challenge to 12 or fewer attributes. After the server-side change, authentication completed successfully on the existing OW-20 4.9 deployment.

subject: P1 escalation: HX-5000 cannot complete software upgrade past 80%
description: Redwood University submitted a portal case for an HX-5000 core switch running 7.2 after a scheduled upgrade window failed. The upgrade would advance into the low 80% range, pause, and then the management plane would restart before the unit rolled back to the previous image. The operations team believed the image file was corrupt, but TAC saw that the failure was repeatable on the same chassis and that the system had a large number of active optics. The upgrade logs contained "ERR-UPG-2207" at the migration step, which aligned with the rollback timing.
resolution: TAC associated the case with KB-6111 and recommended the standard workaround for affected 7.2 systems. The customer cleared legacy transceiver calibration history, saved the configuration, and reloaded the switch before rescheduling the upgrade in a maintenance window. The next upgrade attempt completed successfully.

subject: Intermittent site-to-site VPN resets on NF-300
description: Summit Logistics submitted this case through the customer portal after a branch-to-datacenter VPN started resetting every 45 minutes. They reported that the tunnel came back quickly, but any active file transfer or remote session was interrupted. The Nimbus NF-300 is running 5.1.3. TAC checked the IKEv2 state table and saw the child SA lifetimes change from one rekey to the next, and the firewall log included `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH` at the moment the peer attempted to rekey with an alternate acceptable transform.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3102 and implemented the documented workaround. A single DH group, group 14, was pinned on both peers using `crypto ikev2 proposal default dh-group 14`, followed by `commit`. After that change, the branch tunnel remained up through subsequent rekeys.

subject: Repeated BGP soft clears overload routing process on 9.2.1
description: IronGate Freight called the NOC with a P2 escalation after the Aurora AR-900 at one of their sites started lagging during BGP maintenance. The router is running 9.2.1, and the issue appeared only after several `clear bgp ipv4 unicast 65001 soft` operations were performed back to back on a busy table. TAC observed that `show process cpu` showed the routing task consuming most of the scheduler slice for about a minute, while packet forwarding remained mostly intact. The customer did not report link loss, but route convergence was noticeably delayed.
resolution: TAC referenced KB-2110 and advised the customer to upgrade the Aurora AR-900 to 9.2.3, which fixes the refresh path so it reuses prefix state instead of rebuilding the outbound queue on every soft clear. After the upgrade, the customer repeated the maintenance sequence in a lab window and no longer saw the CPU spike. The unit returned to normal convergence behavior under load.

subject: Wireless APs hang in joining on OW-20 running 4.8
description: BlueRiver Credit Union called about new APs that would not come online on an Orion OW-20 running 4.8. The customer described it as a power or cabling issue, but TAC review showed the controller was reachable, APs stayed in joining for 2-4 minutes, and then the CAPWAP session reset before authorization. `show ap summary` showed the join pending count increasing, and the join retry counter behaved the same way across multiple APs, which pointed away from a single hardware fault. Initial triage confirmed the issue was tied to the controller software rather than the APs themselves.
resolution: TAC associated the symptoms with KB-4103 and recommended upgrading the OW-20 from 4.8 to 4.9. The customer completed the upgrade, which corrected the join path so delayed capability responses are processed against the active session. APs then registered successfully and the join pending backlog cleared.

subject: 3.3 report generation slows the management plane
description: CivicWorks Public Agency reported that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator was still reachable, but report generation had become slow enough to interfere with routine admin work. The on-site engineer initially thought the issue might be tied to a certificate renewal task, but the timing lined up with scheduled reporting and not with any certificate or edge event. TAC checked the orchestrator version and confirmed it was 3.3, with the reporting service running hot while jobs processed a large flow-history set. No tunnel or policy fault was found on the edges. The orchestrator log showed '%ERR-ORCH-5178' during the report window.
resolution: TAC treated this as KB-5107 and applied the supported workaround. We changed flow-history retention to 5 days using `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed it, which reduced report size and brought the management-plane load back to normal.

subject: HX-5000 member flapping in stack view on 7.6
description: Northstar Bank emailed TAC about a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6 where one stack member would disappear and reappear in the management output several times a week. They described it as a possible hardware fault because the cabinet and cabling were unchanged. TAC reviewed the event pattern and confirmed the physical links never dropped, while the stack adjacency briefly reset and then recovered automatically. The behavior is consistent with a known heartbeat timing sensitivity on this release.
resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-6104 and implemented the documented workaround on the 7.6 stack. We applied `stack heartbeat timeout 900` and advised the bank to keep stack cables as short as practical. After the setting change, the stack no longer showed transient member loss.

subject: OW-20 restore came back without last wireless edits
description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed TAC about an Orion OW-20 running 5.1. Their message said a scheduled backup restored successfully, but the newest WLAN change was missing and the controller looked like it had been rolled back by a few minutes. TAC saw that the backup was triggered immediately after a batch of wireless edits, while the configuration database was still processing pending commits. The event log included "%ERR-DB-1809: backup snapshot taken with non-empty commit queue; pending WLAN edits omitted". This matched the reported symptom of a clean restore with incomplete recent WLAN changes.
resolution: TAC handled the issue per KB-4112 and advised the agency to back up only after the commit queue drains to zero. We recommended checking `show configuration database summary`, running `commit` for any staged WLAN edits, and waiting at least 30 seconds after the last change before `backup configuration`.

subject: Brief WAN instability on 3.3 edge when LTE carrier changes
description: HarborPoint Retail submitted this through the customer portal for an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.3. The report said the branch goes 'offline for a minute' whenever the backup LTE link takes over, but wired internet stayed up and the failure was not constant. TAC checked the edge and confirmed both LTE modems were enabled, with the overlay remaining healthy between events and only a short control-plane delay during failover. The customer also noted the problem seemed worse after configuration changes were pushed from the orchestrator. No evidence pointed to certificate expiry, underlay loss, or tunnel MTU mismatch.
resolution: TAC associated the issue with KB-5112 and confirmed the behavior is expected from the 3.3 dual-modem LTE handoff problem. We applied the published workaround by raising the LTE handoff debounce to 5000 ms on the edge and recommended avoiding policy refreshes during carrier switchover periods. After the change, failover no longer produced the brief overlay degradation.

subject: Atlas SD-WAN 2.8 edge lost connectivity after cert rotation
description: Evergreen Clinic Network submitted a portal case for a clinic edge that dropped from the orchestrator after a certificate rotation. The affected device is ECN-CLINIC-03 running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and the disconnect showed up in the UI within about 6 minutes. The customer initially suspected an LTE outage, but transport health and tunnels remained up on the edge. TAC confirmed the registration failure was caused by a stale trust bundle on the orchestrator that no longer matched the renewed certificate chain.
resolution: TAC treated this as KB-5102 and applied the documented workaround, then had the customer upgrade the orchestrator to 2.9. The full certificate chain was reimported on the orchestrator before the next renewal, and the site was brought back into service. After the upgrade, subsequent renewals refreshed the intermediate chain automatically.

subject: policy-based vpn comes up but no traffic on nf-300 5.1.5
description: IronGate Freight called TAC about a site-to-site VPN on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.1.5. They said the tunnel shows as established, but traffic across the link stays at zero and the remote peer keeps renegotiating roughly every 10 seconds. Initial triage confirmed the IKE SA forms, while the child SA never finishes installing when the local selector is configured as a host route. When the selector was widened during the call, the tunnel behavior changed and traffic began to pass.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-3108, a selector limitation affecting policy-based IKEv2 tunnels when the local selector is narrower than /30. We applied the documented workaround by disabling policy-based VPN and moving the service to a route-based design with firewall policy filtering. The customer confirmed the tunnel stabilized and counters started incrementing after the change.

subject: Multiple roaming pauses on Orion OW-20 5.0 during store walk tests
description: HarborPoint Retail emailed TAC after noticing repeated voice dropouts during walk tests in several stores. The Orion OW-20 wireless LAN controller is running 5.0, and the reported issue became worse when many associates were moving at once for opening checks. TAC observed successful reassociation events followed by the log entry '%ROAM-5-FT_KEYTIMEOUT' on affected clients, and `show client detail <mac>` showed `ft fallback: yes` on devices expected to remain on fast transition. The evidence pointed to a controller timing defect rather than a coverage or authentication problem.
resolution: TAC matched the case to KB-4106. HarborPoint Retail upgraded the Orion OW-20 from 5.0 to 5.1, which fixes the FT key push timing issue and removes the roaming-related service gaps.

subject: Intermittent HA switchover on NF-300 cluster, 5.2.0
description: Crescent Health Group called from the datacenter floor about a Nimbus NF-300 HA pair running 5.2.0. The field engineer said the standby unit was taking over every few minutes and then returning to standby without any hardware alarms. TAC checked the behavior against the reported switch layout and found that both the heartbeat traffic and the monitored interface were terminating on the same upstream access switch. The event log included '%HA-3-LINK_MONITOR_FLAP', which aligned with the repeated role changes and indicated a shared L2 disturbance rather than a fault in the firewall itself.
resolution: TAC treated this as KB-3107 and applied the documented workaround. The customer moved the heartbeat links to a separate Layer 2 segment and kept the two nodes on independent switch paths; we also set `ha monitor-interval 10` and committed the change to reduce sensitivity to brief L2 interruptions. After the update, `show ha status` remained stable and the failovers stopped.

subject: Intermittent roam gaps on 5.0 controller
description: An on-site field engineer at Evergreen Clinic Network reported brief audio gaps on a few clinical handhelds during room-to-room movement. The Orion OW-20 controller is running 5.0, and the engineer initially suspected RF coverage because the clients were still reconnecting successfully. TAC checked roaming behavior and found the fast transition path was being completed, but some clients were falling back after reassociation and showing `ft fallback: yes` in client detail output. The issue was reproducible only when several devices moved in a short window, which pointed to a controller-side timing problem.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-4106 and applied the documented workaround. The site reduced roam burst size with `roam batch-size 8` and staggered mobility tests so FT key pushes completed within the completion window on the 5.0 controller.

subject: APs drop offline for minutes on OW-20 controller
description: Evergreen Clinic Network opened a portal case for an Orion OW-20 running 4.7. They described APs that would join, vanish, and then come back later without any changes at the switch ports or cabling. Initial triage showed the issue was limited to a subset of APs, not the whole site, and `show ap detail <name>` indicated that the affected APs were only updating `last-seen` after a much longer delay. That pointed away from a general controller outage and toward the join process itself.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-4102 workaround by reducing the AP join retry interval from 5 seconds to 2 seconds using `ap join retry-interval 2`. This kept the join transaction active long enough for the capability revalidation step to complete. The APs then joined successfully without waiting for the next discovery window.

subject: Repeated trap loss from interface bouncing on AR-900 9.1.4
description: CivicWorks Public Agency reported from the site that their Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4 was dropping some interface traps during a brief physical-layer fault on several user-facing ports. The on-site field engineer observed that the monitoring system received the first few link changes but then began missing later notifications while polling still reported the correct state. In the router log, TAC found "ERR-SNMP-3019" coincident with the burst of link transitions. The symptom pattern matched trap loss under heavy event load rather than a general SNMP failure.
resolution: TAC resolved the case using KB-2109, which documents the AR-900 trap queue overflow behavior. We applied the recommended workaround by configuring 500 ms link debounce on the affected Ethernet interfaces to suppress the storm and advised the customer to keep polling as the source of record for interface state. The customer remained on 9.1.4; no software fix was needed.

subject: LTE site on 3.2 loses preconfigured tunnel MTU after migration
description: MetroLink Telecom reported that a field-deployed branch edge running Atlas SD-WAN 3.2 would establish its LTE overlay but then mis-handle larger traffic after a software change. The site uses a custom APN, and the customer initially suspected a carrier issue because the tunnel status remained up. TAC reviewed the edge configuration and confirmed the interface object existed without the expected tunnel MTU override after the upgrade. No log excerpt was provided, but the behavior aligned with a known migration defect affecting 3.2.
resolution: TAC determined the issue matched KB-5110 and had the customer upgrade the branch to 3.3. After the upgrade, the LTE tunnel MTU was preserved for the custom APN interface and the overlay handled normal payload sizes without fragmentation.

subject: Uneven session-table load on 5.2.0 firewall
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets reported that their Nimbus NF-300 on 5.2.0 was slowing down during peak store traffic, but only for a subset of customer-facing flows. Their portal note mentioned that reloading policy briefly helped, then the problem returned after more sessions built up. TAC checked the system logs and confirmed the message "%SESSION-4-HASH_SKEW" while the session-table summary showed one hot shard at 88 percent occupancy and the rest well under 40 percent. The pattern was consistent with asymmetric routing enabled on traffic sourced from the same address blocks.
resolution: TAC followed KB-3110 and disabled asymmetric routing handling for the affected policy set using config mode, then committed the change. That redistributed new sessions across the shards and cleared the imbalance without requiring an upgrade.

subject: Intermittent 100g fiber flap on HX-5000 7.5
description: Lakeside Hospitality opened a P2 for an HX-5000 core switch on software 7.5. They were seeing an uplink flap on a QSFP28-based 100G port, usually after a temperature or voltage warning cleared on the optic. TAC checked the transceiver counters and found the module itself was recovering cleanly, but the port state was still being withdrawn for several seconds. The behavior matched a software-triggered link-state event rather than a persistent physical layer fault.
resolution: TAC confirmed the issue against KB-6102 and recommended upgrading the switch from 7.5 to 7.6. The customer completed the upgrade and retested the uplink, which no longer exhibited the brief down/up cycle after DOM alarms cleared. TAC closed the case after post-upgrade verification.

subject: Repeated uplink withdraws on HX-5000 after optic alarm clears
description: Redwood University escalated a campus network outage from the NOC involving an HX-5000 core switch on 7.5. They reported that a 100G uplink on QSFP28 optics was briefly going down and coming back after a transceiver temperature alert cleared, which was disrupting a bundled service path. TAC inspected the interface state and saw the optic recover normally, but the link state dropped for several seconds anyway. The event was reproducible on the same port and did not correlate with spanning-tree or LACP changes.
resolution: TAC traced the behavior to KB-6102 and implemented the workaround on the impacted interface to suppress aggressive DOM alarm action. After the change, the uplink remained stable through subsequent temperature and voltage alarm clear events. The customer was advised to continue operation on 7.5 until a maintenance window allowed an upgrade.

subject: SLA class stays down too long after a single timeout
description: HarborPoint Retail escalated from the NOC after store traffic was repeatedly steered off the preferred LTE link during brief evening congestion. The impacted edge is atlas-edge-08 running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and the operator initially suspected a carrier outage because the tunnel state was briefly degraded. TAC reviewed the device output and saw `show app-route sla-class` report the class down for 10 to 20 seconds after one missed probe, even though later samples stayed within threshold. The event log contained "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN" when the class changed state.
resolution: TAC linked the case to KB-5101 and recommended upgrading the edge to 2.9, which corrects the SLA evaluator behavior. HarborPoint Retail completed the upgrade on atlas-edge-08 and retested the same brownout condition. After the upgrade, the class no longer dropped on a single lost probe and active flows remained on the preferred path.

subject: HX-5000 free memory drops during EVPN churn
description: Summit Logistics opened the case through an on-site field engineer on a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6. The engineer reported that the switch stayed up, but management access became slow after several hours and free memory was trending down during EVPN churn. TAC checked the device and confirmed steady growth in the routing process memory footprint, from around 940 MB to 1.6 GB, with no corresponding increase in traffic load. The issue was isolated to the routing daemon, and the rest of the system looked normal. No log excerpt was provided by the customer, and TAC did not need one to identify the pattern.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-6112 and confirmed it was the 7.6 EVPN refresh memory leak. Because the fabric was stable, TAC applied the workaround from KB-6112: reduce unnecessary neighbor resets, keep EVPN adjacency changes out of peak traffic windows, and schedule a reload before free memory falls below 15 percent. The customer implemented the workaround and continued monitoring the routing process until a maintenance upgrade can be planned.

subject: Wireless 802.1X stalls on OW-20 4.9 when external RADIUS is used
description: Partner escalation on behalf of Sunset Power Authority: employees reported that wireless login worked for some devices but failed randomly for others on Orion OW-20 controllers running 4.9. The customer initially suspected a certificate issue because the failure occurred after entering credentials, but the controller was consistently completing the initial request and then stalling on the next challenge. TAC examined the event log and found '%RADIUS-4-ATTR_DROP' tied to Access-Challenge repacking, which correlated with sessions that carried tunneled policy attributes. The failures were reproducible only when the challenge contained a larger attribute list from the external RADIUS server.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-4107 and applied the workaround from the article. The RADIUS policy was adjusted so the Vendor-Specific attribute was sent before the 12th position in the reply, avoiding the controller's attribute drop condition. Once that change was made, client authentication on OW-20 4.9 completed without further timeouts.

subject: Critical upgrade rollback on AR-900 9.1.6 with BGP downtime
description: BlueRiver Credit Union emailed TAC about an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.6 that could not complete an in-service upgrade to 9.2.0. Their note said the unit "half-upgraded" and then reverted, leaving branch routing interrupted until BGP reestablished. TAC reviewed the upgrade output and observed the quoted message "ERR-UPG-1307" at the point where the installer tried to migrate session state. The router had BGP add-path configured on a neighbor, and the device was advertising more than 1,000 paths, which matched the known failure conditions.
resolution: TAC advised the customer to move to 9.2.1, per KB-2111, because that release includes the corrected migrator. The customer performed the upgrade from 9.1.6 to 9.2.1 and the process completed without rollback. After boot, the AR-900 returned to service with BGP stable and no further upgrade errors.

subject: Guest voice users hear brief gaps during AP roaming
description: Lakeside Hospitality called in after guests reported short audio gaps on voice handsets while walking between lobby and meeting-room APs. The wireless controller is an Orion OW-20 running 4.9, and the issue only appears on SSIDs with 802.11r enabled. `show client detail <mac>` shows the client reassociating successfully, but traffic resumes late enough for users to notice the interruption. The controller logs include "%ROAM-5-FT_KEYTIMEOUT" during the roam events.
resolution: TAC tied the report to KB-4105 and applied the workaround from the article. We changed the accounting interval to 60 seconds with `wlan corp accounting interval 60` and advised the customer to reduce controller CPU load during roaming tests. For the voice SSID, TAC also noted that disabling 802.11r is an acceptable temporary measure until maintenance.

subject: AR-900 reports NAT exhaustion during short-lived traffic bursts
description: BlueRiver Credit Union escalated through a partner after their Aurora AR-900 on 9.3.0 started rejecting new outbound sessions during end-of-day file transfers. They reported that `show nat translations` showed only a few dozen active mappings, yet users saw intermittent connection failures for 2-4 minutes after a burst of short-lived HTTPS and VPN flows. TAC reviewed the router logs and confirmed repeated `%NAT-3-ALLOCFAIL` events with the message `ERR-NAT-4108`. Initial triage also showed the issue was reproducible only under heavy session churn, not during steady-state traffic.
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as KB-2108, which matches a 9.3.0 dynamic NAT port exhaustion report caused by deferred port return. We applied the documented workaround by expanding the NAT pool to add additional public address capacity and adjusted the NAT translation timeout to 240 seconds. After the change, new sessions completed normally and the customer continued monitoring NAT headroom during peak windows.

subject: lte tunnel traffic drops after 3.1 upgrade on branch edge
description: Customer reported that after upgrading a dual-SIM Atlas SD-WAN edge to 3.1, voice traffic and larger file transfers started failing over the LTE path while the tunnel still showed up in the orchestrator. The site is using edge 198.51.100.24 on release 3.1, and the issue appears only on the LTE-backed overlay; wired failover is unaffected. Initial triage found `show sdwan tunnels` reporting the tunnel as up, but packet loss begins once payloads exceed about 1420 bytes, and the customer described intermittent fragmentation alerts in the portal. The customer had previously configured a lower LTE tunnel MTU before the upgrade.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-5104. We had the customer reapply the LTE tunnel MTU on the affected interface with `interface lte0 tunnel-mtu 1400` followed by `commit`, then retested with 1472-byte pings. The tunnel resumed passing traffic normally and the site was returned to service.

subject: AR-900 losing IPv6 addresses on access VLAN after RA filtering
description: IronGate Freight NOC opened this after several warehouse scanners on the access VLAN began dropping IPv6 connectivity during a maintenance window. The affected device is an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3, and the router still shows the delegated prefix in configuration while clients lose their global IPv6 address roughly 3 minutes after the last upstream advertisement is filtered. TAC reviewed the event log and found repeated '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' messages at the time the clients stopped renewing their addresses. Initial checks showed the prefix valid lifetime was configured for 7200 seconds, so the observed behavior did not match the configured timer.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-2104, where RA suppression on the active user VLAN causes SLAAC prefix state to age out on the 3-minute hold timer rather than the configured lifetime. We advised the customer not to suppress router advertisements on the production VLAN and to move the segment to DHCPv6 stateful addressing if suppression must remain in place. The team applied the documented workaround and confirmed new hosts retained IPv6 connectivity after the change.

subject: SLA probe flaps on 2.9 edge during peak uploads
description: Crescent Health Group called in after seeing intermittent path changes on one Atlas SD-WAN edge used for clinic voice and remote charting. The appliance is running version 2.9, and the customer initially suspected a WAN provider issue because the link stayed physically up while sessions moved off the preferred path. On triage, TAC checked `show sdwan tunnels` and confirmed that the tunnel health was dropping only during sustained upload bursts, not during idle periods. The edge log included "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN", which aligned with the timing of the application steering events.
resolution: TAC identified the problem as KB-5105 and advised that the defect is fixed in 3.0. The customer upgraded the edge fleet from 2.9 to 3.0 after a maintenance window, then repeated the same traffic test. Post-upgrade, SLA probes were sent on the dedicated control queue and the tunnels no longer oscillated between up and degraded.

subject: hx-5000 100g uplink drops during peak class changes
description: Prairie State College opened this case through the customer portal after reporting intermittent packet loss on the campus core during class changes. The affected device is a Helix HX-5000 running 7.2, with two 100G uplinks carrying aggregated wireless and voice traffic. TAC reviewed `show queue counters` and found tail drops increasing steadily on the oversubscribed egress queues, while average interface utilization stayed in the 70 to 80 percent range. The customer initially suspected a transceiver issue, but the optics and error counters were clean and the loss pattern matched bursty congestion rather than hardware failure.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-6109 and applied the documented workaround. Prairie State College moved part of the workload to a second uplink and reduced burstiness upstream so no single 100G egress port remained above the 85 percent sustained threshold. For the latency-sensitive voice VLAN, TAC also placed traffic into a dedicated queue on the affected interface.

subject: APs stuck joining after controller upgrade to 4.8
description: Pinnacle Energy called in after several APs remained in joining state on an Orion OW-20 running 4.8. The report came in as intermittent wireless loss at first, but `show ap summary` showed a rising `join pending` count and the same APs cycling through join retries before resetting their CAPWAP sessions. Triage on the controller matched the event pattern for delayed capability exchange, and the log buffer included "%ERR-APJ-4417" when the second exchange arrived late. The issue was most visible on the remote site link, which was running around 80 ms RTT with brief retransmit bursts during registration.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-4103 and applied the documented workaround on the OW-20: `ap join timeout 180` and verification that uplink loss stayed below 0.5% during joins. After extending the timeout, the APs completed registration and moved to authorized. The customer was advised to keep new APs staged locally until the branch link is stable enough for initial join.

subject: 5.0 upgrade fails after reboot on OW-20
description: Evergreen Clinic Network reported that their Orion OW-20 on 4.6 would not stay on 5.0 after a planned maintenance window. The unit rebooted, came back with the new image briefly active, and then reverted to the prior image after several minutes. TAC confirmed the failure happened during post-upgrade database migration and that the configuration database contained a large number of older guest portal ACL objects. No alternate faults were found in AP join or redundancy logs.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-4111 by having the customer boot the previous image, remove unused legacy guest portal ACL objects, and re-export the configuration for review. The upgrade was then retried and completed normally on 5.0.

subject: 25g optics flapping on hx-5000, fixed after os update
description: Prairie State College opened an escalation through their partner for an HX-5000 running 7.2 with one 25g access port flapping repeatedly. Their notes said the remote side kept showing a brief optical alarm, and the switch log repeatedly showed "%TRANSCEIVER-4-LOS" before each outage. They did not have a clear local cause and wanted the switch replaced. TAC review of the transceiver counters showed a recurrent bias current spike immediately before each outage, and the module remained present and powered throughout the event. The symptoms aligned with an optics-path defect rather than a failing port ASIC.
resolution: TAC associated the case with KB-6101 and advised upgrading the HX-5000 from 7.2 to 7.3. After the upgrade, the DOM snapshot handling no longer latched the false low-power state, and the link remained up under load.

subject: Redundancy sync stall on OW-20 after config growth
description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed the TAC mailbox about an Orion OW-20 on 4.8 that was still serving clients, but every planned failover caused a short outage and forced some users back through login. Their note suggested a possible RF issue, but TAC saw the symptom only during redundancy events and not during normal operation. The controller reported `sync state: partial`, and the log repeatedly contained `%REDUNDANCY-4-SYNC_STALL`. `show configuration database summary` showed the configuration database had grown beyond 32,768 rows, which fits the known stall condition on this release.
resolution: TAC applied the KB-4104 workaround by deleting obsolete AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts until the configuration database was below 30,000 rows. A manual `redundancy force-resync` then completed without errors, and the standby matched the active configuration. The agency was advised to keep the database below the threshold until a future maintenance window allows for remediation planning.

subject: prepare configuration database for redundancy on 4.8
description: CivicWorks Public Agency asked what should be changed before enabling controller redundancy when the configuration database is large. They are planning active-standby operation and want to avoid sync stalls or a failed initial resync during the switchover window. They asked for the recommended cleanup steps and whether a manual resync is appropriate after pruning the database.
resolution: TAC pointed them to GUIDE-OW and summarized the redundancy prerequisites. Keep the configuration database below 30,000 rows before enabling redundancy to avoid sync stalls at the 32,768-row threshold, and remove unused AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts before enabling active-standby operation. If immediate failover is required after a large configuration change, schedule a full config resync during a maintenance window, and use redundancy force-resync only after confirming the database has been reduced and the commit queue is clear. Confirm status with show redundancy status and show configuration database summary, then review show logging last 50 if resync activity is not completing.

subject: AR-900 9.1.6 to 9.2.0 fails during install; add-path migration error
description: Pinnacle Energy escalated through a partner after repeated failures upgrading an Aurora AR-900 from 9.1.6 to 9.2.0. The partner reported that the installer staged the image, then aborted and reverted to the prior release; the router was briefly unavailable to BGP peers during rollback. TAC confirmed the device was on 9.1.6 and saw the quoted log entry "ERR-UPG-1307" associated with the add-path migration step. Configuration review showed add-path send active on one neighbor, and the routing table contained more than 1,000 advertised paths at the time of upgrade.
resolution: TAC mapped the behavior to KB-2111 and advised moving the appliance to 9.2.1, which contains the fix for add-path migration during upgrade. The customer upgraded the AR-900 directly to 9.2.1 and the install completed successfully. After the upgrade, BGP came back without further intervention and add-path remained configured.

subject: microburst drops on 100g uplink after traffic shift
description: Pinnacle Energy’s partner opened the case on behalf of the customer after users reported brief stalls on storage and backup traffic crossing the core. The device is a Helix HX-5000 running 7.2, and the issue only appeared during large copy windows when utilization stayed near 75 percent but bursts were much higher. TAC checked interface and queue statistics and saw the output queue filling faster than the scheduler could drain it, with tail drops rising in the affected class. The partner also provided a switch log that included '%BUF-3-OVERFLOW' during the busiest interval, which aligned with the burst-loss pattern on the 100G egress path.
resolution: TAC identified the event as KB-6109 and applied the documented workaround. Pinnacle Energy reduced burstiness with upstream shaping, spread storage traffic across additional uplinks, and reserved a dedicated queue on the affected interface for the most sensitive flows. After the changes, queue drops stopped increasing and latency returned to expected levels.

subject: route-based vpn briefly drops traffic on nf-300 5.2.2
description: BlueRiver Credit Union opened this as a P2 after several remote branches reported 1 to 2 second pauses across a route-based IPsec tunnel. The affected appliance is a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2. Their NOC saw `show crypto ikev2 sa` stay ESTABLISHED during the event, but application traffic stalled and counters on the tunnel interface stopped incrementing for short periods. Initial triage shows the issue is repeatable only when both DPD and child-SA rekey are configured at 10 seconds on the same tunnel.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3112. We applied the documented workaround by changing the DPD timer so it no longer aligns with the rekey interval, using `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` under config mode and committing the change. After the timer change, the tunnel continued forwarding through multiple rekey cycles with no observed blackhole.

subject: AR-900 NAT failures after bursty traffic on 9.3.0
description: Redwood University worked with an on-site field engineer after their Aurora AR-900 on 9.3.0 started failing new NAT sessions during large virtual desktop login waves. The engineer initially suspected a firewall policy issue because only some sessions failed, but packet captures showed the router returning port allocation errors after bursts of short-lived connections. TAC reviewed the device state and confirmed `show nat translations` displayed far fewer active entries than the pool should have supported. The system log included `ERR-NAT-4108`, which matched the timing of the customer impact.
resolution: TAC traced the behavior to KB-2108, where 9.3.0 defers freed NAT ports until the 240-second aging cycle completes. We applied the documented workaround by expanding the NAT pool with more public address capacity and keeping the translation timeout at 240 seconds. The immediate result was that new sessions were admitted normally after bursts, and the field engineer validated the fix during the next login window.

subject: ikev2 tunnel up but traffic stalls on nf-300
description: IronGate Freight reported a route-based IPsec tunnel on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 where traffic would freeze briefly while the tunnel itself remained established. During TAC review, the customer mentioned the problem happens more often after a few minutes of stable operation and only on one tunnel with aggressive keepalive settings. We confirmed the firewall is not resetting the SA and the packet loss window is short, on the order of 1 to 2 seconds. Sample logs from the affected unit showed `%IKEV2-4-REKEY_TIMER` at the time of the event.
resolution: This matched KB-3112. TAC applied the workaround by making the DPD interval non-aligned with the rekey interval, using `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committing the configuration. After the change, the tunnel no longer exhibited the brief blackhole during DPD and rekey overlap.

subject: Outbound HTTPS occasionally bypasses SSL inspection on NF-300
description: Summit Logistics reported that some outbound HTTPS sites were intermittently loading with the origin server certificate instead of the inspection certificate on an NF-300 running 5.2.0. The issue was first noticed after the firewall had been up for several days, and it seemed to affect only a subset of web sessions while most traffic continued to decrypt normally. TAC reviewed the SSL inspection counters and saw certificate cache evictions rising steadily during the affected window, which matched the customer's observation that the behavior became more frequent during business hours. The bypass appears tied to cache pressure rather than a specific destination site or policy change.
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as the SSL inspection cache-eviction issue described in KB-3106. We increased the certificate cache size with `ssl inspection cache size 4096`, committed the change, and advised the customer to monitor eviction rates so they remain below 1,000 per hour. Inspection resumed normally after the cache was resized.

subject: APs loop in join state after upgrade to 4.6
description: Sunset Power Authority reported via the portal that a handful of APs never finish coming online after the controller was upgraded to Orion OW-20 release 4.6. The APs appear healthy on the network and can reach the controller, but they stay unavailable for 30 to 60 seconds at a time and then try again. `show ap summary` shows them as down/joining with radios off. The controller logs also show `%CAPWAP-3-JOIN_REJECT` against the affected APs during each attempt.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-4101, which affects 4.6 when an AP join request contains a zero-length RF profile TLV. We applied the workaround from the article by removing the RF profile override from the AP group so the controller no longer advertises the empty TLV. The APs then completed CAPWAP join and began serving clients.

subject: redwood university ar-900 loses bgp routes after circuit flap
description: Redwood University escalated through a partner after an Aurora AR-900 on 9.1.4 stopped installing several eBGP prefixes during a provider handoff. The partner reported that the BGP peering did not drop, but routing to remote campuses disappeared for a short period and recovered only after a manual refresh. TAC reviewed the device state and confirmed the symptoms were consistent with stale next-hop recursion rather than a peer failure. The issue is known to occur when the connected underlay route is withdrawn and relearned quickly on the 9.1 family.
resolution: TAC tied the case to KB-2101 and recommended upgrading the AR-900 to 9.2.0, which fixes next-hop cache invalidation when the resolving route changes. The customer completed the upgrade and verified that the BGP routes remained present during repeated circuit flap testing. We closed the case after confirming stable forwarding with the newer release.

subject: AR-900 routing process pegged after BGP maintenance
description: IronGate Freight emailed TAC about an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.1 that became slow after multiple BGP soft clears were issued during a peering change. They initially suspected an ACL or NAT problem because forwarding traffic stayed mostly intact while the management plane lagged. TAC reviewed the device state and confirmed the routing process was briefly consuming almost all CPU, especially when updates were still being received. The customer also provided a system message quoting "ERR-CPU-7781" during the event.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2110 and applied the workaround from the article. The customer was told to stop repeating soft clears during active update periods and to wait for route churn to settle before performing any refresh, or use a single hard clear in a maintenance window if necessary. After adopting that procedure, the router remained stable and the CPU spike did not recur.

subject: EVPN type-5 prefix stuck after anycast gateway move on 7.6
description: Redwood University called TAC after a campus core pair built on HX-5000 switches running 7.6 started blackholing traffic to a newly announced subnet. The customer believed the issue was limited to one VLAN, but TAC observed that the route stayed present on the local leaf while downstream sites continued using the old next hop for the prefix. The timing aligned with an anycast gateway MAC move during a planned failover test. The log buffer also contained "%EVPN-4-RT5-STALL", which indicated the EVPN process had suppressed the refresh.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-6108 and used the workaround from the article. A controlled EVPN route refresh was issued under router evpn, address-family l2vpn evpn, route-refresh, which forced the type-5 advertisement to update on the fabric.

subject: Repeated policy commit failures on 3.0 with oversized route-map
description: IronGate Freight emailed TAC about Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator 3.0 after a scheduled policy change would not finish and the branch remained on the old routing policy. TAC reviewed the tenant configuration and found one route-map exceeded 256 entries, while the policy worker CPU stayed elevated during each attempt. The customer provided logs from the orchestrator showing the failure condition, including the line "ERR-ORCH-4412". The edge devices were otherwise healthy and continued to use the prior configuration.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-5103 and applied the documented workaround. The route-map was split into smaller policy objects with 256 entries or fewer, then the customer committed the change again. The push completed successfully and the remaining entries were added in a follow-up commit.

subject: OW-20 guest portal fails after failover - need workaround
description: Northstar Bank opened a TAC email case for an Orion OW-20 running 4.9. Guest users authenticate normally on the primary controller, but after a failover the portal keeps sending them back to the login page instead of granting access. TAC reproduced the behavior in a lab sequence and confirmed the issue appears within a couple of seconds of redundancy switchover. The portal validation log also reports "%PORTAL-5-COOKIE_MISMATCH" for the affected sessions.
resolution: This was identified as KB-4109. Because the customer could not schedule an immediate upgrade, TAC applied the documented workaround: guest portal session timeout was reduced to 15 minutes and redundancy failover was inhibited during guest registration windows, with planned maintenance used to expire active sessions before switchover. The bank confirmed the redirect loop stopped when failover was controlled in this way.

subject: tune ap join for remote aps on 5.0
description: BlueRiver Credit Union asked how to tune AP join behavior so remote APs finish registration reliably on affected releases. They reported intermittent join stalls during controller discovery and capability revalidation, with some APs remaining in a pending state longer than expected. They want the recommended controller settings and any release-specific limits that should be checked before changing the join workflow.
resolution: TAC pointed them to GUIDE-OW and summarized the join guidance for the affected releases. For 4.6, remove any RF profile override from the AP group so the controller does not emit a zero-length RF profile TLV. For 4.7, set ap join retry-interval 2; for 4.8, set ap join timeout 180. For remote APs, keep one-way latency under 80 ms on 4.7 systems and keep uplink loss below 0.5% during 4.8 join operations. Verify with show ap summary and check recent events with show logging last 50.

subject: VPN drops on MetroLink NF-300 during rekey window
description: Partner escalated for MetroLink Telecom with reports that a routed IPsec tunnel between two WAN edge sites would fail and then rebuild without manual intervention. The customer initially suspected a peer-side timing issue because the disconnects were periodic and aligned with traffic bursts, but packet loss was limited to the encrypted path. The Nimbus NF-300 is running 5.1.5. During triage, TAC confirmed that the tunnel state oscillated during rekey and quoted the device log entry `%IKEV2-3-PROPOSAL_MISMATCH` immediately after the peer initiated a child-SA rekey.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-3102 and applied the workaround by forcing a single DH group on the tunnel policy. The customer configured `crypto ikev2 proposal default dh-group 14` in config mode and committed the change on both ends. The tunnel stabilized after the change, and no further proposal mismatch events were observed.

subject: P1: multiple branches dropped after certificate renewal
description: BlueRiver Credit Union escalated as P1 because several branches went offline shortly after certificate maintenance on the Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator. The affected edge fleet is running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and the first site to fail was BRCU-ATM-02 before additional branches followed within 2 to 6 minutes. TAC saw the same pattern at each site: the edge renews locally, then the next registration attempt is denied and the orchestrator marks the device disconnected. The edge logs include "%PKI-3-CHAIN-UNTRUSTED", which points to a trust-chain validation problem rather than a transport issue.
resolution: TAC resolved the outage using the KB-5102 workaround. We reimported the complete trust bundle on the orchestrator, including the current intermediate CA, and committed the change before reattempting edge registration. Once the bundle was refreshed, the affected sites checked in again and policy pushes completed successfully.

subject: Policy pushes failing on Atlas SD-WAN 2.9 orchestrator after one day
description: Field engineer on site for Evergreen Clinic Network reports that configuration changes stopped applying through the orchestrator after the system had been running normally for most of the day. The Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator is on version 2.9, and the edges still show healthy tunnels, but any policy update that touches the WAN profile fails during validation. Initial triage found the failure occurs before the job is sent to the edges, so this is not an overlay or transport issue. The customer said the same change had worked earlier in the week and asked whether the certificate service was down.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-5111 and applied the documented workaround. The CRL was refreshed on the orchestrator with `certificate import crl revocation-list.pem`, followed by `commit`, and the policy push succeeded after the updated timestamp was confirmed. We advised the customer to refresh the CRL before the 24-hour mark until they can move off 2.9.

subject: Outbound sessions failing after burst traffic on Aurora AR-900
description: Prairie State College submitted this through the customer portal for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.3.0. They described students losing access to web apps for a few minutes after lab login storms, then everything recovering on its own. TAC asked for NAT state and saw only a small active set in `show nat translations`, which did not match the reported failures. The router logs also contained `ERR-NAT-4108`, indicating source-port allocation failures even though utilization was low at the time of review.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2108 and advised the customer that this is a 9.3.0 NAT port accounting defect rather than true exhaustion. We applied the workaround by increasing the NAT pool size to add one more public address and setting the NAT translation timeout to 240 seconds. After the change, the college stopped seeing the short post-burst outage and no software upgrade was required.

subject: Latency on selected flows, possible session hash skew
description: Summit Logistics called in after seeing short latency bursts on shipment-tracking traffic through a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.0. Their team initially suspected an ISP path issue, but packet captures showed the same flows consistently landing on the same firewall worker queue. TAC verified the log entry "%SESSION-4-HASH_SKEW" and observed a persistent split where one shard stayed near 88 percent occupancy while the others remained below 40 percent. The issue appeared only after a few hundred thousand new sessions and was strongest on large-prefix traffic.
resolution: TAC implemented the workaround from KB-3110 by disabling asymmetric routing handling for the impacted policy set and committing the configuration. With the skew removed, session distribution normalized and the intermittent latency spikes were no longer observed.

subject: Atlas 3.3 edge CPU spikes and overlay flaps during LTE switchover
description: Partner escalation for Redwood University on an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.3 with dual LTE modems enabled. They reported brief overlay degradation and delayed tunnel keepalives during a carrier handoff, and initially suspected a tunnel MTU issue because the event coincided with a scheduled change window. TAC review of the edge telemetry showed control-plane CPU jumping into the high 90s for about 20 seconds during the handoff, then returning to normal without a reboot. The issue was reproducible only on the dual-modem site and not on single-modem branches. No certificate or policy syntax errors were found on the orchestrator side.
resolution: TAC identified this as the dual-modem LTE handoff issue described in KB-5112. We applied the documented workaround by setting handoff debounce to 5000 ms on the edge and advised the customer to avoid policy pushes during carrier switchover windows. After the change, CPU no longer spiked during handoff and overlay status remained stable.

subject: HX-5000 stack member drops off briefly during normal operation
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets reported that their Helix HX-5000 core stack on 7.6 would intermittently lose one member for about 10 to 15 seconds, then recover without any physical link alarms. The customer observed the master staying online while the member disappeared from `show stack`, and they initially suspected a bad stack cable. TAC review confirmed the ports stayed up and the event aligned with stack heartbeat jitter on a long cable run. During the incident, the switch logged "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN".
resolution: TAC identified the behavior as the known 7.6 stack heartbeat issue in KB-6104. We applied the documented workaround by setting `stack heartbeat timeout 900` in configuration mode and advised the customer to keep stack cabling under 1 m where possible. After the change, the stack remained stable and the brief member flaps stopped.

subject: OW-20 on 4.6 cannot stay on 5.0 after upgrade
description: Evergreen Clinic Network sent an on-site field engineer report for an Orion OW-20 running 4.6. The controller accepted the 5.0 image, rebooted, and then rolled back to the previous release after roughly 8 minutes without any AP impact. TAC confirmed the failure occurred during configuration database migration and was isolated to legacy guest portal ACL objects that had been carried forward from earlier releases. The engineer had already verified that the hardware and image integrity checks were clean.
resolution: TAC used KB-4111 and recommended upgrading the controller to 5.1 instead of retrying 5.0. The customer completed the 5.1 upgrade successfully, and the migration translated the legacy guest portal ACL objects without aborting.

subject: Repeated stack re-elections on HX-5000 pair
description: Customer emailed TAC about a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.3 that keeps swapping stack master roles during the day. They described it as a 'random reboot of the main unit,' but the device stays up and only the active supervisor role moves between members. Triage showed no link-down counters on the stack ports, and the behavior aligns with a software election instability rather than a hardware failure. The issue is most visible when the control plane is busy, with the stack showing brief election instability and then recovering on its own.
resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-6103 and instructed the customer to apply the documented workaround: use matched-length stack cables between all members, keep control-plane utilization below 60 percent, and set a higher priority on the preferred master with `configure terminal`, `stack member 1 priority 200`, and `stack member 2 priority 100`. The customer confirmed the stack stopped oscillating after the priority change and cable normalization.

subject: Memory leak on HX-5000 after EVPN route-refresh events
description: MetroLink Telecom raised the issue through an on-site field engineer for a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6. They reported intermittent control-plane lag and said the problem seemed to follow route changes from the EVPN fabric, not a link failure. TAC found that the routing process RSS had risen from about 910 MB to 1.9 GB over the course of the day, while free memory dropped to 12 percent. The system log showed "%MEM-4-LEAK", which aligned with the observed growth in `show process memory`. Spanning tree and interface state were normal, so TAC ruled out a Layer 2 instability.
resolution: TAC linked the symptoms to KB-6112 and determined the HX-5000 was affected by the 7.6 routing process leak during repeated EVPN route-refresh events. The customer upgraded to 8.0, where the refresh handler has been corrected to reuse cache objects and free stale generations immediately. After the upgrade, memory stabilized and the control-plane latency cleared.

subject: Urgent: roaming failures on OW-20 4.9 across campus SSID
description: Prairie State College escalated through a partner because voice users were reporting repeated roam interruptions on an Orion OW-20 running 4.9. The clients reassociate to the next AP, but users hear a noticeable pause before the call recovers, especially in lecture halls with frequent movement. TAC triage confirmed the controller is on 4.9 and that the issue is reproducible during moderate CPU utilization. Based on the pattern, this is a controller-side fast-transition delay rather than an RF coverage problem.
resolution: TAC resolved the case by recommending an upgrade to 5.0 per KB-4105. The issue is fixed in 5.0, where FT key installation uses a dedicated queue with priority over accounting updates. The customer was advised to schedule the upgrade in the next maintenance window and retest 802.11r roaming after completion.

subject: Missing link traps from edge router; monitoring gap during outage, AR-900 9.1.4
description: CivicWorks Public Agency emailed TAC about an Aurora AR-900 edge router running 9.1.4 that appeared to stop reporting some interface alarms during a building-wide network disturbance. They initially suspected an SNMP outage because the management station showed missing interface events, but periodic polling still showed the ports correctly. No detailed log bundle was attached, only a note that the problem happened when multiple switches were power-cycled in quick succession. TAC reviewed the case and determined the symptoms were consistent with a trap-burst condition on the router.
resolution: TAC associated the issue with KB-2109 and confirmed it is caused by the fixed 1024-entry SNMP trap queue on the AR-900. We advised the customer to reduce the event rate by enabling link debounce on the unstable access ports and to depend on polling at a 30-second interval for history reconstruction. The unit remained on 9.1.4, and no software update was required.

subject: AP registration stalls on Orion OW-20 4.8 after WAN jitter
description: Prairie State College opened the case after a batch of APs would sit in joining and then reset their CAPWAP sessions during a campus-to-branch deployment. The partner reported that the problem looked random, but the Orion OW-20 controller was running 4.8 and `show ap summary` showed a growing number of APs in join pending while the same units retried join twice and stopped. TAC review of the logs found "%ERR-APJ-4417" during the delayed capability exchange path. The pattern matched a join stall that was more visible when the uplink had 60-100 ms RTT and short retransmit bursts.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-4103 and advised the customer to upgrade the OW-20 from 4.8 to 4.9. The upgrade moved the join logic to the fixed code path that matches delayed capability responses to the active join session before timeout. After the change, APs joined directly to authorized without further stalls.

subject: HX-5000 port-channel flaps back with missing members after link restoration
description: Lakeside Hospitality escalated a core-switch issue from the NOC on a Helix HX-5000 running 7.4. Their four-link aggregation to an access distribution switch sometimes returns with only two active links after a single member is unplugged and reinserted. They initially suspected a bad cable, but the same behavior repeats across different links and the neighbor remains in LACP sync. TAC observed the local bundle suspending ports during rejoin and confirmed the switch is hitting the known aggregation mismatch behavior.
resolution: TAC tied the symptoms to KB-6106 for HX-5000 7.4. We used the documented workaround by configuring fast LACP timers on the port-channel and the peer, then manually clearing the affected EtherChannel after the links were restored. The bundle re-formed with all four members and the hotel reported no further suspension events during later maintenance work.

subject: OSPF session reset on AR-900 after VLAN cutover
description: Sunset Power Authority reported that their Aurora AR-900 on 9.2.0 stopped learning routes across a new shared-services VLAN after a cutover. The on-site engineer saw the neighbor oscillating between ExStart and Down, which was initially suspected to be a cabling or duplex problem. TAC confirmed the physical link was clean and that the router was sending and receiving OSPF hellos normally, but the adjacency would not move past database exchange on the multiaccess network. The system log included "%OSPF-4-ADJ-EXSTART" each time the neighbor reset.
resolution: TAC advised upgrading the AR-900 to 9.2.1, which contains the fix described in KB-2103. After upgrade, OSPF DBD negotiation completed normally and the neighbor remained in Full state on the VLAN. The customer validated steady LSDB size and route stability before closing the case.

subject: p1: branch lte overlay failing after 3.1 migration
description: Northstar Bank’s NOC escalated a priority 1 incident after several branch edges on Atlas SD-WAN 3.1 started losing access to internal banking applications over LTE failover. One representative device, 203.0.113.52, is running 3.1 and still shows the tunnels as established, but large transactions time out while small keepalives continue to pass. The NOC also forwarded the edge log, which shows repeated "%UPG-5-MTU-MIGRATE" messages after the upgrade. Triage indicates the failure is isolated to dual-SIM LTE interfaces where a custom tunnel MTU had been configured before the upgrade.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-5104 and had the customer restore the LTE tunnel MTU on each affected interface using `interface lte0 tunnel-mtu 1400` followed by `commit`. Once applied, the overlay stopped advertising the incorrect encapsulation size and the failed transactions recovered.

subject: branch vpn instability resolved by software upgrade to 5.1.3
description: BlueRiver Credit Union reported repeated short VPN interruptions on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9, with the issue affecting a branch-to-datacenter tunnel used for transaction processing. The customer noted that the tunnel stayed established for long periods and then briefly failed to pass traffic, but there was no full disconnect alarm from the peer. TAC review showed the child SA counter resetting during rekey while the IKE SA remained established, which pointed to a rekey negotiation defect rather than a routing issue. The case notes referenced a known child-SA proposal handling problem in this release family, and TAC recommended moving to a fixed release instead of continuing with a temporary workaround.
resolution: TAC identified KB-3101 and advised the customer to upgrade the Nimbus NF-300 from 5.0.9 to 5.1.3, where the child SA proposal list is rebuilt on every rekey exchange. After the upgrade and a controlled tunnel clear, the VPN completed multiple rekey cycles without traffic loss. No workaround was left in place after validation.

subject: Guest captive portal sessions drop after controller failover
description: Sunset Power Authority reported that their Orion OW-20 controller, running 4.9, would accept guest sign-ins but lose those sessions after a standby takeover. The field engineer initially suspected DHCP or DNS because users were being redirected back to the portal, but the guest database entries were still present and only the post-failover state was broken. TAC reviewed the controller state and determined the symptom was limited to guest portal session handling during redundancy events. The problem was consistent with a cookie validation defect in the active/standby handoff path.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-4109. The customer upgraded the OW-20 from 4.9 to 5.0, which corrects guest portal cookie validation so it is tied to the redundancy cluster identity instead of the active node UUID. After the upgrade, failover testing showed guest sessions surviving switchover as expected.

subject: OW-20 guest portal re-prompts users after redundancy test
description: Summit Logistics called from the data center after testing redundancy on an Orion OW-20 running 4.9. Their guest network works until the controller role changes, then every browser gets sent back to the portal and users cannot stay authorized. The field engineer verified that the issue only appears after failover and not during normal operation, which ruled out a general portal outage. TAC also confirmed that existing guest entries were not being removed from the database, so the symptom was tied to session validation rather than account creation.
resolution: This case matched KB-4109. TAC implemented the supported workaround by setting guest portal session timeout to 15 minutes, expiring current guest sessions before the planned switchover, and keeping redundancy failover inhibited during guest registration windows. After those changes, Summit Logistics was able to complete maintenance without the portal redirect loop.

subject: Orchestrator CPU spikes when monthly reports run
description: Summit Logistics escalated that their Atlas SD-WAN 3.3 orchestrator became very slow every time the nightly reporting task ran, and the NOC saw administrator actions queue up behind it. They suspected an edge problem at first, but `show sdwan tunnels` on the edges showed normal tunnel state and loss was not changing. TAC confirmed the orchestrator was running 3.3 and that the reporting service was consuming the majority of CPU while the job was active. The symptom pattern matched a known reporting scale limit. The orchestrator log showed '%ERR-ORCH-5178' during the report window.
resolution: TAC resolved the case per KB-5107 by applying the workaround. We reduced flow-history retention to 5 days with `reporting flow-history retention 5d` and committed the change, which lowered the reporting workload and removed the CPU contention during scheduled jobs.

subject: App traffic stays on withdrawn WAN path after failover
description: Summit Logistics reported that application traffic kept using the primary WAN path even after the circuit was intentionally withdrawn during a maintenance window. The issue was observed on an Atlas SD-WAN edge running 3.1, while the orchestrator still showed the route as present for a short period after the withdrawal. TAC checked the edge state and confirmed that `show app-route sla-class` continued to list the withdrawn next-hop as eligible until the cache aged out. The customer also captured the log message "%SDWAN-4-ROUTE-CACHE" during the event, which aligned with the stale route-cache behavior.
resolution: TAC identified this as the 3.1 route-cache defect described in KB-5109. As a workaround, TAC changed the route-cache aging timer to 60 seconds with `app-route cache age-time 60` and then committed the change so the stale candidate would clear sooner during planned underlay changes. The customer was instructed to refresh policy before shifting traffic to the backup link and to restore the normal timer after the maintenance window.

subject: HX-5000 upgrade rollback with calibration import failure
description: MetroLink Telecom’s on-site field engineer opened the case after an HX-5000 core switch running 7.2 failed an in-service upgrade to 7.4. The engineer saw the upgrade progress halt between 78 and 82 percent, then the management plane restarted once and the switch rolled back to the old release. TAC asked for the upgrade trace and the log showed "ERR-UPG-2207" during the calibration import stage. The chassis has many optics installed, and post-rollback inventory commands were slow, especially `show interfaces transceiver detail`.
resolution: TAC identified the failure as KB-6111 and instructed the field engineer to use the documented workaround on the 7.2 image. They cleared nonessential transceiver calibration history, wrote memory, and rebooted the switch so the calibration cache would rebuild smaller before retrying the upgrade. After that, the upgrade completed normally.

subject: HA pair recovers but standby session table lags behind
description: Prairie State College opened a case through the customer portal for a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.9. They reported a short network interruption and said the firewall pair recovered cleanly, but the standby unit continued to show fewer sessions than the active unit for several minutes after failover. TAC verified that `show ha status` indicated synced state, while the session table on the standby remained lower by tens of thousands of entries. No log bundle was attached, but the symptoms were limited to the post-recovery window and then began to self-correct.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-3103 and advised the standard workaround. The customer issued `ha resync full` from config mode and waited for the replay queue to drain before allowing another failover event. The session counts converged without requiring a software change.

subject: OW-20 APs never reach authorized state at branch site
description: Northstar Bank reported a widespread AP outage at a branch using an Orion OW-20 on 4.8. The field engineer observed APs stuck in joining for several minutes, then dropping and retrying without ever reaching authorized, which initially looked like a controller reachability issue. On-site triage confirmed the controller was up and the same join retry counter incremented twice before stopping, while `show ap summary` showed multiple APs in join pending. The event log also contained "%ERR-APJ-4417", and the behavior correlated with a WAN path showing 70-90 ms RTT and short retransmit bursts during the join process.
resolution: TAC linked the symptoms to KB-4103 and confirmed the defect affects Orion OW-20 release 4.8. Because the customer needed a permanent fix and the site was already in outage, Northstar Bank was moved to 4.9, where delayed capability responses are matched to the active join session before it ages out. After the upgrade, AP registration completed normally and the join pending count stopped increasing.

subject: Repeated radar events on 5.1 stop RF channel updates
description: The NOC escalated that an Orion OW-20 running 5.1 was not reassigning 5 GHz channels after a cluster of radar detections. `show ap summary` showed the APs were still up, but the RF dashboard had no new channel-change messages after the first few events and clients were retransmitting more often than normal. TAC confirmed the radar counter kept increasing while the channel-selection queue appeared to stop draining. The controller log included "%RF-4-DFS_FREEZE" coincident with the last successful channel move.
