resolution: TAC followed KB-4110 and applied the workaround: DFS was disabled for the affected radio group, and the radios were pinned to a non-DFS channel set with at least 20 MHz separation from neighboring cells. After the workaround, channel updates were restored and retry rates fell back to normal levels.

subject: Intermittent WAN BFD flap on 9.1.4 edge router
description: Phone call logged by the TAC agent: Cornerstone Supermarkets reported that one WAN path on an Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4 started flapping after several weeks of stable service. The customer initially suspected provider instability, but `show bfd neighbors detail` showed only one side of the session losing transmit activity while the remote peer kept responding briefly. During the call, the agent confirmed the router logged `%BFD-3-ERR-BFD-2201: transmit scheduling stalled for session 203.0.113.8/203.0.113.9`. The issue is consistent with a long-uptime transmit scheduler problem rather than a carrier outage.
resolution: TAC matched the symptom set to KB-2102 and implemented the workaround from the article. The BFD timers were adjusted with `configure`, `router bfd`, `timers 200 200 5` on the noncritical adjacency, and the customer was advised to avoid running past the uptime threshold without a planned restart. This contained the flaps while keeping service stable.

subject: Recent wireless changes not present after OW-20 restore
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets called to report that their Orion OW-20 on 5.1 restored successfully from a backup, but two WLAN tweaks made shortly before the backup were not present afterward. The customer believed the restore had failed because the system came back without any corruption message and all other settings looked normal. TAC checked the sequence of changes and found the backup was initiated while WLAN edits were still staged in the commit queue. The restored image matched the last committed state rather than the most recent in-memory edits.
resolution: TAC closed the case under KB-4112 and instructed the customer to take backups only after the commit queue is empty. We had them confirm the pending state with `show configuration database summary`, commit the WLAN changes, and wait for the queue to drain before rerunning `backup configuration`.

subject: Route-map change will not complete on Atlas SD-WAN 3.0
description: Phone call logged by the TAC agent for Prairie State College on Atlas SD-WAN orchestrator 3.0. The caller said a routine routing policy edit had been spinning for most of the workday and then failed, but the branches still showed the old configuration. TAC reproduced the behavior on the policy worker and found the tenant had a single route-map with 257 rules. The orchestrator CPU climbed into the high 90s during the commit attempt, while the edges continued to advertise the prior policy.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-5103 and applied the documented workaround. The route-map was split so each policy object contained 256 entries or fewer, then the customer committed the change again. The policy push completed successfully and the remaining entries were added in a second commit.

subject: Recurrent 25g loss of signal on hx-5000 7.2
description: Prairie State College emailed TAC about an HX-5000 core switch on 7.2 that was dropping a 25g connection often enough to disrupt class network traffic. Their message described the port as "going dead" and coming back later, but they were not sure whether the optic or the server NIC was at fault. TAC reviewed the interface counters and transceiver detail and confirmed that the module showed a sharp bias current increase just before each down event. The device itself stayed powered, and the pattern repeated on the same port while the optic was in service.
resolution: TAC tied the failure pattern to KB-6101 and applied the workaround from the article by setting the transceiver monitoring interval to 120 seconds on the affected interface. That reduced the DOM polling activity enough to stop the flaps while the customer planned a later maintenance upgrade.

subject: 2.9 edge overlay keeps flipping during backup jobs
description: Northstar Bank opened an NOC escalation after several branch edges on Atlas SD-WAN 2.9 started bouncing between up and degraded during nightly backup windows. The customer reported that voice calls were being rerouted even though the transport circuit stayed up, and the issue appeared roughly every 30 to 60 seconds when upload traffic increased. TAC reviewed `show sdwan tunnels` on edge edge-214 and saw loss counters increment during the burst periods; the edge was running 2.9.0 build 4172. The event log also showed "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN" on the affected tunnel when the probes were delayed behind bulk traffic.
resolution: TAC determined the condition matched KB-5105 for Atlas SD-WAN 2.9, where SLA probes share the data-plane queue with bursty traffic. We applied the documented workaround by placing the SLA probes into a high-priority queue with `app-route sla-class voice probe-queue priority` and committed the change. After the queue change, tunnel state remained stable through the next backup window and loss counters no longer tripped health evaluation.

subject: HX-5000 stack master keeps changing on 7.3
description: On-site field engineer reported intermittent stack leadership changes on a Helix HX-5000 core switch stack running 7.3. The stack has four members, and the customer sees brief control-plane interruptions during normal business hours, especially when backup jobs and SNMP polling are active. `show stack` shows the members in separate election domains for a short period before converging again, and the event log includes repeated "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN" messages without any physical stack cable alarms. I confirmed the issue is reproducible under moderate control-plane load and is consistent with a software election problem rather than a cabling fault.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-6103 and advised the customer to upgrade the stack to 7.4, where master election uses the current adjacency score and ignores transient scheduler delay spikes. After the upgrade, the stack remained stable through validation testing and no further re-election events were observed.

subject: Traffic not failing over immediately after underlay withdrawal
description: BlueRiver Credit Union's partner opened an escalation after branch traffic stayed on the primary underlay during a planned ISP cutover. The Atlas SD-WAN edge in question is running 3.1, and the partner reported that the edge continued to send application traffic toward the removed next-hop even though the link was no longer advertised upstream. TAC reproduced the behavior in the lab and saw that the withdrawn route remained eligible in the app-routing cache until the normal aging timer expired. The event logs included "%SDWAN-4-ROUTE-CACHE", which supported the stale route-cache diagnosis.
resolution: TAC identified the defect as KB-5109 and used the supported workaround rather than waiting for cache expiry. The route-cache timer was reduced to 60 seconds with `app-route cache age-time 60`, then `commit` was applied so the stale candidate would clear faster during maintenance. The partner was instructed to confirm the backup path was selected before removing the primary underlay from service.

subject: Throughput collapse during threat update on NF-300
description: Pinnacle Energy called TAC after their NF-300 on 5.1.5 showed a sharp throughput drop during a threat database update. The appliance stays online, but branch traffic falls from about 8 Gbps to under 1 Gbps for roughly 45 seconds, then returns to normal once the new signatures are active. TAC confirmed that the session table continued to grow with new sessions while established sessions aged out at the expected rate, which is consistent with an activation-time stall rather than a hardware failure. The customer supplied a timestamped alert and the firewall log line '%TP-4-SIGNATURE_STALL' from the same event.
resolution: TAC traced the symptom to KB-3105 and recommended upgrading the NF-300 from 5.1.5 to 5.2.0. The customer completed the upgrade, and the signature activation path now completes without the dataplane mutex hold that caused the temporary throughput collapse. Post-upgrade testing showed no repeat of the issue during the next threat update.

subject: Guests stuck in portal loop after standby takes over
description: Evergreen Clinic Network submitted a portal form ticket for an Orion OW-20 running 4.9. Their guest users can sign in successfully, but when the controller fails over the browser immediately returns to the login page and the session never becomes authorized. TAC checked the redundancy state and portal behavior and saw the issue appear right after the standby became active. The portal log includes repeated "%PORTAL-5-COOKIE_MISMATCH" entries during the affected sessions.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-4109. Since the customer needed a short-term fix, we applied the documented workaround: guest portal session timeout was set to 15 minutes and redundancy failover was inhibited during guest registration windows, with sessions expired before planned switchover. Evergreen confirmed the redirect loop stopped once failover was controlled and users reauthenticated after maintenance.

subject: intermittent tunnel pause every few minutes on nimbus nf-300
description: Summit Logistics called in to report that a site-to-site VPN on a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.2.2 would occasionally stop passing traffic for about a second, then recover without intervention. The customer initially suspected an ISP issue because the IKEv2 session never fully dropped. TAC reviewed the device state and confirmed the tunnel stayed up, with the outage only appearing during periodic liveness and rekey activity. The timing pattern is consistent with an overlap in aggressive VPN timers rather than a general WAN fault.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-3112. We resolved it by staggering the DPD timer away from the child-SA rekey timer, following the documented workaround. The customer entered `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 3` in config mode and committed the change, which removed the recurring forwarding pause.

subject: Intermittent loss on uplink traffic during multicast bursts
description: Prairie State College opened the case after reporting intermittent drops on unrelated unicast traffic traversing a Helix HX-5000 core switch. The device is running 8.0, and the issue was most visible during classroom video distribution windows. TAC checked queue statistics and found bursts of discard increments on the uplink queue, typically a few hundred packets at a time, while port utilization remained below 80 percent. The customer also provided a syslog excerpt containing "%BUF-3-OVERFLOW", which aligned with the observed loss pattern.
resolution: TAC used the workaround documented in KB-6110. We lowered the multicast reservation on the affected leaf and recommended isolating replication-heavy workloads onto a separate uplink group so the shared buffer pool would not be exhausted during bursts. The customer verified that the discard spikes and user-visible packet loss no longer occurred after the change.

subject: Branch router CPU jumps when IPv6 hosts join network
description: Lakeside Hospitality sent an on-site field engineer report for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 at a hotel branch. The engineer observed that whenever a large number of guest devices came online at once, the router CPU rose sharply and some IPv6 clients needed several minutes before they were reachable. TAC review showed the issue was isolated to neighbor discovery bursts on one guest access VLAN; BGP and NAT services remained stable. `show control-plane protection statistics` was not showing a corresponding increase in drop counters during the event, which pointed away from a simple overrun condition.
resolution: TAC linked the behavior to KB-2106 and treated it as the 9.2.3 IPv6 ND policer accounting defect. We applied the workaround by lowering the IPv6 ND control-plane limit to 2000 pps and advised the field engineer to add storm control on the guest access VLAN while investigating the source of the burst. The customer reported the CPU spikes stopped and IPv6 neighbor resolution returned to normal.

subject: Core switch dropping packets even though links are not saturated
description: Sunset Power Authority reported that a Helix HX-5000 core switch on 8.0 was dropping packets in short bursts and asked whether the uplinks were failing. Their monitoring showed the links were well below line rate, so the initial assumption was a physical issue, but TAC did not see optics or interface errors on the affected ports. On review, the drop events correlated with multicast-heavy periods and the unicast egress queue showed brief headroom exhaustion rather than continuous oversubscription. This matched the known 8.0 replication behavior for the platform.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-6110 by limiting multicast fanout on the busiest leaf and moving replication-heavy workloads onto a separate uplink group. We also advised the customer to schedule predictable bursts outside congestion-sensitive windows when possible. After the change, the short loss events stopped and the case was resolved.

subject: P1: SSL inspection bypass affecting multiple web users
description: Cornerstone Supermarkets escalated through a partner because multiple stores reported that outbound HTTPS sessions were reaching the internet without decryption on an NF-300 running 5.2.0. The issue was severe enough to be treated as a priority one because it affected several user groups at once, although the firewall continued to pass traffic normally. TAC review showed the SSL inspection cache under heavy churn, with repeated certificate cache evictions correlating to the time window when the bypass was observed. The symptoms were intermittent and did not align with a single application or server group, which pointed away from a policy mismatch.
resolution: TAC identified the defect as the cache-eviction bypass condition documented in KB-3106. We applied the supported workaround by increasing the certificate cache size to reduce eviction pressure, then committed the change and confirmed that SSL inspection resumed for new HTTPS sessions. The customer was advised to keep eviction rates below 1,000 per hour and to restart SSL inspection only if they needed to clear stale lookup state immediately.

subject: 2.9 edge marks tunnels degraded during student backup jobs
description: Redwood University phoned TAC after noticing that classroom voice traffic and exam portals were being steered away from the preferred WAN path each evening. The customer said the internet circuit looked healthy, but the SD-WAN edge kept reporting poor path quality whenever campus backup jobs ran. TAC confirmed the appliance was an Atlas SD-WAN edge on version 2.9 and checked `show sdwan tunnels`, which showed loss spikes only under heavy outbound load. The event trace also contained "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN", indicating the probe packets were being delayed long enough to fail the latency threshold.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-5105 and applied the recommended workaround. We moved the SLA probes to a priority queue using `app-route sla-class voice probe-queue priority` and committed the change so probes would not sit behind bulk traffic. After the change, the edge stayed up on the preferred path throughout the nightly backup cycle.

subject: BFD session stop sending packets on 9.1.4 after long uptime
description: Phone call logged by the TAC agent: BlueRiver Credit Union reported that their Aurora AR-900 running 9.1.4 had one BFD neighbor repeatedly timing out, then recovering, then timing out again. The customer thought the issue was related to a firewall change, but the router-side counters told a different story: `show bfd neighbors detail` showed the local session as Up while transmit activity had frozen on the affected peer. The device also emitted `%BFD-3-ERR-BFD-2201: transmit scheduling stalled for session 192.0.2.20/192.0.2.21`. TAC confirmed this matched a known uptime-related defect rather than a filtering problem.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-2102 by changing the BFD profile to longer timers on the affected noncritical peer: `configure`, `router bfd`, `timers 200 200 5`. The customer was also told to schedule a restart or process reload before the platform reaches the known wrap point to prevent recurrence. This restored stable forwarding until a permanent code fix can be deployed.

subject: Topology-change storm on access switch after virtual host reboot
description: Redwood University phoned TAC about a Helix HX-5000 running 7.2 in a lab network. After one downstream virtualization host rebooted, the switch began emitting topology-change notifications every 2 to 4 seconds for several minutes, which the customer first described as an STP loop. TAC reviewed the logs and observed "%STP-5-TCN-STORM" on the affected access interface. `show spanning-tree detail` showed the same port reentering forwarding repeatedly, and MAC entries on that segment were aging out long before the configured timer expired.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-6105 and confirmed it is a configuration and design constraint of rapid-pvst on ports that learn multiple moving MAC addresses. We instructed the customer to stop using rapid-pvst on that edge connection and to place the server behind a dedicated edge VLAN design or restrict the port to a single access device. The workaround was implemented and the repeated topology-change notifications stopped.

subject: HX-5000 upgrade stalls and reboots during transceiver calibration import
description: Summit Logistics’ NOC escalated a repeated upgrade failure on an HX-5000 core switch running 7.2. During the move to 7.4, the progress bar consistently stopped around 80%, the management plane restarted once, and the system came back on the old image. The team first suspected stack instability, but TAC found no stack fault history and the behavior pointed to the upgrade parser. The trace included "ERR-UPG-2207", and the chassis had enough populated optics that `show interfaces transceiver detail` took noticeably longer after rollback than before the upgrade attempt.
resolution: TAC traced the issue to KB-6111 and applied the workaround described there. The NOC backed up the configuration, removed nonessential DOM history, ran `configure terminal`, `no transceiver calibration-history`, `write memory`, and `reload`, then retried the upgrade after reseating the most recently installed optics. The upgrade completed without a rollback on the second attempt.

subject: EVPN type-5 routes stale after gateway MAC move on HX-5000 7.6
description: IronGate Freight opened this as a NOC escalation after a pair of HX-5000 leafs running 7.6 lost reachability to several warehouse prefixes during a gateway failover. Their report said traffic blackholed for roughly 10 minutes after the anycast gateway moved, while the local switch still showed the routes present. TAC checked the EVPN control plane and confirmed the prefix was still installed locally on the leaf, but remote VTEPs were holding the previous next-hop. The switch log also showed "%EVPN-4-RT5-STALL" at the time of the MAC move.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-6108 and advised that the issue is fixed in 8.0. IronGate Freight upgraded the affected HX-5000 pair from 7.6 to 8.0, and the EVPN type-5 advertisements resumed updating immediately after subsequent gateway moves.

subject: prevent sla class flapping on marginal wan links
description: CivicWorks Public Agency asked how to keep an SLA class from flapping when a WAN link shows brief loss spikes. They are running Atlas SD-WAN 3.1 and want the class to stay stable during short degradations rather than bouncing between up and down states. Their use case is latency-sensitive voice traffic on a link that is already close to threshold.
resolution: TAC pointed them to GUIDE-AT and recommended using a probe window of at least five samples so a single 1-second loss spike does not clear the SLA class. We also advised setting a 5000 ms hold-down before recovery, and increasing the packet-loss threshold by 1 to 2 percent if the link is already near the limit. For voice classes, keep the probe interval at 1000 ms unless there is a site-specific design reason to slow it down; then apply the change with `app-route sla-class voice loss-threshold 5 latency-threshold 80 probe-interval 1000 hold-down 5000`, commit, and verify with `show app-route sla-class`.

subject: pinnacle energy hx-5000 dropping bursts on core uplink
description: Pinnacle Energy called TAC by phone after monitoring showed rising packet loss on a core-facing 100G port. The switch is a Helix HX-5000 running 7.2, and the customer reported that the problem was most visible during scheduled backup and replication windows. TAC observed that average utilization remained in the low 70 percent range, but the output queue was still building and `show queue counters` showed tail drops climbing steadily. Initial suspicion was a design change in the WAN handoff, but the queueing profile matched a known scheduler limitation on this software release.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-6109 and recommended the upgrade path. Pinnacle Energy upgraded the HX-5000 from 7.2 to 7.4, which includes the scheduler reservation window expansion and earlier buffer watermark checks. After the upgrade, the customer confirmed that burst-related output drops on the 100G port stopped recurring.

subject: Renewed certificate accepted on edge, but orchestrator rejects registration
description: Redwood University wrote in about a campus edge that renewed its certificate successfully but then disappeared from the orchestrator. The device is RU-EDGE-WEST running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and TAC observed the site flipping to disconnected status about 4 minutes after renewal. The edge log is explicit: "%PKI-3-CHAIN-UNTRUSTED" during the next registration attempt. Initial triage indicates the stored trust chain on the orchestrator still references the old intermediate CA, so the new chain cannot be built to a trusted root.
resolution: TAC resolved this per KB-5102. We reimported the full certificate chain, including the active intermediate CA, on the orchestrator and committed the update. The edge then re-registered successfully and policy deployment to the site completed without further certificate errors.

subject: OW-20 5.1 RF manager stops moving 5 GHz APs after DFS activity
description: On-site field engineer reported intermittent coverage gaps on an Orion OW-20 running 5.1 after several radar events on the 5 GHz band. The APs themselves remained online, and `show ap summary` showed normal join status, but the affected radios stayed on one channel far longer than expected. TAC verified that the radar counter continued to increment while no additional channel re-evaluation occurred. The issue appeared only after multiple DFS hits in a short interval and did not correlate with AP uptime or client authentication.
resolution: TAC used the workaround documented in KB-4110. DFS was disabled on the impacted radio group and the 5 GHz radios were pinned to a non-DFS channel plan with proper channel separation from adjacent cells. That prevented the RF manager stall and restored predictable channel movement.

subject: Backup path not selected until cache expires on edge 3.1
description: HarborPoint Retail opened the case through a partner escalation after several stores saw traffic remain on a decommissioned circuit for a few minutes longer than expected. The affected Atlas SD-WAN edge is running 3.1, and the customer initially suspected an SLA probe issue because application traffic did eventually move without any manual changes. TAC reviewed the edge behavior and found that the withdrawn route was still being treated as a valid candidate by the application policy until the route cache aged out. No log bundle was attached, but the symptom pattern matched a stale route-candidate issue during underlay withdrawal.
resolution: TAC tied the behavior to KB-5109 and applied the documented workaround. The route-cache timer was shortened to 60 seconds with `app-route cache age-time 60`, followed by `commit`, so the stale entry would clear more quickly during planned maintenance. The partner was advised to confirm the stale candidate no longer appeared in `show app-route sla-class` before moving traffic to the backup link.

subject: Outbound HTTPS sometimes shows site cert instead of inspection cert
description: Northstar Bank submitted a portal request for an NF-300 running 5.2.2 after users reported that some banking-related HTTPS sessions were not being decrypted. The reports were inconsistent at first, which made the bank suspect browser pinning or a server-side TLS change, but TAC found the issue was reproducible during periods of high SSL inspection churn. `show ssl inspection statistics` showed certificate cache evictions well above the healthy range, and the problem tended to appear after the cache had been under pressure for roughly 5 to 10 minutes. Other forwarding functions and policy enforcement were normal during the same interval.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3106 and confirmed that no software upgrade was required. We implemented the supported workaround by raising the certificate cache size, committed the configuration, and verified that new outbound TLS sessions resumed full inspection.

subject: Backup on OW-20 missing staged WLAN edits after restore
description: MetroLink Telecom reported from an on-site field engineer that an Orion OW-20 on 4.7 restored cleanly, but the most recent wireless profile change was absent after the restore. The engineer initially suspected a bad backup file, but the controller otherwise loaded normally and no integrity alarms were present. TAC reviewed the change timing and found the backup had been taken while the configuration database commit queue was still active. The controller had backed up the persisted state only, so the latest staged WLAN edit was not included. "%ERR-DB-1809: backup snapshot taken with non-empty commit queue; pending WLAN edits omitted"
resolution: TAC resolved the case using KB-4112 and explained that no software defect needed to be remediated in the field. We instructed the engineer to check `show configuration database summary`, wait until the queue reaches zero, then `commit` and take `backup configuration` only after the WLAN changes have been idle for at least 30 seconds.

subject: Intermittent path switch on app-aware routing after missed probe
description: Summit Logistics reported that shipping-label traffic was intermittently rerouted during brief wireless fades, but the link never appeared fully down. The affected device is atlas-edge-22 running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and TAC reproduced the issue by observing one missed 1-second probe followed by a prolonged class-down state. `show app-route sla-class` showed the class as down for several intervals even though loss remained under 2 percent afterward. The edge log recorded "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN" at the time of the transition.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-5101 and advised the customer to upgrade to 2.9, where the SLA evaluator uses the configured rolling window before changing state. Summit Logistics upgraded atlas-edge-22 to 2.9 and confirmed the routing policy held during the same brownout pattern. No further path flaps were observed after the upgrade.

subject: image verification error after https download on nf-300
description: Pinnacle Energy emailed TAC after their Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 failed two maintenance-window upgrades to 5.0.9. They reported that the image downloads successfully, but the reboot returns to the prior release and the console shows "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". Initial checks showed the image file size and SHA-256 checksum are valid on the source server, which suggested a boot-loader verification issue rather than a corrupted download. The behavior is isolated to this 5.0.8 appliance and happens immediately after the HTTPS stage download path completes.
resolution: TAC mapped the symptoms to KB-3104 and recommended the supported resolution path: upgrade the system to 5.0.9. Once the customer performed the upgrade, the image verification step completed normally and subsequent reboot cycles retained 5.0.9.

subject: Packet loss on HX-5000 during multicast traffic windows
description: Redwood University opened this on behalf of the customer after several staff complaints about brief application stalls on a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 8.0. The customer initially suspected spanning-tree instability, but TAC found no topology change events and no evidence of a loop. Queue counters showed repeated discard increments on the uplink queue in bursts of roughly 200 to 600 packets, and the logs included "%BUF-3-OVERFLOW" at the same times. Interface utilization remained under 80 percent, which pointed away from sustained congestion and toward a buffer reservation issue during multicast replication.
resolution: TAC implemented the KB-6110 workaround by reducing multicast reservation on the affected leaf and shifting the replication-heavy traffic to a separate uplink group. We also recommended keeping the bursty multicast workloads outside peak business windows where possible. The customer confirmed that the packet loss on unrelated unicast traffic cleared after the change.

subject: Packet loss after threat signature update on 5.1.5
description: Northstar Bank, through their partner, reported short-lived packet loss on an NF-300 running 5.1.5 after a scheduled threat database refresh. Their users noticed slow access to internal apps for roughly one minute, but the firewall did not fail over and normal traffic returned on its own. TAC confirmed that session aging remained normal and that the slowdown matches the signature activation period rather than an interface or routing problem. The partner asked whether a software defect was involved because the pattern repeats after each large update.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-3105 and recommended the supported upgrade path. The customer upgraded the NF-300 from 5.1.5 to 5.2.0, where signature activation is chunked and no longer blocks the dataplane mutex for the full load duration. After the upgrade, the throughput drop during threat updates no longer reproduced.

subject: Stack master instability on HX-5000 core switch
description: Customer submitted a portal report for a Helix HX-5000 core switch stack on version 7.3. They said the 'main switch' keeps changing and management sessions drop for a few seconds, but they could not reproduce it on demand. Initial triage found no cable faults, no member loss, and no stack port errors; the issue appears only when the control plane is under routine business load. The behavior matches a transient stack election issue rather than a physical failure.
resolution: TAC associated the incident with KB-6103 and applied the workaround from the article. The customer replaced mixed-length stack cables with matched-length cables, reduced control-plane load during peak periods, and set the desired master to a higher priority using the documented configuration commands. The stack remained stable after the changes.

subject: HX-5000 upgrade from 7.2 aborts near 80% and rolls back
description: HarborPoint Retail opened this through a partner escalation for an HX-5000 core switch running 7.2. They reported that an in-service upgrade to 7.4 repeatedly stalled around 80% and then rolled back after a management-plane restart. TAC reviewed the upgrade output and found the log entry "ERR-UPG-2207" at the point of failure. The switch has a high optic count, and `show interfaces transceiver detail` was slow to return after rollback, which matched the reported delay.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-6111 and advised the documented workaround for 7.2 systems with large transceiver history. The customer backed up the configuration, cleared nonessential DOM history with `no transceiver calibration-history`, saved the config, and retried the upgrade in a maintenance window after reseating the most recently installed optics. The upgrade completed on the next attempt without rollback.

subject: Frequent stp notifications on 10g access port after host restart
description: HarborPoint Retail called in on a Helix HX-5000 running 7.5 after a warehouse virtualization host rebooted. The site saw repeated spanning-tree events every few seconds and initially suspected a cabling issue, but the port stayed link-up and did not increment physical error counters. TAC captured the switch logs and saw "%STP-5-TCN-STORM" repeating while `show mac address-table flapping` indicated the same downstream MACs moving on the access interface. `show spanning-tree detail` also showed the port repeatedly reentering forwarding even though the attachment was unchanged.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-6105, which describes rapid-pvst generating continuous topology-change notifications on multi-MAC edge ports. We applied the documented workaround: move the host to a dedicated edge VLAN design and avoid running rapid-pvst on that port, with portfast retained only where the port connects to a single access device. After the configuration change, the TCN storm stopped and MAC aging returned to the normal 300-second interval.

subject: Edge went offline after certificate renewal on orchestrator 2.8
description: HarborPoint Retail reports that one Atlas SD-WAN edge stopped checking in shortly after a certificate renewal window. The affected device is edge site HPR-SEA-14 running Atlas SD-WAN 2.8, and the orchestrator now shows it disconnected about 5 minutes after the change. The customer also noted that policy updates to that site are failing, while other sites remain up. TAC review confirmed the renewal completed on the edge, but the orchestrator is rejecting the next registration attempt because it cannot validate the presented chain.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-5102. We reimported the full certificate chain on the orchestrator with the active intermediate CA, then committed the change and re-ran registration. The edge returned to connected state and policy push succeeded after the trust bundle was refreshed.

subject: nf-300 fails image verification during scheduled upgrade
description: HarborPoint Retail opened this through the customer portal after a scheduled upgrade from Nimbus NF-300 release 5.0.8 to 5.0.9 repeatedly rolled back. The appliance downloads the image over HTTPS, but after the reboot the console stops at image verification and returns "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". TAC reviewed the upload history and confirmed the published SHA-256 hash for the 5.0.9 image matches the file on the management host, so the image itself is intact. The failure only occurs on this 5.0.8 unit during the boot-stage verification step.
resolution: TAC identified this as KB-3104 and advised upgrading the appliance to 5.0.9, where the boot loader hashes only the unpadded payload. After the customer staged the same image and retried the upgrade, the device booted successfully into 5.0.9 and the rollback no longer occurred.

subject: Northstar Bank AR-900 IPv6 sessions failing after maintenance RA filter
description: Northstar Bank opened a NOC escalation for an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.3 after a maintenance change on the upstream edge caused IPv6 workstations in one office VLAN to lose connectivity. The bank reported that hosts kept their addresses for a short period, then new TCP sessions failed and Neighbor Discovery stopped resolving peers even though the router still displayed the delegated prefix. TAC found '%IPV6-4-RA-LIFETIME' in the logs during the interval when clients lost IPv6 reachability, which lined up with the reported 180-second delay after the last valid router advertisement was filtered. The configured valid lifetime on the prefix was 7200 seconds, so the observed expiry behavior was inconsistent with the intended network design.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as KB-2104 and confirmed that the active VLAN was using SLAAC with router advertisement suppression, which causes prefix state to age out on the 3-minute hold timer. We applied the documented workaround by removing RA suppression from the user VLAN and recommending DHCPv6 stateful addressing if suppression is required for the site design. The bank validated that client IPv6 addresses remained stable after the change and closed the incident.

subject: Unexpected throughput dips on AR-900 during voice bursts
description: Pinnacle Energy contacted TAC about an Aurora AR-900 on 9.2.1 that was showing brief throughput dips on a shared WAN port. The customer described it as a random slowdown affecting nonvoice applications for about a second at a time, while the voice service itself remained stable. TAC found no physical layer alarms, no interface resets, and no control-plane anomalies. The routing table and neighbor state were stable, but `show qos interface` showed the strict-priority queue draining continuously and the weighted queues not receiving expected service during the burst window. The customer had originally tried changing MTU values, which did not affect the issue.
resolution: TAC linked the case to KB-2105 and recommended upgrading the Aurora AR-900 from 9.2.1 to 9.2.3. The customer completed the upgrade and repeated the traffic test under the same load. The scheduler behavior normalized after the upgrade, and the short throughput dips did not recur.

subject: Best-effort drops during voice bursts on AR-900 uplink
description: Customer emailed TAC reporting that intermittent ordering and POS traffic on a single Aurora AR-900 uplink was stalling for 1 to 2 seconds whenever the voice VLAN became active. The device is an Aurora AR-900 running 9.2.1, and the site has a 10 Gbps egress with a strict-priority voice class. Initial checks showed no physical errors, no interface flaps, and no BGP or OSPF instability. `show qos interface` showed the priority queue draining continuously while the weighted queues stayed near near empty during the affected interval. The customer initially suspected an optics problem because the issue only appeared in short bursts.
resolution: TAC matched the behavior to KB-2105 and applied the documented workaround. The voice class was capped to 30 percent bandwidth on the egress policy, which prevented the strict-priority queue from monopolizing the transmit window during microbursts. After the change, best-effort traffic remained stable and the latency spikes stopped.

subject: critical core loss on hx-5000 7.2 requires immediate remediation
description: CivicWorks Public Agency contacted TAC through NOC escalation for an active outage on a Helix HX-5000 running 7.2. The core switch was not down, but several application teams reported severe latency and intermittent drops on one oversubscribed 100G port feeding the data center edge. TAC confirmed the port was forwarding at line rate with bursty traffic, and `show queue counters` showed sustained tail drops climbing by several thousand packets per minute. The customer’s team had already ruled out link flaps and spanning tree events, so the symptoms pointed to an egress scheduling problem on the switch itself.
resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-6109 and guided CivicWorks Public Agency through an upgrade to 7.4. The updated release includes the scheduler reservation window expansion and earlier buffer watermark checks needed to correct the burst-loss behavior on oversubscribed 100G ports. After the upgrade, queue drops stopped climbing and latency returned to normal levels.

subject: LTE tunnel fragmentation after 3.2 upgrade on custom APN
description: CivicWorks Public Agency escalated through its partner after a branch upgrade to Atlas SD-WAN 3.2. The affected edge is a branch unit running 3.2 with an LTE transport bound to a nondefault APN; the tunnel comes up, but traffic above roughly 1418 bytes fragments or fails intermittently. TAC reviewed the post-upgrade configuration and confirmed the interface object was present, but the configured LTE tunnel MTU was missing after migration. The edge log also showed "%UPG-5-MTU-MIGRATE" during the upgrade window.
resolution: TAC identified the issue as the 3.2 migration defect described in KB-5110. We re-applied the LTE tunnel MTU on each affected LTE interface with the custom APN using `interface lte0 tunnel-mtu 1400` followed by `commit`, then validated the path with 1400-byte and 1472-byte probes before returning the circuit to service.

subject: HX-5000 uplinks dropping short bursts of traffic on 8.0
description: Evergreen Clinic Network reported brief packet loss on a Helix HX-5000 core switch during normal daytime traffic, mostly affecting VoIP and EMR sync flows. The switch is running 8.0, and the customer noted that interface utilization stays below 80 percent even when the drops occur. TAC reviewed the queue counters and saw short discard bursts on the uplink queue, with the customer also capturing the log message "%BUF-3-OVERFLOW" at the time of each event. The pattern is consistent with multicast replication bursts exhausting shared buffer headroom rather than a sustained congestion condition.
resolution: TAC applied the workaround from KB-6110 by reducing multicast reservation on the busiest leaf and moving the replication-heavy VLANs to a separate uplink group. We also advised scheduling large multicast bursts outside congestion-sensitive windows and monitoring show queue counters for further discard increments. The case was closed after the customer confirmed the short unicast losses stopped.

subject: NF-300 5.1.5 upgrade completed but config partially reset
description: BlueRiver Credit Union escalated that an NF-300 on 5.0.8 was upgraded to 5.1.5 and booted normally, but a subset of firewall and VPN policy entries disappeared after the first administrator login. The customer reported intermittent access issues and thought the new release had corrupted the database. On triage, the appliance was up, sessions were established, and the missing entries were isolated to configuration objects only; `show running-config` showed default values where custom objects had been present. The event log also included "%UPGRADE-4-REPLAY_CURSOR", which pointed to a migration replay problem.
resolution: TAC confirmed the condition matches KB-3111 and instructed the customer to upgrade the NF-300 to 5.2.0, where the replay cursor defect is fixed. The customer then restored the affected policy set from the pre-upgrade backup and verified that the configuration remained stable after reboot. No further object loss was observed after the 5.2.0 upgrade.

subject: support call: nf-300 rejects valid upgrade image
description: IronGate Freight called TAC about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 that kept reverting after an attempted upgrade to 5.0.9. The customer initially suspected a storage problem, but the appliance consistently downloads the image and then fails during the next boot with "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". TAC asked for the image inventory and confirmed the SHA-256 hash matches the vendor-published value, which ruled out a damaged file. The issue appears only on the HTTPS stage download path and only on the 5.0.8 boot loader.
resolution: TAC matched the failure to KB-3104 and applied the documented workaround from the article: stage the image with SCP so it is written without HTTPS padding. The customer copied the image via SCP, verified it with the image status command, and the reboot completed without triggering the verification failure.

subject: Overlay path instability on 2.9 edge under backup load
description: IronGate Freight reported that one distribution-site edge on Atlas SD-WAN 2.9 was causing shipping applications and voice softphones to fail over repeatedly. The NOC described it as a circuit problem, but carrier testing showed the physical transport remained up and only the overlay state was changing. TAC reviewed the edge output from `show sdwan tunnels` and saw rising loss counters and degraded path selection during large file transfers. The edge log showed "%SDWAN-4-SLA-DOWN" at the same times the backups peaked, and the device was running 2.9.1.
resolution: TAC matched the symptoms to KB-5105 and applied the documented workaround on the edge. We configured the SLA class to use a high-priority probe queue with `app-route sla-class voice probe-queue priority` and committed the policy. The tunnel no longer flapped during backup traffic, and the customer agreed to keep the current release until a planned upgrade window.
